papers.summary: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer one model for many chemistries, but their deep, globally coupled architectures do not fit the spatial decomposition that scales classical and short-ranged MLIPs. We present pair_style uma, a LAMMPS pair style that evaluates the Universal Model for Atoms (UMA) through LibTorch on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs from a single source tree. It reimplements FairChem's edge-sharded graph parallelism in C++ over exported TorchScript modules, with one MPI rank per device, NCCL or oneCCL collectives, and the whole energy and force path in double precision. The strain-gradient virial is carried through the exported modules and the cross-device reductions, so that fix npt runs on both vendors' hardware. We measure NPT capacity and cost on one 4xA100-40GB node, one 8xH200 node, and one 12-tile Intel node, and on up to 32 Intel nodes. Without activation checkpointing, one node holds NaCl cells of about 8,000 atoms (A100, 0.21 ns/day), 22,000 atoms (Intel, 0.10 ns/day), and 47,000 atoms (H200, 0.16 ns/day). Graph parallelism raises the capacity of a single device by 8.0x on H200 and 4.6x on A100. Across nodes, capacity grows to about 779,000 atoms on 32 Intel nodes, with a slower speed at 0.007 ns/day. On H200 and A100, a FLOP count of FairChem's graph-parallel predictor gives lower bounds of 31% and 51% of FP64 peak. From one omat checkpoint and with no refit, nine 100 ps NPT heating ramps (NaCl, equiatomic Pt-Ru, and equiatomic (HfNbTaTiZr)N, on all three node types) ran to completion.

authors.name: Xiaoli Yan, Eliu Huerta

papers.title: On the Electrodynamics of a Non-Contact Inductive Sensor for High-Accuracy Tip Deflection Measurements of Piezoceramic Bending Actuators and its Application for Energy Harvesting Purposes
papers.summary: Piezoelectric bending actuators provide deflections of several hundred micrometers and are used in electrical and mechanical engineering, acoustics, automation, automotive technology and healthcare. Highly efficient, low-cost piezoceramics offer a wide range of technical solutions. Their highpiezoelectric coefficients enable large strains at low electric field strengths. However, hysteresis, drift and creep impair positioning accuracy. Precise switching and positioning require compensation for these material-related effects, as well as varying mechanical loads and vibrations. A non-contact inductive proximity sensor is therefore combined with high-precision electronic circuit. Within a closed-loop control system, this sensor-actuator arrangement detects disturbances and enables their compensation, allowing highly efficient piezoceramics to be used for high-accuracy positioning. This paper investigates the electrodynamics of a specially developed eddy-current-based proximity sensor suitable for integration into confined spaces. A theoretical description explains its physical operating principle and enables analytical determination of the relative change in inductance as a function of actuator tip deflection. Experimental measurements validate the electrodynamic approach. The paper also considers energy harvesting applications. Measuring tip deflection allows the power dissipated in the piezoelectric transducer to be determined. The sensor system thus provides a basis for investigating and evaluating the performance of piezoelectric energy harvesters.

authors.name: Ruediger G. Ballas

papers.title: Ray propagation of circularly polarized light in an inhomogeneous medium: the optical Magnus effect from Maxwell's equations
papers.summary: We derive the ray propagation of circularly polarized light in an inhomogeneous, isotropic and lossless medium, including the first correction to geometrical optics, the optical Magnus (spin Hall) effect. Starting from Maxwell's equations and the eikonal expansion to first order in $1/k_0$, we show that the polarization is parallel transported along the ray, identify the Berry connection and curvature of the helicity states, and obtain a ray action in which the Berry phase appears as a correction to the optical path length. This action leads to a Hamiltonian in which the refractive index is evaluated at a position shifted by the Berry connection, $\mathcal H_\sigma(\mathbf r,\mathbf p)=|\mathbf p|-n(\mathbf r+\mathbf A_\sigma(\mathbf p)/k_0) \simeq|\mathbf p|-n(\mathbf r)-k_0^{-1}\boldsymbol\nabla n\cdot\mathbf A_\sigma(\mathbf p)$. In terms of the physical position, the equations of motion contain the Berry curvature as an anomalous velocity. We give the equivalent non-canonical bracket form, the gauge transformation, and the equivalent time-parametrized formulation with the Hamiltonian $\hbar\omega=\hbar c|\mathbf k|/n$, and we state the approximations involved. The resulting ray equations are compared with analytic and numerical results. A planar interface, the helical ray in a cylindrical medium and the exact conservation of angular momentum provide checks. The formulation is set up for numerical propagation of rays in a medium with a spatially varying refractive index.

authors.name: Igor Kuzmenko, Y. B. Band

papers.title: Tropical Cyclone-Following Dataset for Limited-Area Machine Learning Applications
papers.summary: This work presents a lightweight dataset of tropical cyclone (TC)-following meteorological variables to facilitate the development and application of machine learning (ML) methods in TC research. Using outputs from our previous climate downscaling and idealized simulations, the dataset is constructed as multichannel video sequences that track TC centers throughout their lifetimes. To demonstrate the dataset utility, we present an application in which a regional ML model is trained to predict TC intensity with explicit incorporation of lateral boundary conditions. Our results highlight the importance of lateral boundary information for predicting TC intensity with ML models inside a limited-area domain, underscoring the need to properly account for lateral boundaries when developing regional ML models for TC intensity forecast.

authors.name: Minh-Khanh Luong, Chanh Kieu

papers.title: Labtune: Treating Lab Organization and Information Sharing as Experimental Variables in LLM-Agent Discovery
papers.summary: De-siloing can create groupthink; silos can prevent knowledge sharing and reduce research efficiency. The same tension appears in research systems built with large language model (LLM) agents, yet their organization is usually fixed by design. I propose treating laboratory structure and information sharing as experimental variables. I introduce Labtune, an open framework for bounded research workflows with user-selected laboratory organization, communication policy, model configuration and budget. Users can choose among six editable designs, from multidisciplinary silos and transdisciplinary teams to co-leaders, hub-and-spoke structures, flat co-labs and a single scientist. Information sharing can independently vary from none to high detail, with an optional channel for conditional abstractions called wisdom. Sharing is enforced by the controller at phase barriers rather than through unrestricted agent chat, while delegation does not create additional budget or permissions. Development evidence is separated from protected confirmation, and an optional multi-lab layer allows laboratories with different structures to exchange filtered information. Labtune is an idea and system-description paper, not a benchmark result. Its contribution is to make laboratory organization and information sharing configurable and measurable under matched budgets. I do not claim that one design or level of sharing is best; the aim is to create a concrete experimental space in which those differences can be tested.

authors.name: Goran Mitevski

papers.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moir\'e Flatband Superlattices
papers.summary: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moir\'e superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moir\'e modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moir\'e superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moir\'e superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.

authors.name: Amin Zamani, Lihang Feng, Jianji Liu, Ze Zheng, Gabriel Sanderson, Mohsen Rahmani, Peilong Hong, Lei Xu

papers.title: Hydrogen Electron Cyclotron Resonance Dissociator Demonstrator for the Project 8 Experiment
papers.summary: Project 8, a neutrino mass experiment, employs the novel frequency technique of cyclotron radiation emission spectroscopy (CRES) to perform a model independent measurement of neutrino mass via tritium beta decay. Our pioneering experiment will consist of a beamline that dissociates molecular tritium, surface cools atoms through accommodation, evaporatively cools and slows atoms, and traps them in a CRES resonant cavity to advance towards our sensitivity goal of 40 meV/c^2 for our final electron-weighted neutrino mass measurement. We are prototyping an electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) dissociator that uses a tunable 1 kW 2.45 GHz RF generator and electromagnets to ignite a hydrogen plasma in an aluminum resonant cavity. Our ECR source is designed to produce a high atom flux (~10^19 atoms/second) near room temperature. We present the engineering development, gas diagnostics, and spectroscopy data from our hydrogen plasma.

authors.name: Manjinder Oueslati, Walter Pettus, Anna Reine, Hamish Robertson

papers.title: Direct Analysis in Real Time Mass Spectrometry (DART-MS) Study of Amino Acids in the Vacuum Stable Liquids EMI-BF$_4$, EMI-Acetate, DEMA-OTf, DEMA-MsO, and Glycerol
papers.summary: The detection of organics and potential biomolecules is an important goal of planetary science and astrobiology spacecraft missions, and many types of analytical chemistry for studying organics depend upon liquid solvents as working fluids. However, most liquids are difficult to maintain in the vacuum of space, complicating their use and increasing spacecraft mass and cost. Here we present a study using Direct Analysis in Real Time mass spectrometry (DART-MS) as a rapid screen for the detectability of histidine, glycine, arginine, lysine, and aspartic acid at mole fractions of about $5\times10^{-4}$ to $10^{-3}$ in five vacuum-stable liquids: EMI-BF$_4$, EMI-acetate, DEMA-MsO, DEMA-OTf, and glycerol. In all of the ionic liquids, the solvent cation dominated the spectra and no amino acid was detected, apart from a weak histidine signal in EMI-BF$_4$ at 350$^\circ$ C (median 5\% of the normalized peak intensity). The protic DEMA ionic liquids did not enhance detection, and their ionic components instead dominated the mass spectra. Aspartic acid was not detected in any liquid. In glycerol solutions, histidine, glycine, arginine, and lysine were all detected, and histidine was frequently a dominant line. We thus find glycerol to be the most promising of the liquids tested for organic detection with an ideal operating DART helium temperature of 350--400 $^\circ$C. We also found no clear evidence of water uptake or aqueous alteration in the ionic liquids, which was a secondary goal relevant to ionic liquid spacecraft electric propulsion.

authors.name: Zach Ulibarri, Samantha E. Adamski, Amy E. Hofmann, Elaine M. Petro

papers.title: Reconfigurable multi-tone mmWave/THz generation powered by high-efficiency Kerr parametric oscillation
papers.summary: Broadband and simultaneously accessible multi-tone millimeter-wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) signals are attractive for multi-band wireless communication and spectroscopy applications, yet their generation remains constrained by electronic bandwidth limitations and inefficient optical frequency conversion. Here, we demonstrate reconfigurable photonic generation of multi-tone mmWave/THz signals with comb spacings of 100, 200, 300, and 400 GHz, using a strongly asymmetric dual-ring silicon-nitride (SiN) microresonator and a broadband spiral plasmonic photomixer. A localized avoided-mode crossing (AMX) introduced by an auxiliary ring supports a fixed optical parametric oscillation (OPO) mode pair over an extended pump-detuning range, consistent with passive compensation of detuning-dependent phase mismatch. This enables a maximum pump-to-generated-line conversion efficiency of 67.3 % with 25.06 dB of pump depletion across different pump wavelength selections. Direct photomixing of these optical states produces simultaneous multi-frequency tones spanning 100 to 900 GHz without intermediate optical amplification. The generated carriers are further characterized through down-converted spectra, frequency-noise power spectral density (PSD), and Allan deviation measurements, yielding a \b{eta}-separation linewidth of 26 kHz at an observation time of 0.1 s. Optical modulation offers high radiated power levels exceeding 2 mW at 100 GHz at a duty cycle of 1 %, while mitigating thermal breakdown in the photomixer. High optical conversion efficiency, reconfigurable and selectable comb spacings, and broadband multi-tone generation on a chip-scale platform provide a compact route toward reconfigurable multi-band mmWave/THz sources for wireless communication, spectroscopy, and sensing.

authors.name: Dong IL Lee, Fanqi Shen, Wenzheng Liu, Xinghe Jiang, Anika Tabassum, Alwaleed Aldhafeeri, Manas Choure, Jasmine Lu, Mona Jarrahi, Chee Wei Wong

papers.title: Collective animal motion: The case of midge swarms
papers.summary: Among collective states of animal groups, midge swarms pose several puzzling questions. Their polarization order parameter is very small, and the insects interact only weakly with one another while remaining strongly bound to the swarm. In laboratory studies performed without external perturbations, the correlation length is small. By contrast, field studies reveal strong correlations, scale-free behavior, and power-law scaling of the correlation length, susceptibility, and correlation time. The dynamic correlation function exhibits data collapse only for short times when time is rescaled by the correlation time. Is there a theory that explains these disparate observations? We review several models proposed in the literature and extend our harmonically confined Vicsek model to anisotropic confinement. Within the extended criticality region of the phase diagram, numerical simulations predict elongated swarms and static critical exponents that lie between those of the two-dimensional and isotropic three-dimensional models. These values agree better with those measured in natural swarms. We also calculate probability density functions for both natural and laboratory swarms. Numerical simulations indicate that the laboratory distributions correspond to a different region of parameter space, although some open questions remain.

authors.name: L. L. Bonilla, R. Gonz\'alez-Albaladejo

papers.title: Microstrip-Line Characterization of Artificial Dielectric Materials for MRI Applications
papers.summary: Artificial dielectric materials (ADMs) offer a flexible means of shaping radiofrequency fields in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, ADM designs based on plane-wave characterization may not directly predict their effects on RF fields in MRI. We propose a travelling-wave microstrip-line (MSL) approach to approximate the spatially nonuniform excitation experienced by dielectric pads near MRI RF coils and to guide ADM characterization and tuning against a reference dielectric. Both materials are tested under identical MSL measurement conditions, and the ADM geometry is adjusted until its reflection minimum occurs at the same frequency as that of the reference. Simulations and bench measurements show that the tuned ADM more closely matches the reference dielectric's reflection-minimum frequency than a plane-wave-based design. MRI simulations show that the tuned ADM produces a transmit magnetic-field distribution similar to that of the reference pad. Phantom images acquired at 7 T also show similar image-intensity patterns. These results demonstrate the utility of MSL response matching for guiding ADM design in the tested configuration. The proposed approach provides a practical bench-top step for assessing and tuning manufactured ADMs before MRI evaluation.

authors.name: Haiwei Chen, Huan Wang, Xiaotong Zhang, Yang Gao

papers.title: Life Cycle Sustainability Assessment of Fossil- and Bio-Based Membrane Manufacturing
papers.summary: The transition towards sustainable membrane manufacturing is challenged by its reliance on fossil-based polymers, organic solvents, and generation of large volumes of contaminated water. We combined process simulation, life cycle assessment, and Monte Carlo simulation to identify hotspots in the manufacturing of ultrafiltration hollow-fiber membranes for pharmaceutical applications and evaluate strategies to mitigate impact and reduce waste generation. Process models informed by industry input compared fossil- and bio-based membranes on a cradle-to-gate basis per square meter of membrane produced. Key environmental hotspots include polymer and bore solution preparation, driven by the contribution of polymer and solvent, accounting for 30-80% of total impacts across the categories investigated, and wastewater dilution, driven by the environmental burden of solvent-contaminated wastewater management. Under the modeled conditions, although polymer substitution can reduce environmental burdens, cellulose-based membranes show higher impacts than polysulfone membranes in at least 85% of simulations within each impact category, due to chemical-intensive cellulose modification and regeneration. In contrast, solvent recycling can mitigate solvent- and wastewater-related burdens when combined with reduced water demand, yielding climate change benefits at water demands below approximately 36 L per m2 under the modeled recovery configuration and highlighting its potential to reduce the environmental footprint of membrane manufacturing.

authors.name: Elizabeth Aigaje-Espinosa, Christina Carbrello, Rui Shi

papers.title: Extracting and Characterizing Near-Fault Effects from Strong Motion Observations of the 2022 Chishang Earthquake Sequence
papers.summary: Accurately characterizing near-fault ground motions, particularly permanent tectonic displacements and velocity pulses associated with rupture directivity, is essential for seismic hazard assessment and infrastructure design. However, conventional ground-motion processing can distort or remove these characteristics. This study extends existing baseline correction methods by synchronously processing all three components of strong-motion recordings to preserve near-fault effects. The proposed methodology is applied to 59 recordings from the 2022 M 6.5 Guanshan foreshock and M 6.9 Chishang mainshock in Taiwan. Comparison with nearby Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) observations demonstrates that the method reliably captures the amplitude and orientation of permanent tectonic displacements. Analysis of the processed recordings reveals pronounced velocity pulses and permanent displacements, with the largest peak-to-peak velocities concentrated along the direction of rupture propagation. A classification framework is also introduced to distinguish fling-step pulses from dynamic velocity pulses. The results indicate that fling-step pulses typically occur early in the ground shaking, whereas dynamic pulses span a broader temporal range. Furthermore, the spatial distribution and orientation of near-fault effects are consistent with bridge damage documented during post-earthquake reconnaissance. The resulting dataset provides ground-motion time histories that preserve near-fault characteristics for seismic hazard assessment and engineering applications.

authors.name: Grigorios Lavrentiadis, Domniki Asimaki, Trevor J. Carey, Henry Benjamin Mason

papers.title: Bicarbonate/carbonic acid equilibria in aqueous solutions: Conformational Dynamics, Ion-Pair Speciation, and Free Energy Landscapes from Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics and Metadynamics
papers.summary: Carbonic acid (H2CO3) is connected with the dissolved CO2 and bicarbonate (HCO3-) equilibria in aqueous solutions. Its two elementary reactions in water, acid dissociation and dehydration to CO2, are difficult to resolve because both are coupled to proton transfer through hydrogen-bonded networks. In this work, we combine 0.5 ns of unbiased PBE-D3 molecular dynamics of 1 molar solution of H2CO3 with metadynamics on the O - H coordination (H2CO3 = HCO3- + H+) and the C - O distance of the leaving hydroxyl (H2CO3 CO2 + H2O). These unbiased trajectories show frequent cis-cis cis-trans interconversion through long-lived bicarbonate (well separated from solvated proton, H3O+, and also mediated by a short-lived three-water [H2O...H3O+...H2O] ring that acts as a solvent-shared ion pair (SSIP); only 16-23% of deprotonation events reach a solvent-separated ion pair (SShIP). Resolving ion-pairs as SSIP for proper reaction leads to an improved estimate of pKa1 from 1.1 to 2.4, toward the experimental 3.45-3.59 (measured at supposedly infinite dilution). Further, metadynamics simulations provide a dehydration barrier of 17.8 (1D) and 15.3 kcal/mol (2D), suggesting that the final product CO2 + H2O is 2.8 kcal/mol below H2CO3. Our two-dimensional free energy surface also shows that C--O cleavage proceeds through the CO2 + OH- which further goes down by 9.9 kcal/mol to product CO2 + H2O.

authors.name: Prabhat Prakash, Karnamohit Ranka, Frances A. Houle, William A. Goddard III

papers.title: Fractional Orbital Bombardment Systems
papers.summary: We analyze Fractional Orbital Bombardment Systems (FOBS) as a means of delivering nuclear weapons by placing warheads into partial orbits around the Earth, and show that they do not represent a game-changing advance in technology or capability. We consider potential uses of such a weapon, including evading missile defenses and delivering attacks with short warning time. FOBS could underfly current exoatmospheric defenses, but the required payload reduction may not justify its use if other countermeasures are deemed effective. If a FOBS attack could be successfully disguised as a satellite launch, the warning time could be short enough to raise fears of a decapitating strike. The development of such a capability could lead countries to shorten decision-making timelines in a crisis, which would be destabilizing. The US can take steps to ensure that very-short-warning attacks would not succeed, thereby enhancing deterrence during a crisis.

authors.name: David Wright, Steve Fetter

papers.title: Active Learning with Generative AI in Introductory Physics: A Multi-Institutional Study of the P-A.I.R. Framework
papers.summary: Generative AI tools have become part of how students study physics, yet unstructured use may reduce students' opportunities to work through problems independently. The Physics AI-Replication (P-A.I.R.) framework structures AI use as a four-step cycle: students identify a challenging problem, obtain an AI-generated explanation and solution, request similar practice problems, and solve them independently before reviewing the AI's solutions. We evaluated P-A.I.R. in 11 algebra- and calculus-based introductory physics sections at four U.S. institutions using a common end-of-semester survey. Most students reported improved conceptual understanding (90.9\%) and found the replicated practice problems helpful (97.7\%), and these two ratings were strongly associated ($r_s = 0.58$). Perceptions of both components, as well as post-engagement confidence ($\mu = 7.18$ on a 1-10 scale), were consistent across institutions. Post-engagement confidence was associated with perceived improvement in conceptual understanding ($r_s = 0.37$) and the helpfulness of replicated practice ($r_s = 0.35$), but not with how often students used AI ($r_s = 0.02$) or with self-reported GPA ($r_s = 0.13$). Thematic analysis of open-ended responses showed that students valued AI primarily for conceptual clarification and structured problem solving (63.0\%), while their main concerns were AI accuracy (34.2\%) and the need for explanations that guide rather than simply provide answers (29.7\%). These findings suggest that how students engage with AI matters more than how often they use it, and that frameworks sequencing AI assistance with independent problem solving offer a practical, transferable approach for physics instruction.

authors.name: Bilas Paul, Shantanu Chakraborty, Shruti Shrestha, Binod Nainabasti, Bisaj Paul

papers.title: Dielectric Models of Normal and Diseased Human Trabecular Bones at Microwave Frequencies
papers.summary: The dielectric properties of biological tissues are used to investigate the interaction of electromagnetic (EM) fields with the human body. These properties are integrated into EM numerical simulations, such as the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, using dielectric models such as Cole-Cole and Debye models. These computational tools are employed to study the propagation of EM waves within the human body. This paper has developed the one-pole and two-pole Cole-Cole and Debye models for the dielectric properties of normal and diseased human trabecular bone tissue at microwave frequencies (0.5-8.5 GHz). The dielectric properties of normal trabecular and cortical bone were derived based on the literature, while those of diseased human trabecular bones (osteoporotic and osteoarthritis) were acquired from a previous study conducted by the authors, which characterised the properties within the 0.5-8.5 GHz frequency range. This study has employed a weighted least squares method to optimise the one-pole and two-pole dielectric models' parameters. The accuracy of the developed dielectric models is validated by comparing the simulated results with the experimental data already published by the authors. The comparative analysis of the models demonstrated that the one-pole Cole-Cole model achieved a better fit compared to the one-pole Debye model across all bone types. Additionally, the two-pole Cole-Cole model exhibited a better fit than the two-pole Debye model. The proposed models can be used in numerical simulations to investigate the interaction of EM fields with bone tissue and develop and optimise microwave bone health monitoring and treatment techniques.

authors.name: Bilal Amin, Amra Mehboob, Eoghan Dunne, Ana Gonz\'alez-Su\'arez, Finn Krewer, Aoife Lowery, Martin O'Halloran, Adnan Elahi

papers.title: Dynamics of Vortex Electrons in a Uniform Magnetic Field Across Nonrelativistic and Relativistic Regimes
papers.summary: The dynamics of a vortex electron in a transverse uniform magnetic field involves not only the cyclotron motion of the wave packet center but also the evolution of its internal wavefunction structure. To study this process, we develop a quantum framework and investigate the dynamics of vortex electrons in both the nonrelativistic and relativistic regimes. A discrete Bessel-Gaussian initial wave packet is expanded in the basis of Dirac eigenstates to obtain the time-dependent wavefunction and to analyze its spatiotemporal evolution. In the nonrelativistic regime, the results deviate significantly from the rigid point-dipole model, as the intrinsic kinetic orbital angular momentum exhibits dynamics more complex than simple Larmor precession, owing to the nonstationary internal current distribution of the wave packet. In the relativistic regime, the nonlinear dependence of the energy levels on the quantum numbers destroys the equal spacing of the spectrum. Consequently, the relative phases among the eigenstate components of the wave packet evolve nonuniformly, resulting in wave-packet spreading and deformation, accompanied by modified intrinsic orbital angular momentum dynamics. We introduce a dimensionless parameter to quantify this relativistic dephasing, providing an approximate criterion for selecting physical parameters and evolution times to mitigate the resulting wave-packet distortion. These results clarify the limitations of the rigid point-dipole model, highlight the essential role of internal wavefunction structure, and provide theoretical guidance for understanding and manipulating relativistic vortex electrons.

authors.name: Yujian Lin, Zhigang Bu, Shiyu Liu, Taoming Guo, Liangliang Ji

papers.title: Dielectric characterisation of human adrenal glands and adrenal tumours for the development of microwave ablation technologies for hypertension treatment
papers.summary: Adrenal gland-induced hypertension results from underlying adrenal gland disorders including Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, and Pheochromocytoma. Due to the limitations of existing pharmaceutical and surgical treatment methods, minimally invasive treatment options like microwave ablation (MWA) have received significant attention for treating adrenal gland disorders. A precise comprehension of the dielectric properties of human adrenal glands will help to tailor energy delivery for MWA therapy, thus offering the potential to optimise treatments and minimise damage to surrounding tissues. This study reports the ex vivo dielectric properties of human adrenal glands, including the cortex, medulla, capsule, and tumours, based on the data obtained from four patients (diagnosed with Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, and Pheochromocytoma) who underwent unilateral adrenalectomy at the University Hospital Galway, Ireland. An open-ended coaxial probe measurement technique was used to measure the dielectric properties for a frequency range of 0.5-8.5 GHz. The dielectric properties were fitted using a two-pole Debye model, and a weighted least squares method was employed to optimise the model parameters. Moreover, the dielectric properties of adrenal tissues and tumours were compared across frequencies commonly used in MWA, including 915 MHz, 2.45 GHz, and 5.8 GHz. The study found that the dielectric properties of adrenal tumours were influenced by the presence of lipid-rich adenomas, and the dielectric properties of Cushing's syndrome tumour were lowest in comparison to the tumours in patients diagnosed with Conn's syndrome and Pheochromocytoma. Furthermore, a notable difference was observed in the dielectric properties of the medulla and cortex among patients diagnosed with Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, and Pheochromocytoma.

authors.name: Bilal Amin, Adnan Elahi, Grazia Cappiello, Niko I\v{s}tuk, Eoghan Dunne, Finn Krewer, Anne Marie Quinn, Aoife Lowery, Punit Prakash, Michael Conall Dennedy, Martin O'Halloran

papers.title: A Two-Dimensional Physics-Informed Neural Network Model of a Hall Effect Thruster Plasma: Self-Consistent Electrostatics and Physical-Consistency Diagnostics
papers.summary: We present a two-dimensional axisymmetric physics-informed neural network (PINN) of the discharge channel of the P5 Hall thruster at 300 V and 5.4 A, which solves eleven coupled plasma fields and assimilates 145 internal probe measurements per field reconstructed from the data of Haas and Gallimore. The electric potential is obtained from Poisson's equation in charge-separation form, n_e = n_i(1+eta), with eta bounded by construction, which keeps the stiff electrostatic constraint active and trainable. The reference solution agrees with the training profiles to relative L2 errors of 0.017, 0.073 and 0.205 for the potential, electron temperature and ion density, and held-out tests show the potential to be far more robust than the ion density to the withdrawal of measurement lines. We then test the solution against requirements the data fit does not reveal: global particle and current balances, the electron current implied by the momentum equation, the field-aligned electron force balance and the axial ion momentum budget. These expose a neutral inflow six times the measured flow, a bound in the potential representation, and a momentum-implied electron current, more than 99% field-aligned, exceeding the discharge current by orders of magnitude. Correcting these, with a divergence-free magnetic field fitted to measured data, uncertainty-weighted data, the electron pressure gradient and progressively imposed field-aligned and current constraints, yields a solution that conserves particles to within 3%, holds the current between 5.1 and 5.4 A and places 97% of the potential and 88% of the temperature measurements within their uncertainties. Within the tested single-velocity fluid formulation, however, the ion density, potential and ion velocity could not be matched together, and the field-aligned electron balance remains the main obstacle to electron self-consistency.

authors.name: Josh Adjedj, Subrata Roy

papers.title: Accurate representation of the continuum orbital in a Gaussian basis set: application to Auger decay rates
papers.summary: Many processes in chemistry and physics, such as autoionization, photoionization, or electron-impact collisions, involve unbound electrons. Despite their importance, theoretical methods for modeling continuum electrons remain significantly less developed than those for purely bound electronic states. Here we present a novel approach for treating continuum electrons within Gaussian-based quantum chemistry. The method represents continuum orbital in a discrete basis of standard Gaussian-type orbitals (GTOs), where the continuum wave function is obtained by solving the Lippmann-Schwinger equation with proper boundary conditions using an analytical representation of the Green's function in an auxiliary GTO basis set. The resulting continuum orbital is multicentered and multichannel, providing a rigorous description of scattering states. As an initial application of the new methodology, we compute Auger decay rates for several atomic and molecular systems, including Ne, H$_2$O, CO$_2$, and Ar. We demonstrate a consistent improvement of the results with increasing the quality of the continuum representation. We show also that higher-order electron-correlation effects in the bound domain are essential for an accurate treatment of satellite transitions. The present formalism therefore provides a systematically improvable Gaussian-based framework for continuum-electron problems that is fully compatible with standard quantum chemistry methods.

authors.name: Dibyendu Mahato, Saikat Roy, Wojciech Skomorowski

papers.title: Shallow lunar fractures dominate the long-lasting seismic coda
papers.summary: Lunar seismic records are characterized by long-lasting spindle-shaped coda, which has long been considered to be caused by strong velocity contrasts in a continuous-medium lunar crust; however, simulated waveforms could not well match the observation even with unrealistically strong velocity contrasts, demonstrating its mechanism still unsolved. Here we propose a novel model of coda wave generation with random fractures in the lunar crust, where vacuum fractures prevent seismic wave propagation as insulating boundaries, causing strong persistent reverberation in terms of total reflection among fractures. Our model can easily reproduce the typical characteristics of observed Apollo data even using a limited number of simplified fractures in homogeneous matrix, with envelope correlations over 0.9, much higher than previous studies. Numerical simulations suggest that fractures in the uppermost ~1 km of the crust may dominate lunar seismic scattering. This model enables us to investigate the shallow lunar fracture system using seismic data and to suppress seismic coda for detecting critical phases reflected from deep interiors.

authors.name: Lei Zhang, Qian Huang, Minghao Huang, Jinhai Zhang, Dijun Guo

papers.title: Differentiable topology optimization for high-fidelity acoustic holography beyond the thin-element approximation
papers.summary: Acoustic holography in the megahertz range can impact applications from manufacturing and non-destructive testing to transcranial ultrasound. Designing lens topologies for complex holograms in the sub-megahertz to low-megahertz regime most relevant to transcranial therapy is difficult because wave propagation through an acoustically thick lens cannot be ignored. Here we show that the heterogeneous angular spectrum approach (HASA), which admits in-plane varying speed-of-sound maps and supports rapid differentiable optimization with the Adam optimizer, can generate three-dimensional lens topologies directly. With it we quantify the failure of the thin-element approximation (TEA) at these frequencies, where lenses enter an acoustically thick regime (thickness L much greater than the wavelength) governed by refractive walk-off, and we introduce a dimensionless refractive walk-off number Nw that defines a frequency-dependent operating regime. Topology optimization outperformed TEA-based design in all 45 configurations tested, with the largest structural gains at or below 1 MHz; for high-numerical-aperture designs the fidelity at 1 MHz matched that at 2 MHz, while structural similarity was highest at 0.5 MHz. The sub-megahertz to low-megahertz window is therefore a favorable operating regime for high-fidelity transcranial holography rather than one to be avoided. Free-field hydrophone measurements of 3D-printed lenses reproduced the designed patterns, and because the framework also accounts for aberration in heterogeneous media, patient-specific lenses corrected skull-induced aberration in simulation and ex vivo experiment, generalized across skull segments, and shaped volumetric beams through the human skull. Together these results provide a framework for designing simple, economical, and high-performance ultrasound systems.

authors.name: Pradosh Pritam Dash, Costas D. Arvanitis

papers.title: High-Efficiency Wakefield Acceleration of Positrons via a Slit Plasma Channel
papers.summary: Although plasma-based wakefield acceleration has achieved remarkable success for electrons, efficient positron acceleration remains a long standing challenge, as positrons suffer severe defocusing in the accelerating phases of such structures. Here, we propose a slit plasma wakefield acceleration (SPWA) scheme, in which a relativistic electron beam propagating through a slit channel formed by two parallel plasma slabs excites crossing plasma-electron filamentary structures within the slit, generating intense wakefields tailored to simultaneously provide longitudinal acceleration and transverse focusing for a trailing positron bunch. A theoretical model is developed to characterize the wakefield structure responsible for positron acceleration and focusing. Three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations validate the model, and demonstrate that the SPWA scheme achieves a positron trapping efficiency of nearly 100%, while maintaining low emittance growth and narrow energy spread for an injected positron beam. These findings establish a new and robust approach to high-efficiency positron acceleration, with promising implications for future compact electron-positron colliders and high-energy positron applications.

authors.name: Yu-Jie Wang, Xing-Long Zhu, Hong-Kang Zuo, Zheng-Ming Sheng

papers.title: From Sea Surface Height to Velocity - A Machine Learning Approach
papers.summary: Inferring upper-ocean velocity from altimetric sea surface height (SSH) remains challenging below 50~km, scales now resolved by the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission. Conventional methods rely on geostrophic or cyclogeostrophic balance. Here, we demonstrate that deep learning can predict the full velocity vector from SSH and environmental data and recover derivative-based diagnostics, including spectral energy flux. We trained a U-Net encoder--decoder on hourly fields from the pre-SWOT Cape Basin extraction of the LLC4320 ocean simulation, with 1.5-km grid spacing ($11.8$--$15.8^\circ$E, $41$--$45^\circ$S). Inputs were SSH, sea surface temperature (SST), and wind stress; targets were horizontal velocities at the surface and 50~m, where wind influence is weaker. At 50~m, the best model achieves a speed RMSE of $0.049\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, 29% lower than the geostrophic approximation. Predicted relative vorticity has a correlation of 0.93, compared with 0.75 for the geostrophic approximation. The model also recovers divergence with a correlation of 0.66, whereas geostrophic velocity is nondivergent by definition. Tests of training strategies yield four findings: SSH gradients outperform raw SSH as inputs; wind stress is the most useful covariate for total velocity prediction; SST benefits vary seasonally; and including vorticity and divergence in the loss improves accuracy. These results offer a path for transferring high-fidelity simulation physics to SWOT applications, where kilometer-scale SSH snapshots contain superposed balanced and unbalanced signals.

authors.name: Yaswanth Reddy Yaradoddi, Jinbo Wang, Elyes Serghine

papers.title: Flow and transport characteristics of hydrogen in a square-spiral Knudsen pump with coupled thermal transpiration and Poiseuille flow
papers.summary: Gas transport driven by thermal transpiration under temperature gradients, known as a Knudsen pump, has shown strong potential in gas separation and delivery applications. However, its performance and operational stability are strongly affected by structural design, system integration, and manufacturing complexity, highlighting the need for efficient and manufacturable multi-stage configurations. In this study, a novel spiral-structured Knudsen pump is proposed. Within the microchannels, a temperature gradient drives gas from the low- to high-temperature region, inducing pressure rise and thermal transpiration. In the main channel, a pressure gradient drives gas from the high- to low-temperature region, forming Poiseuille flow. Numerical methods are employed to investigate the flow mechanisms, and the effects of varying the numbers of series and parallel microchannels on gas transmission behavior are evaluated. The results indicate that bends of the main channel lead to nonlinear variations in pressure and temperature, as well as flow deceleration in the curved regions. Increasing the number of serial channels reduces the pressure load across the microchannel, thereby enhancing the overall transport performance. For instance, a ten-stage serial configuration improves performance by 3.35% compared with the four-stage case, reaching 3.10E10-7 kg/(m*s). In contrast, increasing the number of parallel microchannels reduces pressure loading while enhancing gas rarefaction, thereby strengthening thermal transpiration. A five-stage parallel configuration yields an 70.80% improvement over the two-stage case, reaching 3.07E10-7 kg/(m*s). These results provide valuable guidance for the design and fabrication of high-performance Knudsen pumps.

authors.name: Yawei Huang, Jianjun Ye, Junlong Xie, Jian Xiao, Dinggen Li, Xuesong He

papers.title: Conceptual Design of Pumping Systems up to 1000 m3/s Based on Non-Evaporable Getters in a Gas-Dynamic Magnetic Trap
papers.summary: The Gas-Dynamic Magnetic Trap (GDMT), a new linear magnetic facility for confining high-temperature hydrogen plasma, is currently under development at the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics (BINP SB RAS). The total hydrogen flow that must be removed from the end expanders by the vacuum system is approximately 10^22 molecules/s, which corresponds to a required pumping speed on the order of 500 m3/s. Non-evaporable getters (NEG) are considered as a possible pumping method for this application. This article presents experimental studies of Ti-Zr-Al getters manufactured by Polema LLC. The pumping speed, sorption capacity, and sticking factors of the getter surface were measured. The sticking factors for hydrogen and deuterium are 2.23% and 1.54%, respectively. The getter pumping speed is maintained over 60 air-vent/reactivation cycles. Based on these results, a conceptual design of a NEG-based pumping system for the GDMT end expanders is proposed, providing a specific pumping speed of 74 m3/(m3s) for the getter panel. The proposed pumping system design and the required heating power are discussed.

authors.name: Alexey M. Semenov, Nataliy G. Vasilieva, Sergey V. Polosatkin

papers.title: Asymptotic electromagnetic transition conditions for thin layers: the arithmetic-mean field and susceptibility hybridization
papers.summary: Effective transition conditions that replace a thin polarizable layer by a zero-thickness sheet are commonly applied in electromagnetic models of two-dimensional (2D) materials and metasurfaces. These conditions usually take the arithmetic mean of the fields on either side as the polarizing field at the boundary, and characterize the layer by the $0^\mathrm{th}$ moment of its susceptibility, but both choices are typically imposed rather than derived. We derive transition conditions for a finite-thickness, in-plane homogeneous, in-plane isotropic layer with a general nonlocal susceptibility, using a single-scale asymptotic expansion in $\eta = l\max(k_0,q)$, where $l$ is the layer thickness, $k_0$ the free-space wavenumber and $q$ the in-plane wavenumber. The sheet limit must be taken after resumming the out-of-plane depolarizing field, as this ensures that the resulting sheet susceptibility is independent of the material thickness. The arithmetic mean then emerges as the leading-order polarizing field for general susceptibility profiles. Asymmetries in the layer profile modify the effective susceptibility appearing in the transition conditions, rather than altering the arithmetic-mean field prescription. If the spatial profile is not even in both out-of-plane coordinates, in-plane and out-of-plane response hybridize, turning the diagonal volumetric susceptibility into a $q$-dependent effective tensor surface susceptibility with off-diagonal components. Mirror symmetry alone does not remove this hybridization. Comparison with exact solutions for local and separable layers shows that the derived conditions remain accurate to $O(\eta)$ across propagating and evanescent excitations, whereas the standard sheet conditions fail once hybridization becomes appreciable.

authors.name: Asbjorn Hansen

papers.title: The preplasma origin of the plasma-mirror reflectivity response
papers.summary: Plasma mirrors (PM) enhance the temporal contrast of high-power lasers, but declining reflectivity at subrelativistic intensities limits their energy throughput. Here we show that prepulse-generated preplasma drives this decline in p polarization primarily through absorption. Particle-in-cell simulations using a measured prepulse profile reproduce the reflectivity decrease, with near- and far-field energy accounting showing a weak contribution from scattering. Optical-cycle-resolved electron tracking reveals successive electron bunches extracted from the plasma surface, supporting a vacuum-heating interpretation. Under the simulated conditions, s-polarized absorption remains weak and no comparable decline occurs. Applying the model to two representative double-plasma-mirror (DPM) systems, BELLA and CoReLS, it captures both the p-polarized and s-polarized reflectivity responses across the operating range. Yet, the model still misses the high-fluence s-polarized reflectivity rollover, and further investigation of the scattering channel might be needed. These findings connect prepulse history to polarization-dependent energy loss, informing the choice of plasma-mirror operating conditions.

authors.name: Zhongwei Wang, Douglass Schumacher

papers.title: Reference-Beam-Assisted Perturbation-Resistant Imaging Through A Single Multimode Fiber
papers.summary: Multimode fiber (MMF) imaging is highly sensitive to mechanical perturbations, which alter modal coupling and disrupt the speckle-to-target mapping. Here, we propose a reference-beam-assisted method for image reconstruction across multiple fiber configurations. An independent reference beam propagates through the same MMF as the imaging signal without target modulation, providing target-independent transmission-state information through its speckle patterns without requiring a separate configuration-sensing structure. A neural network jointly processes the signal and reference speckles to reconstruct target images. Experiments with MNIST and Fashion-MNIST across 10 fiber configurations demonstrate improved reconstruction quality, faster training convergence, and more accurate configuration identification. Further evaluation across 40 configurations confirms the reconstruction benefit of reference-beam assistance over a larger set of perturbed fiber states. These results provide a foundation for developing perturbation-adaptive MMF imaging systems for flexible endoscopy and minimally invasive optical diagnostics.

authors.name: Bowen Sun, Maohan Li, Jingwei Luo, Zhuoren Wan, Zhaoyang Wen, Yuan Chen, Wending Huang, Zijian Wang, Ming Yan, Heping Zeng

papers.title: Transitional Fluid-Ablation Interactions on a Compression Ramp at Mach 8
papers.summary: Direct numerical simulations (DNS) are performed for a Mach 8 flow over a 15 degree compression ramp undergoing ablation to analyze fluid-ablation interaction (FAI) effects on instability growth and transition of the high-speed boundary layer. Wind-tunnel experiments at these conditions show characteristic heating streaks which are first replicated for laminar flow over an inert ramp. Perturbations superimposed on the laminar baseflow are informed by stability calculations. The ramp is then replaced by a low-temperature ablator in our DNS and the interaction of the streaks with the ablating surface is examined. Ablation models implemented in two independently-developed fluid dynamics solvers are used to study this problem. Overall, both solvers have shown an excellent agreement regarding heat fluxes, mass blowing rates, and recession patterns. Numerical experiments are performed to assess the impact of accelerating recession and of higher amplitude perturbations. We demonstrate accurate predictions of ablative recession and present novel findings regarding its influence on the perturbation evolution for this configuration.

authors.name: Ata Onur Ba\c{s}kaya, Sean Dungan, Stefan Hickel, Christoph Brehm

papers.title: Probabilistic Modeling of Photon Interaction Chains in a Silicon Detector
papers.summary: Compton camera imaging relies on the positions and energies of multiple photon interactions recorded in the detector. In silicon detectors that resolve individual interactions, these measurements do not directly provide the causal interaction order, and in nuclear medicine applications the photon may also have scattered in the object before entering the detector. We present a probabilistic model for photon interaction chains in a silicon detector and use it for two inference tasks at the event level: interaction order inference and classification of primary versus object-scattered photons. The model combines photon transport based on Compton scattering and attenuation with a detector response model. It is evaluated on Monte Carlo data for monoenergetic point sources at 140~keV and 511~keV, with and without a cylindrical water phantom. For interaction chains of length two to four, the maximum a posteriori order estimate gives high accuracy in the case without a phantom, exceeding 0.95 for all chain lengths at 511~keV, and decreasing with increasing phantom radius. The gap between the two highest posterior order probabilities provides a confidence measure for the ordering estimate and can be used to increase accuracy at the cost of reduced retention. For scatter classification, likelihood-ratio testing yields receiver operating characteristic curves with area under the curve above 0.85 across all phantom radii considered. These results support the use of probabilistic modeling of measured interaction sequences for inference directly at the event level, and show that both interaction ordering and scatter discrimination can be treated within a common framework.

authors.name: Per Lundhammar, Luca Terenzi, Mats Danielsson, Moa Yveborg Tamm, Mats Persson

papers.title: GeoSim: Benchmarking Multi-Field Neural Operators for Geodynamics
papers.summary: Learning reliable surrogates for geodynamic models requires benchmarks that resolve coupled fields and temporal stability. We present GeoSim, a benchmark of high-resolution two-dimensional mantle-plume simulations generated with I2VIS, comprising 237 trajectories across two parameter regimes, with six coupled fields, physical timestamps, and trajectory-level splits. GeoSim defines short-window prediction and autonomous rollout, and evaluates representative neural operators field by field. Across models, we observe a pronounced scalar--velocity gap: scalar fields are reconstructed accurately while velocity errors remain large, and short-window accuracy does not imply stable rollout. We also evaluate MFGNO (Multi-Field Graph Neural Operator), a joint multi-field graph baseline designed for this benchmark; on GeoSim-Plume1, under a fixed per-field objective, it reduces horizontal and vertical velocity errors by 58.4% and 38.5% relative to an independent-field graph baseline, while an explicit field-difference input shows no measurable benefit at this scale. GeoSim provides a reproducible benchmark for field-wise diagnosis and long-horizon evaluation of geodynamic surrogates.

authors.name: Hailong Liu, Dinghui Yang, Mengxue Liu, Rui Qi, Meng Zhao, Yihang Tang, Jin Wen, Zhilong Fang

papers.title: Machine learning emulators of dynamic global vegetation models for fast gridded carbon budget predictions
papers.summary: The land carbon sink explains most of the variability of the atmospheric CO2 growth rate, but the Global Carbon Budget estimates it with dynamic global vegetation models (DGVMs) run once a year. Emulators could provide it sooner if they reproduce each model outside its training period. Here we show that convolutional neural network emulators of 19 of these models, driven by ERA5 climate and their own past predictions, reproduce the global land sink of these models and its spread over two years not used in training. Global monthly net biome production (NBP) anomalies were reproduced with a median R^2 of 0.81. The error of the multi-model mean annual NBP was at most 0.23 GtC yr^-1. At the grid-cell level, the median R^2 of monthly anomalies was 0.30, partly because of errors that accumulate in the emulated NBP history.

authors.name: Piyu Ke, Xiaofan Gui, Stephen Sitch, Zhu Liu, Xun Li, Jiang Bian, Pierre Friedlingstein, Philippe Ciais

papers.title: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
papers.summary: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2\pi$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole contributions in atoms exhibiting only electric dipole transitions. This eliminates the need to simultaneously excite pure electric-dipole and magnetic-dipole responses with exactly matched radiation. We derive a two-mode model for this response and show that it accurately captures full coupled-dipole simulations near the optimal lattice spacings. Because of the wide applicability of coupled-dipole models, the relevance of our microscopic analysis extends beyond atomic physics to nanostructured metasurfaces. Moreover, the same platform also connects directly to established subradiance-protected single-photon storage protocols, suggesting a route toward combining wavefront engineering, storage, and retrieval in a simple atomic bilayer.

authors.name: K. E. Ballantine, J. Ruostekoski

papers.title: Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Reveals Grotthuss Transport in Concentrated Electrolytes
papers.summary: Proton transfer is responsible for the anomalous high conductivity in acidic or basic aqueous solutions. Yet, the contribution of the proton transfer mechanism to the conductivity of concentrated aqueous solutions is unknown. In this work, we compute the transport properties of KOH(aq) systems with different concentrations, using Molecular Dynamics simulations with a Machine Learning Interatomic Potential (MLIP), which includes proton transfer. We quantify the contribution of the proton transfer mechanism to the diffusivities of hydroxide ions and water molecules, and the ionic conductivity and transport numbers of the electrolytes. The contribution is substantial at lower concentrations, but diminishes at very high concentrations.

authors.name: {\O}ystein Gullbrekken, Sondre Kvalv{\aa}g Schnell

papers.title: Impedance-controlled Laser Dynamics in Near-Zero Index Media
papers.summary: Near-zero-index (NZI) media have been explored for controlling spontaneous emission, but their impact on stimulated emission and lasing properties remains unexplored within their different classes, i.e., epsilon-near-zero (ENZ), mu-near-zero (MNZ), or epsilon-and-mu-near-zero (EMNZ). Here, we show theoretically that lasing emission depends on the class of NZI medium and can be controlled through its impedance. The major difference, as compared to conventional laser media, arises from the incorporation of dispersive electric and magnetic properties in the derivation of the Maxwell Boch equations. In this framework, the analysis of laser rate equation reveals that the ENZ class, with high impedance, can reduce the lasing threshold through enhanced electric-field interaction. Numerical simulations further show that the NZI class also governs the spectral response: whereas ENZ and MNZ classes suffer from multimode emission, the EMNZ class preserves single-mode emission.

authors.name: Adrien Debacq, Andrei V. Lavrinenko, Elizaveta Semenova, Olivier Deparis, Micha\"el Lobet

papers.title: Fluid memory beyond creeping flow: a history kernel for a sphere at finite Reynolds numbers
papers.summary: Predicting the history force on a sphere beyond the creeping-flow limit remains challenging. Existing formulations have been derived or calibrated for selected flow histories, with limited evidence of their predictive accuracy under more general conditions. We develop a systematic approach to extract the history kernel of a fixed sphere in spatially uniform, unsteady flow from axisymmetric Navier-Stokes simulations of finite-duration acceleration and deceleration ramps at initial Reynolds numbers from 0.2 to 200. The resulting kernel surface recovers the Basset limit at short lags and in the creeping-flow limit and is continued beyond the resolved lags using far-wake asymptotics. At higher Reynolds numbers, the kernel develops non-monotonic behaviour at intermediate lags, associated with delayed adjustment of the boundary layer and wake. For the cases tested, the present kernel substantially improves history-force predictions for finite ramps, oscillatory forcing and non-periodic composite velocity histories relative to the literature formulations considered, without case-specific adjustment. These findings indicate that lag and Reynolds number capture the dominant memory response.

authors.name: M. D. {\L}asica, J. G. M. Kuerten, S. K. F. Stoter

papers.title: Low-Terahertz Channel Performance in Falling Wheat for Moisture Sensing
papers.summary: Terahertz (THz) waves are highly sensitive to water and therefore offer a promising noncontact approach to wheat moisture sensing, but existing THz studies have been limited to static samples. This article investigates moisture sensing based on the performance of a THz channel in falling wheat, as encountered at grain intake. The channel power loss is measured at six frequencies from 120 to 320 GHz for three moisture contents and interpreted with a physics-based model that couples the double-Debye permittivity of water, Landau-Lifshitz-Looyenga mixing, and Lorenz-Mie extinction. The model reproduces the measured loss. Above the extinction maximum, the dielectric moisture response peaks where the wavelength approaches the kernel diameter, and that a two-frequency loss ratio removes the loading dependence. A channel-level analysis of QPSK and 16-QAM links shows that a 1 dB moisture-induced loss change alters the bit error rate (BER) by a factor of 3 to 30. THz communication channels at grain intake could therefore sense moisture as a byproduct of data transmission.

authors.name: Xiaoxiang Li, Hanchen Liu, Kefeng Huang, Jiabiao Zhao, Mingxia Zhang, Jie Yang, Yuheng Song, Wenbo Liu, Peian Li, Chunhua Zhu, Jianjun Ma

papers.title: A flux-balanced diffuse-interface kinetic model for rarefied gas-solid boundaries with arbitrary absorption probability
papers.summary: Rarefied gas--solid interactions determine mechanical loads, heat transfer, and material exchange in microscale devices and low-pressure processings. Modeling these interactions becomes challenging when gas non-equilibrium effect and complex moving boundaries must be resolved together. We develop a diffuse-interface kinetic model (DIKM) that describes rarefied gas transport and gas--solid interactions in one kinetic formulation on a single fixed Eulerian mesh. A smooth order parameter represents solid geometry, while a localized molecular flux operator incorporates boundary interactions directly into the kinetic equation by distinguishing incident and reflected distributions in the interface region and specifying their mass, momentum, and energy exchange, including prescribed surface absorption. Matched asymptotic analysis shows that the diffuse formulation recovers the corresponding partially absorbing diffuse-reflection boundary condition for smooth stationary or moving surfaces in the sharp-interface limit. Discretization uses Strang splitting, combining an order-parameter-weighted discrete unified gas kinetic scheme for the transport substep with a positivity-preserving update of the interfacial source. Benchmarks over planar and curved, stationary and moving boundaries reproduce rarefaction-dependent velocity slip and wall heat transfer, absorption-driven flow, and feedback between gas forces and solid translation and rotation. In final simulations, the order parameter evolves by a Cahn--Hilliard equation with degenerate mobility, and thin-film growth exhibits distinct surface profiles at different vapor incidence angles. By connecting implicit geometry to molecular surface exchange, DIKM provides a basis for coupling rarefied gas dynamics to solid motion and material evolution.

authors.name: Chujin Qin, Dongke Sun

papers.title: Eddy currents and error fields in the toroidally segmented shell configuration aka Armadillo
papers.summary: A stream function formulation for the calculation of the eddy current distribution in a toroidally segmented conducting shell (Armadillo) is presented and verified. The governing Poisson-like equation is solved spectrally via a Discrete Sine Transform, which enforces the zero-current boundary condition at each gap exactly by construction, and the related radial magnetic field at the plasma surface is obtained by Biot-Savart integration. The toroidal eddy current flows in the same direction on every sector with a cosine-like poloidal distribution, while the poloidal return current, required by current continuity, peaks near each gap and reverses sign between adjacent sectors. The scaling of both components with the number of gaps is governed by the competition between the poloidal geometric scale of the shell and the toroidal segmentation scale. The transition between the two regimes is set by the aspect ratio of the device, around eight gaps for an RFX-mod2-like geometry, as predicted by the analytical wall time model of the Armadillo configuration. At the gap, the poloidal return current produces a radial field of opposite sign to the value far from the gap; the resulting non-axisymmetric error field peaks near this transition and becomes negligible for highly segmented shells. These results provide a first characterisation of the eddy currents and error fields of the Armadillo configuration, needed for future resistive wall mode and tearing mode stability analyses.

authors.name: D. Abate, A. Corbioli, G. Marchiori

papers.title: On flow unsteadiness in strongly separated high-speed ramp flows using kinetic and data-driven methods
papers.summary: The gas dynamics of high speed flows over several compression-expansion ramp geometries with large separation regions were investigated using a particle kinetic approach and data driven methods. These large separation regions allow study of the role of scaled angle predicted by triple deck theory on recirculation strength, separation size, and appearance of secondary recirculation regions, all of which lead to flow unsteadiness. Examining four different free stream conditions for the same geometry using the direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) approach, we show that the stability of single recirculation in the separation region is more sensitive to wall temperature and free stream velocity than physical ramp angle. Stability in this context refers to appearance of secondary separation regions. In addition, configurations with similar types of recirculation regions from literature considered, we find that general trends regarding unsteadiness, such as appearance of secondary recirculation regions, mostly hold; however, the flows are too complex to be characterized by only scaled angle. Thus, stochastic flowfields generated by DSMC were investigated using data driven methods, namely spectral proper orthogonal decomposition and dynamic mode decomposition. We found that both methods yield similar frequency components and mode shapes for spatio-temporal coherent structures of unsteady DSMC flows. With the help of these structures, the main mechanisms of unsteadiness were identified as oscillations of the reattachment shock, Kelvin-Helmholtz like instability of the shear layer, and c-shaped mode of the separation bubble. This is the first time SPOD has been applied to a DSMC generated flowfield and compared with DMD.

authors.name: Irmak Taylan Karpuzcu, Mert Senkardesler, Deborah A. Levin

papers.title: Designing turbulence through hierarchies
papers.summary: Turbulence is defined by a set of emergent and singular phenomena: a constant-flux energy cascade, intermittency, a dissipation rate that survives the vanishing of viscosity, and the spontaneous loss of determinism of the inviscid limit. Which physical ingredients produce them remains unclear, because in fluids they always come together with incompressibility, spatial structure and vortex dynamics. Here we show that a hierarchy of inertia, coupled by the purely geometric nonlinearity of rigid constraints, is enough. A planar chain of rigid pendula whose lengths and masses decrease geometrically, coupled only through nearest-neighbor constraints, develops a far-from-equilibrium cascade that replaces thermal equipartition, with statistically local and time-irreversible energy transfer despite intrinsically nonlocal coupling. Its fluctuations are intermittent, yet self-similarity is restored by a hidden scale symmetry. As the viscosity vanishes, the dissipation rate saturates at a finite value, and thermal noise consistent with fluctuation-dissipation balance is amplified from the smallest to the largest scales within a fraction of a large-scale period. Because the hierarchy can be tuned and the same dynamics can be realized mechanically or electrically, turbulence becomes a property that can be designed and measured in the laboratory.

authors.name: Flavio Tuteri, Andr\'e Freitas

papers.title: Perioperative shear wave elastography for the evaluation of spinal cord release in pediatric dysraphism: first experience in 21 patients
papers.summary: OBJECTIVE Shear wave elastography (SWE) is a recent method for evaluating soft tissue stiffness. Its application to the spinal cord is limited by the ultrasound bone barrier. Spinal dysraphism can cause neurological symptoms impairing bladder, bowel, and lower limb function due to a mechanical stress known as tethered cord syndrome. Detethering of the spinal cord is a part of surgical treatment. This study aimed to assess the feasibility of intraoperative elastography to guide surgery in patients with spinal dysraphism involving traction of the spinal cord. METHODS This single-center retrospective study included all patients who underwent surgery for spinal dysraphism between November 2023 and July 2024. SWE was performed under general anesthesia with the patient in the prone position before and after spinal cord detethering. All SWE measurements were performed using the Aixplorer system. Demographic, clinical, and radiological data (age at surgery, neurological status, and MRI findings) were collected. RESULTS Twenty-one patients with a mean $\pm$ SD (range) age of 3.7 $\pm$ 5.3 (0--17.5) years were included. Etiologies included open saccular dysraphism (n = 3), spinal cord conus lipoma (n = 6), limited dorsal myeloschisis (n = 3), and fibrolipomatous filum (n = 9). In 85% of patients, at least 1 clip was of sufficient quality for analysis both before and after release. The mean $\pm$ SD (range) spinal cord stiffness at the beginning of surgery was 25.2 $\pm$ 9.2 (12.3--39.1) kPa and 11.2 $\pm$ 3.8 (6.2--16.5) kPa at the end of release, with a significant stiffness decrease (p = 0.018). No complications attributable to SWE were observed. CONCLUSIONS SWE of the spinal cord in patients with spinal dysraphism is a safe and feasible imaging method. This technique may assist in assessing the adequacy of untethering during surgery. However, no established normative SWE values for the pediatric spinal cord currently exist. Until it does, the intraoperative interpretability and clinical utility of this technique remain limited.

authors.name: Mathilde Gaume (IBHGC), Lou Richard (IBHGC), Claudio Vergari (IBHGC), Eleonore Blondiaux (ISIR, SU FdS, AP-HP), Marius Buffard (ISIR, SU FdS, AP-HP), Raphael Vialle (ISIR, SU FdS, AP-HP), Timoth{\'e}e de Saint-Denis (SU)

papers.title: RadarFill: Observation-Constrained Gap Filling of Systematic Blind Zones in 3-D Weather Radar Reflectivity Mosaics
papers.summary: Ground-based weather radar mosaics contain systematic blind zones, especially at low altitudes, where missing reflectivity lacks corresponding complete observations for direct verification. We present RadarFill, an observation-constrained conditional diffusion framework for gap filling in three-dimensional radar reflectivity mosaics. RadarFill conditions on partially observed reflectivity and an observation mask, enforces available observations throughout reverse sampling, and preserves valid measurements in the final field. For training and controlled evaluation, structured synthetic missingness is designed from altitude-dependent missing-data statistics and the vertical nesting of blind zones in an operational 3-D radar mosaic product. Across 4,384 held-out test times and representative convective and typhoon cases, RadarFill recovers principal precipitation structures and moderate-to-strong echoes under extensive low-level missingness and generally outperforms conventional interpolation and a learning-based reference model. For real blind-zone evaluation, RadarFill model is applied directly to Fujian Province and compared with 90 matched volume scans from an independent phased-array radar. Within the principal 1-2 km low-level blind zones, RadarFill yields lower reflectivity errors than conventional interpolation, and the gap-filled precipitation structures show broad agreement with independent observations. In two controlled nowcasting experiments, improvements in RadarFill-initialized fields persist into subsequent forecasts, with the largest benefits at low altitudes and short lead times. These results provide complementary evidence from controlled synthetic missingness, independent radar observations, and downstream nowcasting, supporting the potential of observation-constrained conditional generation for gap filling in real 3-D radar blind zones.

authors.name: Xin Huang, Haofei Sun, Wei Han, Yunfan Yang, Huaguan Chen, Xingtao Song, Dong Xiao

papers.title: Reconstructing Rayleigh--B\'enard flows from temperature-only measurements using the Ensemble Kalman Filter
papers.summary: Reconstructing the full state of a multiscale chaotic system from observations of only a subset of its degrees of freedom is a central problem in data assimilation. Turbulent Rayleigh--B\'enard convection offers a paradigmatic example, for which Charney conjectured that temperature measurements alone should suffice to determine the velocity field. Synchronization-based methods such as nudging and direct replacement nonetheless fail in chaotic regimes, because they require the measurement of the determining modes of the system, a set to which the velocity belongs but the temperature does not. Here we show that the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF), equipped with a proper inflation scheme, removes this asymmetry by exploiting the flow-dependent cross-covariances between temperature and vorticity, and recovers the velocity from noisy and spatio-temporally sparse temperature data alone. We assess the filter in two chaotic regimes of two-dimensional bulk convection by means of a scale-by-scale spectral analysis. When the whole temperature field is observed, both fields synchronize with the true state at all resolved scales, with the temperature estimate becoming even more accurate than the measurements themselves for sufficiently frequent observations. Equispaced observation networks preserve this full-spectrum synchronization down to a threshold density, below which only the largest scales remain synchronized, as also happens when observations are confined to a subdomain. We conclude that Charney's conjecture is numerically verified in two-dimensional turbulent convection when the assimilation is performed using a properly calibrated EnKF.

authors.name: Francesco Fossella, Luca Biferale, Alberto Carrassi, Massimo Cencini, Mathieu Desbrun, Kiwon Um

papers.title: Observation of pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals
papers.summary: Photonic pseudospins enable selective excitation and routing of light, but perturbations that mix opposite pseudospins can induce backscattering in helical edge channels. Here, we experimentally demonstrate pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals, combining pseudospin selectivity with nonreciprocal unidirectional propagation. By jointly engineering lattice deformation and magnetic bias, we control dipolar-quadrupolar band inversions and construct interfaces supporting pseudospin-selective chiral channels. Microwave near-field and transmission measurements reveal a single chiral edge branch that is selectively excited by only one source handedness and exhibits pronounced nonreciprocal transport. Extending this mechanism to multidomain structures, we combine two pseudospin channels into a common waveguide, separate them into distinct outputs, and route them through intersecting interfaces. These configurations realize a nonreciprocal photonic pseudospin multiplexer and demultiplexer, together with a waveguide crossing exhibiting average measured crosstalk of -14.1 and -15.8 dB for its two input channels. Our results present an experimental route to integrating pseudospin-selective channel control with chiral edge transport, providing a foundation for nonreciprocal photonic networks that use pseudospin to organize and route multiple wave channels.

authors.name: Chengle Fan, Kaizhou Shi, Xiang Xi, Zhen Gao

papers.title: Influence of Geometry and Tissue Damage on the Mechanical Behaviour of Skin Meshing
papers.summary: Skin meshing increases graft coverage, yet the clinically achieved expansion often falls below the manufacturer's nominal meshing ratio. Previous elastic analyses have demonstrated that mesh topology and skin anisotropy strongly influence graft expansion; however, the effect of progressive damage at larger deformation remains unexplored. This study therefore investigates how progressive damage affects the expansion and mechanical response of skin meshes. The performance of auxetic mesh geometries is compared with conventional Zimmer mesher (ZM) geometry. Human back skin was modelled using a one-term Ogden ground matrix and a Gasser Ogden Holzapfel (GOH) collagen network, with separate scalar Kachanov-type continuum damage variables for each constituent. The auxetic geometries, including 1st- and 2nd-order alternative slits (AS1 and AS2), I-shaped (IS) and H-shaped (HS) re-entrant patterns, and ZM, were analysed with Langer's lines oriented either parallel or perpendicular to the loading direction. Hyperelastic and damage-based formulations were compared up to 25% strain, and the damage-based simulations were subsequently extended to 40% strain. ZM was further loaded to 155% strain; the area ratios attained by HS at 40% strain were matched by ZM at 142.1% and 124.7% strain for Langer's lines parallel and perpendicular to loading, respectively. Results indicate that HS achieves greater coverage than ZM for a given stretch, whereas its damage advantage depends on the orientation of Langer's lines.

authors.name: Masoumeh Razaghi Pey Ghaleh, Denis O'Mahoney, Kevin Moerman

papers.title: A Multidimensional Evaluation Framework for Artificial Intelligence-Based Ocean State Forecasts
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) based ocean state forecasts now approach or surpass those produced by operational ocean forecasting systems as measured by conventional pointwise metrics. However, these metrics may favor spatially smoothed forecasts and cannot determine whether forecast variables remain physically coherent.
