The formulation is verified for plane P- and S-waves propagating in an elastic homogeneous full space with a mirror suspended in a spherical cavity, assuming that the wavelength is much larger than the radius of the cavity, so that wave scattering can be ignored. Excellent agreement with analytical solutions is obtained. Similar good agreement is reported for the Newtonian noise on a test mass suspended at a finite distance above the free surface of a homogeneous elastic halfspace in which a Rayleigh wave propagates. The methodology has been implemented in the ANNA Newtonian Noise Analysis toolbox which runs in the MATLAB programming and numeric computing platform and is compatible with the open-source GNU Octave Scientific Programming Language; a Python version is also available. The proposed finite element framework provides a physically consistent and computationally efficient approach for computing gravitational-seismic coupling in heterogeneous media.

authors.name: Pieter Reumers, Xhorxha Kuci, Stijn Fran\c{c}ois, Geert Degrande

papers.title: Small-Scale Dynamo for Full Spectrum of Hydrodynamic Turbulence in Kazantsev Model
papers.summary: A method is proposed for computing coefficients in the Kazantsev equation of small-scale dynamo for the full spectrum of hydromagnetic turbulence comprising the inertial range together with the range of viscous dissipation. The dynamo equation with so-defined coefficients is solved numerically for magnetic (Rm) and hydrodynamic (Re) Reynolds numbers from $10^2$ to $10^8$. The threshold value ${\rm Rm}_c$ for onset of dynamo increases initially with Re but then saturates at a constant value of ${\rm Rm}_c \simeq 300$ for ${\rm Re}\geq 10^5$. In the case of small Prandtl number Pm = Rm/Re 1$ but slows down and then saturates at a value somewhat below the inverse lifetime of most short-living eddies. An explanation of the results is proposed.

authors.name: Leonid Kitchatinov

papers.title: Supershear Rupture Indicator in Near-fault Particle Motion
papers.summary: Earthquake rupture propagation speed is an essential source parameter that fundamentally controls hazard and risk. In this paper, we develop and demonstrate the capability of a single near-fault seismic record in delineating earthquake rupture speed by inspecting displacement particle motion. We apply this method to near-fault strong-motion data in M7+ strike-slip earthquakes and identify diverse particle-motion signatures associated with subshear rupture, supershear rupture, supershear transition, initial rupture expansion, and potential multiple rupture fronts. This study highlights the value of near-fault observations for determining rupture speed.

authors.name: Suli Yao, Hongfeng yang, Harsha S. Bhat, Hideo Aochi

papers.title: Positron Emission Tomography with quantum-entangled Compton events: first imaging results at clinically relevant activities
papers.summary: In Positron Emission Tomography, a potential, yet unutilized enhancement, may come from exploiting the quantum entanglement of the annihilation quanta, inscribed in the correlation of their polarizations. To investigate this, we built a PET demonstrator capable of measuring polarization correlations of annihilation quanta by their Compton scattering, based on single-layer scintillator polarimeters. We present a detailed study of the imaging of two $^{68}$Ge line sources, 45 MBq each, to extract the spatial resolution and assess image quality. The results show that a spatial resolution of 2.5$\pm$0.1 mm is obtained using single-pixel events, while resolutions obtained with polarization-correlated Compton events range from 3.6$\pm$0.3 mm to 4.9$\pm$0.3 mm, depending on data selection criteria. We also found that the polarization-correlated Compton events exhibit up to 20% higher average signal to random background ratio compared to the single-pixel events. We also present the first imaging of the NEMA NU-4 phantom filled with a $^{68}$Ga solution of 378 MBq initial activity, successfully combining polarization-correlated events with conventional single-pixel event selection. Based on the extracted spatial resolution, signal-to-background, signal-to-noise, contrast, and contrast-to-noise ratio, we estimate that up to 10% sensitivity increase may be attained by exploiting the polarization-correlated events, while preserving a high image quality.

authors.name: Mihael Makek, Ana Marija Ko\v{z}uljevi\'c, Tomislav Bokuli\'c, Darko Gro\v{s}ev, Zdenka Kuncic, Siddharth Parashari, Luka Paveli\'c

papers.title: Interaction of vortex rings generated by two unsynchronised drop impacts
papers.summary: A liquid drop falling into a pool can create a vortex ring at the right impact conditions. Such drop-formed vortex rings are of importance in nature and technology and the dynamics of rings created by single and synchronised double drop impacts have been extensively studied. In practice, two neighbouring drops rarely impact a liquid surface exactly at the same time, yet the interaction of two unsynchronised vortex rings have not been studied. Here, we have performed experiments with two water drops impacting a water pool at varying time differences $\Delta t$. By using particle image velocimetry, we have quantified the time-evolution of the resulting vortex rings. We find four distinct categories of vortex ring evolution depending on $\Delta t$. At $\Delta t<0.5$ ms, fully symmetric merging of the vortex rings occur. At unsynchronisation larger than this, the merging either becomes asymmetric and incomplete ($0.5 < \Delta t<7$ ms) or non-existent ($\Delta t \geq 7$ ms). At $7 \leq \Delta t<80$ ms, the creation of the second vortex ring is impaired, whereas at $\Delta t\geq 80$ ms, the first impact no longer affects the formation of the second ring and the two rings evolve without influencing each other. We show that these regimes can be explained by the capillary waves created by the first droplet. Our results demonstrate the importance of the time difference between drop impacts in the creation and subsequent interaction of two adjacent drop-formed vortex rings, which is important for achieving uniform and controlled mixing in high-throughput applications.

authors.name: Anna A. L. Huttunen, Guilherme Moreira Bessa, Matilda Backholm

papers.title: Spectral taxonomy for quartic systems: fundamental clock, parity, and continuum
papers.summary: A symmetric quartic potential is a physics model with expansive applications, ranging from broadband energy harvesters, quantum tunneling in molecules and the early universe, to torque-free spacecraft rotation. Its rich dynamics have been traditionally classified into regimes and expressed as disjointed time-domain solutions. Here we build a taxonomy for this broad class of motions and discover that their regimes exhibit a symmetrical spectral structure: they share a fundamental clock, obey parity selection, and dissolve into the separatrix through a discrete-to-continuum transition. Applied to the famous Dzhanibekov effect where a rotating body periodically undergoes rapid 180-degree flips in its attitude, the taxonomy reveals its spectral anatomy. The three principal-axis rotations share a common clock while occupying distinct parity channels, with stable-axis branches exchanging DC bias across the separatrix. We discuss a case study where the three spectral pillars: clock, parity, and continuum, survive the Wick rotation from real-time into imaginary-time kinematics.

authors.name: Teepanis Chachiyo

papers.title: Disorder-Induced Eigenstate Localization of Molecular Polaritons Despite Spectroscopic Strong Coupling
papers.summary: Molecular polaritons are hybrid light--matter states whose collective character is associated with a molecular excitation extended across many molecules. However, clearly resolved polariton peaks do not by themselves establish that the corresponding eigenstates retain this molecular delocalization. Here, we use a disordered Tavis--Cummings model to distinguish spectral signatures of strong coupling from eigenstate-level molecular delocalization of electronic polaritons. Static energetic disorder can strongly reduce the molecular extent of optically visible polariton states while resolved polariton peaks persist and their apparent separation can even increase. We quantify this crossover using complementary molecular localization measures applied to individual optically visible eigenstates and the photon-weighted bright sector. Finite-size scaling shows a stable large-ensemble crossover; for Gaussian disorder, retaining approximately half of the homogeneous molecular extent requires a collective coupling roughly seven times the Gaussian disorder standard deviation $\sigma$, although the numerical scale depends on the disorder distribution. Including cavity and molecular linewidths through a non Hermitian Hamiltonian reveals a contrasting spectral and eigenstate response: finite linewidths reduce spectral resolvability, while cavity--molecule linewidth imbalance shifts the localization crossover to larger static disorder by suppressing the disproportionate contribution of near-resonant molecular transitions. Spectroscopic strong coupling and eigenstate-level molecular delocalization therefore characterize distinct properties and need not evolve in parallel under disorder and dissipation.

authors.name: Amitav Sahu, T\"onu Pullerits

papers.title: Open-ended innovation arm-race in zero-sum games
papers.summary: We discuss zero-sum games with open-ended innovation, whereby each player may introduce new strategies. The innovation process is modeled as a draw of new strategies form a distribution. It is argued that, when the cost of innovation is vanishingly small, this setting can lead to an everlasting innovation arm-race. In particular, the introduction of new technologies of the advanced player increases the marginal utility for technological innovation of the backward one, whereas innovation of the backward player discourages the more advanced one to innovate.

authors.name: Matteo Marsili, Leandro Chaves Rego

papers.title: Valley polarization driven by two-color circular fields from a strong-field tunneling perspective
papers.summary: Valley polarization in hexagonal materials driven by the form of the lightwave and its orientation relative to the lattice, rather than solely by the helicity of the driver, has recently been demonstrated both theoretically and experimentally. This has extended valley control to the non-resonant, sub-cycle regime and to inversion-symmetric materials. One interpretation of this field-orientation-dependent valley polarization is that the laser-dressed, cycle-averaged band structure obtained from a Floquet-type approach is modified so as to lift the degeneracy between the valleys. Here, we derive a complementary explanation based on strong-field tunneling dynamics. We show that the effective valley gap at the dominant injection times depends on the orientation of the field relative to the lattice through the trigonal-warping term of the low-energy dispersion. We derive general expressions for co- and counter-rotating $\omega+N\omega$ fields and show that the leading orientation-dependent contribution survives the cycle average only for field configurations compatible with the threefold lattice symmetry, most notably counter-rotating $\omega+2\omega$ and co-rotating $\omega+4\omega$ fields.

authors.name: Rui E. F. Silva, Olga Smirnova, Misha Ivanov, \'Alvaro Jim\'enez-Gal\'an

papers.title: Chemical potentials from structure factors: I. Neutral multi-component mixtures
papers.summary: The chemical potentials of multi-component mixtures underlie many physical and chemical phenomena, but remain challenging to compute. The S0 method enables the computation of chemical potentials from equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, by leveraging the thermodynamic relationship between particle number fluctuations and derivatives of chemical potentials, followed by numerical integration along different compositions. Here we generalize the S0 method from two-component mixtures to neutral multi-component mixtures. We first extend the statistical mechanical formalism to high-dimensional compositional space, and then introduce a Gaussian process integration scheme combined with active learning to efficiently integrate chemical potentials and sample diverse compositions. We use this method to compute the mixing free energies of a molten metal alloy, and the solubilities of two paracetamol polymorphs in water-ethanol solvents. The extended S0 method provides a practical and scalable route for computing chemical potentials in neutral bulk multi-component mixtures from atomistic simulations.

authors.name: Roya Savoj, Xiaoyu Wang, Musahid Ahmed, Bingqing Cheng

papers.title: Observation of s-p Coupling in Ultralong-Range Rydberg Molecules
papers.summary: Ultralong-range Rydberg molecules, formed by the interaction between a highly excited Rydberg atom and a ground-state atom, provide a unique platform for exploring quantum phenomena spanning nanometer- to micrometer distances as well as exotic few-body interactions. The molecular binding arises from electron-atom scattering, which is conventionally described by an independent s- and p-wave channels picture. Here we report the experimental observation of s-p coupling in Rb(nS)-Rb(5S) ultralong-range Rydberg molecules via high-resolution photoassociation spectroscopy. By varying the principal quantum number n from 31 to 36, we resolve an avoided crossing between the s- and p-wave molecular states: whenever a vibrational level bound by the p-wave well approaches one bound by the s-wave well in energy, the two states are mixed by the off-diagonal coupling U_sp, and the shifted s-wave level is identified, which is consistent with theoretical predictions. This mixing is most pronounced for low-node p-wave molecules, whose binding energies lie closer to those of the s-wave molecules. The resulting level repulsion and redistribution of spectral intensity reveal the mixed s-p character of ultralong-range Rydberg molecules and provide a more precise molecular spectroscopy.

authors.name: Qing Li, Shi-Yao Shao, Jun Zhang, Han-Chao Chen, Li-Hua Zhang, Bang Liu, Guang-Can Guo, Dong-Sheng Ding, Bao-Sen Shi

papers.title: An Interacting-Response Constraint for Photon Density Functionals
papers.summary: When the coupling to a quantized field becomes weak, the leading term of the photon exchange--correlation action depends on the fluctuations of the interacting electronic system, not those of a density-matched noninteracting reference. We establish this requirement by proposing an adiabatic connection formulation of electron-photon coupling at fixed electronic density and controlling the density derivatives. Approximating the response in the integral yields a ring functional in terms of the Kohn--Sham response and electronic kernel. Exact model tests verify fourth-order rather than second-order errors. In a two-electron Hubbard dimer, the functional correctly predicts a correlation-induced polarization reversal, while two Kohn--Sham photon prescriptions don't. In an interacting quantum-dot resonator model with electron injection and escape, the functional recovers resonant photon-assisted transport missed by two Kohn--Sham photon prescriptions.

authors.name: Xiaoyu Zhang

papers.title: Phase-controlled super-modes in a `lossy' tri-waveguide coupled micro-ring resonator system
papers.summary: In coupled micro-ring resonator (MRR) systems, the coupling process plays a critical role in determining the optical response, yet models of these structures typically assume this process to be either lossless, or dissipative with either purely real or purely imaginary coupling rate, respectively. Dissipative coupling is contingent on having appropriately phase engineered structures with intricate coupling geometries, but systems exhibiting `lossy coupling', i.e., characterized by complex-valued coupling rates, have received comparatively little attention. In this work, we investigate the effect of such `lossy' coupling, by modelling the optical response of a tri-waveguide coupled MRR system, using Temporal Coupled-Mode Theory (TCMT). The `lossy' coupling occurs via a common bus waveguide, positioned between a pair of MRRs, leading to the emergence of a pair of intrinsic resonances, whose frequency and linewidth may be tailored by controlling the respective coupling rates from either MRR. We develop these ideas, and by connecting the input (driving) waveguides, using a 3dB y-splitter, demonstrate a novel, coherently driven, lossy-coupled MRR, which exhibits either an absorptive or transparent resonance peak on demand by phase-controlled super-modes.

authors.name: Tianrui Li, Max Goodwin, Matthew P. Halsall, Iain F. Crowe

papers.title: Polarized quantum effects in countable signals from intense laser - electron beam interactions
papers.summary: We investigate the feasibility of precision counting experiments in laser-electron-beam collisions for testing strong-field quantum electrodynamics (QED), with particular emphasis on spin-dependent effects. To resolve such rare signals, we develop a high-precision Monte Carlo model combining spin- and polarization-resolved QED rates with weighted photon packets, hierarchical-mesh sampling, and adaptive time stepping. The model is quantitatively benchmarked against the high-energy edge of the photon spectrum and the positron yield in the SLAC E-144 experiment. The high-energy photon spectrum and total positron yield are only weakly affected by spin-dependent corrections, even at higher laser intensities. In contrast, we find that spin asymmetry in photon emission significantly affects the polarization of photons in the high-energy tail, while spin asymmetry in pair production manifests itself as a spin-dependent imbalance in the large-angle positron population. These microscopic spin asymmetries give rise to experimentally countable signals through their correlations with the oscillating laser field. Our predictions could be tested using moderate-energy electron beams and optical lasers with intensities of approximately 10^22 W/cm2, as envisaged in future ELI-NP experiments.

authors.name: Toseo Moritaka, Kensuke Homma, Kazunori Itakura

papers.title: Hydrogen and Lithium Isotope Analysis via Optical Spectroscopy of Laser-Produced Plasmas
papers.summary: Accurate detection and quantification of light-element isotopes, particularly hydrogen (H) and lithium (Li), are essential across chemistry, materials science, geology, nuclear energy, forensics, and defense applications. Their isotopic compositions provide insight into fuel cycles, materials degradation, mass transport, and environmental processes. Hydrogen and Li isotopes are especially relevant in nuclear environments because neutron-induced reactions directly connect their isotopic inventories. Despite their importance, analysis of these light isotopes remains challenging due to their low atomic mass, high mobility, and, in some cases, radiological constraints. While some existing analytical techniques can detect and measure H and/or Li, they typically require extensive sample preparation, laboratory-based instrumentation, or extended analysis times that preclude real-time monitoring capabilities. To address these limitations, optical spectroscopy of laser-produced plasmas offers a promising solution, enabling field-deployable, standoff sensing of isotopic signatures with real-time analysis capability and no sample preparation requirement. This Topical Review summarizes fundamentals and recent advances in H and Li isotopic analysis using optical spectroscopy, with emphasis on laser-produced plasmas generated by laser ablation of solid targets. Key concepts relevant to isotope-resolved optical measurements are introduced, including isotope shifts, fine and hyperfine structure, and line-broadening mechanisms. Progress in optical emission, laser induced fluorescence, and absorption spectroscopy is reviewed for H and Li isotopes.

authors.name: Elizabeth Kautz, Caleb Clark, Nusrat Karim, Mark C. Phillips, Sivanandan S. Harilal

papers.title: Characterization of immersed SiPM arrays in liquid scintillator between room temperature and $-30\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$
papers.summary: Liquid scintillator detectors instrumented with distributed silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) arrays can be used in compact, topology-sensitive, and low-background experiments, but the temperature dependence of SiPMs immersed directly in the scintillation medium has not been widely characterized. We report the operation of a 125-liter linear-alkylbenzene-based liquid scintillator detector read out by 125 SiPM channels immersed in the active volume, over the range from room temperature to $-30\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. The detector response was measured with cosmic-ray muons, including stopping muons followed by their Michel-electron decay. Cooling from $+15\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $-30\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ reduced the SiPM dark-count rate by a factor of 13.5, increased the single-photoelectron response by 49.1%, and increased the cosmic-ray muon light yield by 16.7%. The improved photoelectron separation and baseline stability at low temperature enabled a selection of stopping-muon events, from which the effective muon lifetime was measured to be $1959\pm132\,\mathrm{ns}$, consistent with the value expected for a hydrocarbon scintillator once $\mu^{-}$ capture on carbon is taken into account.

authors.name: M. S. Kwak, J. S. Chung, C. Ha, T. Z. Huang, J. Kim, S. A. Kim, H. Kimku, B. C. Koh, H. S. Lee, S. Lee, Y. J. Lee, J. Seo

papers.title: Emergence in Network Systems is Bounded by Boundary-Crossing Paths
papers.summary: Emergence, features of a whole that no part shows alone, is central to complex systems but rarely measured so as to locate its source. Viewing a system structurally, as a network of interacting parts, we evaluate emergence as what observing the coupled whole reveals beyond, or erases from, the combined observations of the parts. For observations that build what they see route by route, we show that every emergent feature is produced by its own route across the interface between parts, a route that traces it to the components and interactions responsible. We show the number of all such boundary-crossing paths bounds the total emergence discrepancy, and equals the emergence of measures that count routes. The bound is computed locally around the interface, validated through network examples, and in a nervous system the routes show that interneurons relay most of the emergence. Our work associates emergence with path structure in the network system that can be anticipated, attributed, and engineered.

authors.name: Johnny Jingze Li, Gabriel A. Silva

papers.title: Residual AM and PM Noise of Selected X-Band Amplifiers
papers.summary: In microwave systems design, amplitude modulation (AM) noise is often ignored relative to phase modulation (PM) noise. However, in high-performance applications requiring ultra-low PM noise, AM noise becomes a critical limiting factor due to AM-to-PM conversion mechanisms. Because AM noise specifications are rarely, if ever, provided for commercial microwave components, this study characterizes the residual AM and PM noise of several 10 GHz amplifiers. We present performance data for various Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor (HBT) amplifier designs and demonstrate the noise reduction achieved through power-summed configurations. For example, a discrete-die GaAs HBT amplifier achieves residual PM noise below $-160$ dBrad$^2$/Hz and AM noise of approximately $-155$ dB/Hz at a 1 kHz offset in a quad power-summed configuration. A notable finding is that the majority of amplifier designs surveyed in this study exhibit higher AM noise relative to their PM noise, with only a few exceptions. The impact of bias supply quality on residual noise is also quantified, demonstrating that the choice of voltage regulator is a first-order design parameter below 1 kHz offset.

authors.name: Archita Hati, Craig Nelson, Scott Littrell

papers.title: Advances in the Vacuum Magnetic Birefringence measurement using a pulsed Foil Coil
papers.summary: In this paper, in the framework of the {\it Bir\'efringence Magn\'etique du Vide} (BMV) experiment, we present our current apparatus in detail and we discuss its critical points. We also report the results obtained using specially designed pulsed coils called Foil Coils. Our novel measurement of the vacuum linear magnetic birefringence constant is $K_{VMB} < 1.7 \cdot 10^{-21}~\text{T}^{-2}$ at a confidence level of 68$\%$, which is an improvement with respect to our previous 2014 measurement.

authors.name: Enzo Rodriguez Alvarez, Jonathan Agil, Julien Billette, J\'er\^ome B\'eard, R\'emy Battesti, Carlo Rizzo

papers.title: When can buoyancy be neglected in simulations of crystallization fouling? Evidence from a confluence flow cell
papers.summary: Predicting crystallization fouling remains difficult because it couples supersaturation, nucleation, crystal growth, transport, and adhesion. Separating these processes requires model systems in which they can be independently controlled. One such system is the confluence flow cell, where two incompatible brines mix and generate supersaturation at their interface. The mixing pattern is often predicted using constant-density simulations because density differences between the brines are typically only a few percent or less. We investigate whether this assumption holds when calcium chloride and sodium sulfate react to form gypsum. A constant-density simulation predicts deposition on the channel floor along the centreline. Experimentally, however, gypsum forms bands on both side walls, with deposition moving upstream as flow rate decreases. Dye experiments spanning density differences of 0.14 to 2.1 %, three channel heights, and 32 flow rates show that the distance required for the dyed stream to reach the opposite wall is governed by the bulk Richardson number, $Ri=g'H/U^2$, following $L/H = 3.31\,Ri^{-0.66}$ over four decades in Ri ($R^2=0.89$). When the stream densities are matched, the dyed stream typically no longer reaches the opposite wall, and a reacting experiment shows gypsum deposition on the floor, consistent with the constant-density simulation. A small density difference alone is therefore insufficient to neglect buoyancy; the Richardson number must also be small. At the low flow rates typical of confluence flow cells, this condition is often not met. Because Ri depends only on density difference, channel height, and flow velocity, we recommend evaluating it before applying constant-density models of mixing, reaction, or fouling.

authors.name: Isaac Appelquist L{\o}ge, Candela Almaz\'an P\'erez, Maike W. Baltussen, Nadia Shardt

papers.title: Advanced computational methods for simulating the classical hydrogen atom in stochastic electrodynamics
papers.summary: Stochastic electrodynamics (SED) is a theory of nature seeking to derive key aspects of quantum mechanics and quantum electrodynamics from a purely classical physics perspective. While SED has been successful in many areas, it has had mixed success when addressing the classical hydrogen atom bathed in classical electromagnetic zero-point radiation. Because analytical approaches are largely intractable, advanced numerical simulation methods are required. To address this, we develop a pseudo-wave formulation that integrates the solid angle in k-space utilizing symmetry, resulting in a significantly reduced memory footprint and lower computational overhead for generating the zero-point radiation spectrum. This optimization is paired with a logarithmic frequency grid, a sliding window tracking the instantaneous Keplerian frequency, and a Tukey smoothing function to eliminate discrete force discontinuities. Integrated via an adaptive RK4 algorithm with step-doubling across highly dense grids of up to 100-million bins, these techniques demonstrate the asymptotic convergence of ensemble stability. We show that increasing grid resolution in the high-frequency domain systematically mitigates artificial electron decay, yielding a simulated probability density function that closely aligns with the quantum mechanical ground state P(r). Crucially, the simulations exhibit stable, low-eccentricity orbits without any observed atomic ionization events.

authors.name: Daniel C. Cole

papers.title: Negative partisanship drives anti-frontrunner volatility in election dynamics
papers.summary: Negative partisanship-where voter mobilization is driven primarily by aversion toward an opposing candidate rather than positive alignment-profoundly reshapes modern electoral dynamics. Here, we formulate a two-dimensional piecewise map to model campaign opinion dynamics, where voter abstention arises endogenously from a latent spectrum of voter activation barriers. We show that cross-candidate rejection sensitivity triggers a non-smooth collapse of abstention, dividing the phase space into an under-mobilized regime and a fully mobilized campaign regime. In symmetric elections with radicalized voter bases, spontaneous symmetry breaking via a pitchfork bifurcation gives rise to asymmetric polling attractors partitioned by mirror-symmetric basins of attraction, where early public perceptions-encoded in initial campaign conditions-act as a deterministic catalyst selecting candidate lead lock-in long before election day. For elevated cross-rejection, the symmetric equilibrium destabilizes via a period-doubling flip bifurcation, driving persistent anti-frontrunner polling swings. Rather than predicting static candidate hegemony, our model reveals that high negative partisanship turns elections into time-sensitive dynamical systems, where final election outcomes reflect discrete sampling snapshots of an oscillating campaign trajectory.

authors.name: Jos\'e F. Fontanari

papers.title: Non-Maxwellianity in Temperature Relaxation between Plasma Species
papers.summary: Temperature relaxation between plasma species is usually described by Landau--Spitzer (LS) theory, which assumes Maxwellian distributions throughout. We show analytically that, for two Maxwellian species in homogeneous isotropic plasmas, the interspecies collisions driving relaxation generate a universal three-lobe initial distortion and that these distortions initially reduce energy exchange over a broad parameter range. Full Fokker--Planck simulations reveal substantial relaxation delays when interspecies deformation competes with self-thermalization. For post-shock deuterium--tritium plasmas relevant to inertial confinement fusion, with $T_{\mathrm{T}}/T_{\mathrm{D}}=1.5$, the relaxation time exceeds the LS prediction by 47%. The accompanying distortions lower the apparent DD/DT temperature ratio and produce positive DD and negative DT Gamow-shift residuals relative to Maxwellian predictions. These results also motivate examining non-Maxwellianity in fuel heating by fusion $\alpha$ particles.

authors.name: Yao Guo, Dong Wu, Jie Zhang

papers.title: A living catalog of stream interaction regions in the Parker Solar Probe era
papers.summary: Stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are important phenomena in heliospheric physics. These large-scale structures vary temporally and spatially, both in latitude and with radial distance. The additions of Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter have allowed for investigations into the radial evolution of these structures over a wide range of heliocentric distances for the first time since the Helios era. To better enable investigations of SIRs and CIRs within the inner heliosphere, we have developed a living catalog of SIR and CIR observations by Parker Solar Probe with corresponding observations by STEREO-A as well as ACE and Wind at 1 au. The methodology used for the identification of events and the generation of this catalog, the initial catalog of PSP observations spanning orbits one through five along with corresponding 1 au observations, and information on accessing the living catalog for future studies is described. This list of SIR and CIR events from PSP and corresponding observations from other heliophysics missions will enable case studies utilizing unique orbital arrangements, as well as aid in future statistical studies to further understand the properties and evolution of these structures.

authors.name: R. C. Allen, G. C. Ho, L. K. Jian, S. K. Vines, S. D. Bale, A. W. Case, M. E. Hill, C. J. Joyce, J. C. Kasper, K. E. Korreck, D. M. Malaspina, D. J. McComas, R. McNutt, C. M\"ostl, D. Odstrcil, N. Raouafi, N. A. Schwadron, M. L. Stevens

papers.title: Delayed maximum energy solar energetic particle events: Statistical analysis from Solar Orbiter
papers.summary: Investigations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) have long utilized the dispersive nature of onset times, as in, the earlier arrival of higher-energy particles compared to lower-energy particles, to infer information such as the path length to the acceleration site at the time of initial particle release. However, recent observations by Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe have begun to characterize SEP events with an apparent delay in arrival times of the higher energy portion of the particle distribution, above a critical energy separating the delayed particles from that of the typical velocity dispersion signature at lower energies. Features of these delayed maximum energy (DME) SEP events, sometimes referred to as "inverse velocity dispersion" events, could provide new insight into the impacts of magnetic connectivity to locations along an expanding coronal mass ejection-driven (CME-driven) shock wave, variations of acceleration along the shock surface, and transport effects in the inner heliosphere. This study focuses on the occurrence rate and characteristics of DME events observed by Solar Orbiter relative to their footpoint locations with respect to the initial flare site. These DME events show a bias in occurrence rate towards events when the observer's footpoints were westward of the associated flare location. Additionally, estimated locations at which the highest-energy particles of DME events are released into the flux tube suggest continued release of increasingly higher-energy particles from the CME-driven shock into the connected flux tube well into the inner heliosphere. This indicates that DME events could be attributed to inner heliospheric effects and are not actually coronal in origin. This finding is consistent with previous observations and interpretations of SEP events connected westward of the associated flare.

authors.name: R. C. Allen, G. C. Ho, G. M. Mason, Z. Ding, M. H. Walker, A. Kouloumvakos, R. F. Wimmer-Schweingruber, J. Rodriguez-Pacheco, S. K. Vines, R. J. Filwett, Z. Xu, C. M. S. Cohen

papers.title: Stabilization of counter propagating currents by energy conservation in collisions
papers.summary: Current filamentation generates magnetic fields and shapes electron transport in dense plasmas, where collisions can either suppress or enhance its growth. Here we show that conserving electron kinetic energy in a collisional model can change both the dominant instability and its characteristic wavelength. We develop a linear kinetic theory for drifting, anisotropic electron populations with a relaxation operator that conserves particle number and laboratory-frame kinetic energy while allowing momentum transfer to a stationary ion background. For counterstreaming currents, energy conservation maintains the stabilizing influence of charge separation over a broader range of collision frequencies than a model conserving particle number alone. At intermediate collision rates, the resulting suppression of transverse filamentation allows a nearly aperiodic oblique mode to dominate, reducing the maximum growth rate and shifting the wavelength of the fastest-growing perturbation. Two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations support predicted growth rates of up to more than a magnitude lower than expected without energy conserving collision.

authors.name: Thomas Kluge, Jannis Schulz, Arthur Hirsch-Passicos, Pawel Ordyna, Ulrich Schramm

papers.title: Symmetry breaking in minimum dissipation networks
papers.summary: Natural and engineered supply networks exhibit universal structural patterns, such as the formation of loops, yet the principles governing optimal structures remain unclear. These patterns can be interpreted as solutions of optimization problems in which dissipation is minimized under a constraint on the available resources. Optimal networks break the symmetry of such a problem in two distinct ways: weakly, where the topology stays symmetric but the edge capacities do not, and strongly, altering the topology itself. Both scenarios are organized by the symmetry group of the optimization problem, which determines the pattern of capacities in the weakly broken state and may constrain the residual symmetry of the strongly broken one. Symmetric structures are favored at intermediate fluctuation levels, i.e., noise both induces and suppresses symmetry breaking. Here, we show that symmetry breaking, influenced by network meshing, resource constraints and fluctuations, is a generic organizing principle of optimal transport networks.

authors.name: Aarathi Parameswaran, Pezhman Ebrahimzadeh, Andrea Benigni, Dirk Witthaut, Iva Ba\v{c}i\'c

papers.title: Forecasting Low-Dimensional Navier-Stokes equations via Multi-Dimensional Hybrid Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.summary: The prediction of complex dynamics remains an open problem across many domains of physics, where nonlinearities and multiscale interactions severely limit the reliability of conventional forecasting methods. Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for information processing by exploiting the high dimensionality of the Hilbert space, where the dynamics of quantum systems take place. Here, we introduce a hybrid quantum-classical reservoir architecture capable of handling multivariate time series through quantum evolution combined with classical memory enhancement. Our model employs a five-qubit transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian with input-modulated dynamics and temporal multiplexing, enabling the encoding of input signals over multiple timescales. We apply this framework to two paradigmatic models of chaotic behavior in fluid dynamics, where multiscale dynamics and nonlinearities play a dominant role: a low-dimensional truncation of the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations and the Lorenz-63 system. By systematically scanning the quantum system's parameter space, we identify regions that maximize forecasting performance, as measured by the Valid Prediction Time. The observed robustness and reliable performances for both dynamical systems suggest that this hybrid quantum approach offers a flexible platform for modelling complex nonlinear time series.

authors.name: L. Salatino, L. Mariani, A. Giordano, F. D'Amore, C. Mastroianni, L. Pontieri, A. Vinci, C. Gencarelli, L. Primavera, F. Plastina, J. Settino, F. Carbone

papers.title: Universality of Layered Programmable Decompositions by Fourier Absorption
papers.summary: Decomposing arbitrary unitary transformations into physically realizable operations is fundamental to quantum information, quantum control, and linear optics. Layered programmable architectures implement such transformations by alternating tunable phase masks with fixed mode mixers. However, establishing their universality at fixed depth remains challenging: we show that neither a sufficient parameter count nor successful synthesis of sampled targets guarantees global coverage. We prove that an architecture is universal exactly when every reachable transformation can absorb a diagnostic input Fourier multiport by reprogramming its phase masks. The associated Fourier absorption residual (FAR) requires no external target ensemble, vanishes exactly for universal architectures, and bounds worst-target synthesis error. For four-mode Fourier architectures, a permutation obstruction rules out universality with five masks, even under small unitary mixer perturbations, whereas a constructive factorization establishes universality with seven. Beyond exact universality, comparison with a universal reference of the same depth yields certified uniform approximation bounds in terms of unitary mixer errors. Finally, numerical simulations using a geodesic phase optimizer illustrate the distinction between Fourier absorption and direct target synthesis.

authors.name: Javier \'Alvarez-Vizoso, David Barral

papers.title: On the non-uniformity of the 2026 FIFA World Cup draw
papers.summary: The group stage of a sports tournament is often made more appealing by introducing additional constraints in the group draw that promote an attractive and balanced group composition. For example, the number of intra-regional group matches is minimised in several world championships. Under such constraints, the traditional draw procedure may become non-uniform, meaning that the feasible allocations of the teams into groups are not equally likely to occur. Our paper quantifies this non-uniformity of the 2026 FIFA World Cup draw for the official draw procedure, as well as for 47 reasonable alternatives implied by all permutations of the four pots and two group labelling policies. We show why simulating with a recursive backtracking algorithm is intractable, and propose a workable implementation using integer programming. The official draw mechanism is found to be optimal based on two of five non-uniformity measures, including the average distortion of the 771 non-zero assignment probabilities. Nonetheless, non-uniformity can be more than halved if the organiser aims to treat the best teams drawn from the first pot equally.

authors.name: L\'aszl\'o Csat\'o, Martin Becker, Karel Devriesere, Dries Goossens

papers.title: Quantum Matrix-Element Estimators for Spin-Coupled Generalized Valence Bond (SCGVB) Wavefunctions
papers.summary: Valence-bond wavefunctions such as spin-coupled generalized valence bond (SCGVB) provide compact and chemically interpretable descriptions of strong correlation, but their nonorthogonal determinant structure makes quantum evaluation of overlaps and Hamiltonian matrix elements difficult. Here we introduce an ancilla-free, measurement-driven framework that reformulates these quantities as vacuum expectation values of Pauli-string operators, enabling evaluation with shallow circuits, local Clifford rotations, and computational-basis measurements, without controlled operations. We validate the method for H$_4$ along a dissociation pathway and for a 70-determinant C$_2$ active-valence benchmark. The reconstructed matrices agree with the classical L{\"o}wdin-based reference, while Chirgwin-Coulson weights remain chemically consistent. These results establish the proposed estimators as a low-depth, circuit-compatible formulation for evaluating SCGVB matrix elements, while making no claim of quantum computational advantage.

authors.name: Bruna Bruna G. M. Ara\'ujo

papers.title: Loss of altermagnetic order and smooth restoration of Kramers' spin degeneracy with increasing temperature in CrSb and MnTe
papers.summary: We describe how thermally induced spin fluctuations modify the electronic structures of two prototypical altermagnets, CrSb and MnTe, via application of the disordered local moment picture. For both materials, our self-consistent, ab initio calculations demonstrate that local magnetic moments persist on Cr and Mn atoms in their paramagnetic states, necessitating a spin-polarised description of the electronic structure even above the N\'eel temperature, $T_\mathrm{N}$. Moreover, Kramers' spin degeneracy, which is broken for both materials in their altermagnetic ground states, is shown to be smoothly restored - on the average - as the local moments thermally disorder. In metallic CrSb, this occurs at temperatures well below $T_\mathrm{N}$ and the signature effects of its altermagnetism are lost as the magnetic disorder induces heavy smearing of strongly dispersive electronic states around the Fermi energy. By contrast, in semiconducting MnTe, with its band gap largely unaffected by magnetic disorder, the spin degeneracy only returns at temperatures close to and above $T_\mathrm{N}$. We quantify the temperature dependence of the altermagnetic order parameter and the underlying electronic structures of both materials, with implications for their spin transport and spectroscopic properties.

authors.name: Christopher D. Woodgate, Nabil Menai, Arthur Ernst, Julie B. Staunton

papers.title: Resource-efficient energy-based operator selection in fermionic ADAPT-VQE via exact Hamiltonian transformation
papers.summary: Energy-based variants of ADAPT-VQE select operators by minimizing a one-parameter cost function for each candidate generator. In fermionic implementations, the cost of reconstructing this function often becomes a bottleneck. We reduce this cost using exact fermionic Hamiltonian transformations to obtain a generator-dependent partition of the Hamiltonian that reconstruct the same one-parameter energy function from fragment measurements. This method reproduces the fermionic Rotoselect scoring function exactly with approximately half the Pauli-string measurements. We use this formulation to benchmark the gradient-based and energy-based selection approaches in combination with two ansatz-optimization strategies---$\textit{last}$, where only the appended operator is optimized, and $\textit{full}$, where the full ansatz is re-optimized---and with both fixed-orbital and orbital-optimized formulations. The benchmark comprises $\text{LiH}$, $\text{BeH}_2$, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ at both equilibrium and stretched geometries. In the most weakly correlated system, pairing energy-based selection with $\textit{last}$ optimization enables the resource-efficient construction of an accurate ansatz, which avoids any VQE optimization. As correlation increases, full ansatz re-optimization and orbital optimization become the main factors governing convergence and overall resource cost. This study shows how exact Hamiltonian transformations provide an effective route to reducing the measurement overhead of fermionic energy-based ADAPT-VQE. Moreover, the benchmark clarifies the relative role of operator selection approach, parameter reoptimization strategy, and orbital optimization in the performance of ADAPT-VQE.

authors.name: Emanuele Rossi, Erik Rosendahl Kjellgren, Artur F. Izmaylov, Stephan P. A. Sauer, Karl Michael Ziems, Sonia Coriani

papers.title: Mechanisms governing photon-pair generation and emission directionality in quantum metasurfaces
papers.summary: Metasurfaces are emerging as a promising platform for photon-pair generation through spontaneous parametric down-conversion, thanks to their compactness, integrability, and intrinsic multifunctionality, which enables the engineering of complex quantum states. However, their full potential remains only partially exploited because the physical mechanisms governing key properties of the generated photon pairs, such as generation efficiency and emission directionality, are not yet fully understood. As a result, metasurface designs and experimental configurations are often optimized through trial-and-error procedures. Here, we theoretically investigate the main mechanisms that control photon-pair generation and detection by studying how different pump configurations and measurement geometries affect the generation efficiency, emission directionality, and collection efficiency of the emitted photon pairs. This framework allows us to interpret existing experimental results and to provide general guidelines for the design of metasurfaces and the choice of experimental configurations in future experiments. Finally, we show that substrate thickness and multilayer configurations represent additional degrees of freedom for quantum metasurface design and can be engineered to enhance the generation efficiency and control the emission directionality, providing a new route for the optimization of photon-pair sources based on metasurfaces.

authors.name: Alberto Paniate, Ivano Ruo-Berchera, Francesco Monticone

papers.title: Emergent odd response in active chiral films
papers.summary: Active chiral fluids can support an anomalous transport coefficient known as odd (or Hall) viscosity. Hydrodynamic descriptions of such fluids typically introduce odd viscosity phenomenologically. How such a response emerges from specific microscopic interactions remains incompletely understood. Here, building on classical shear rheology, we microscopically derive an odd rheological response in active chiral films: thin layers of torque-exerting, elongated particles anchored to a no-slip surface. A canonical realization of such a film is the bacterial carpet, in which flagellated bacteria are tethered head-down to a solid surface while their flagella remain free to spin and inject angular momentum into the surrounding fluid. Using a Smoluchowski kinetic theory for the orientational dynamics of these anchored particles, we derive their stress response to an imposed shear flow. We reveal that shear-induced reorientation leads to a flow-aligned polarization and a transverse surface traction from which the odd-viscosity tensor follows in closed form. This approach stands in contrast with existing microscopic theories, in which the axis of torque injection is insensitive to the flow rather than set by it. Numerical solutions of the kinetic theory further highlight saturation of the transverse traction at strong shear, driven by this orientation dynamics -- signaling departure from linear response. Our results demonstrate how odd viscosity can emerge self-consistently as a coarse-grained rheological signature of active fluid-structure interaction and establish active chiral films as a new controllable setting for odd hydrodynamics.

authors.name: Seema Chahal, Naveen Kumar D, Brato Chakrabarti

papers.title: On Optimal Measurement-State Preparation via Geometric Transport of the Squeezing Ellipse
papers.summary: Preparation of optimal measurement states is a key requirement in quantum metrology utilizing squeezed states. Besides positioning the mean state, such preparation requires proper alignment of the squeezing ellipse. We discuss a geometric framework that transforms an initially misaligned squeezed input into a measurement-optimal state in SU(2)-symmetric systems. Within this framework, the orientation of the squeezing ellipse constitutes an additional geometric degree of freedom and evolves as the mean state follows a controlled trajectory on the unit sphere. The resulting rotation of the ellipse depends on the chosen trajectory and is linked to the geometric phase through the evolution of the local basis. The discussed framework is applicable to different physical platforms admitting an effective SU(2) description. As a particular example, we consider polarization-squeezed light and outline a possible implementation using a continuously varying birefringent element.

authors.name: Vsevolod Salakhutdinov, Nikolay Kalinin

papers.title: Chemical potentials from structure factors: II. Charged multi-component mixtures
papers.summary: The chemical potentials of charged multi-component mixtures are central to electrolyte thermodynamics, but remain difficult to compute from atomistic simulations. The S0 method enables computing chemical potentials of mixtures from equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations. Here we extend the S0 method to charged mixtures by combining the composition-space framework developed in Part I: Neutral Multi-component Mixtures with a Coulombic treatment of the small-wavenumber limits of static structure factors. This approach separates thermodynamically relevant neutral composition fluctuations from forbidden macroscopic charge fluctuations, and further accounts for charge-neutrality constraints. We use the method to compute the chemical potentials of multiple-halide aqueous salt solutions, elucidating the ion-specific thermodynamic effects. We also calculate the mixing free energies of molten salt mixtures, demonstrating the importance of correctly describing long-wavelength electrostatic correlations.

authors.name: Xiaoyu Wang, Roya Savoj, Musahid Ahmed, Bingqing Cheng

papers.title: A Square-Root Barrier to Quantum Gate Speed under Linear Coupling
papers.summary: Faster quantum gates can reduce the decoherence accumulated during a computation, but in superconducting processors, speeding up gates often involves stronger microwave pulses, which can increase leakage, off-resonant excitation, stray-field errors, and crosstalk. This creates a central energy--speed--error tradeoff: can quantum state engineering make a gate faster without paying proportionally more drive energy? We address this question by treating the driving pulse as a quantum bosonic field rather than a classical waveform. For a finite-dimensional system coupled linearly to that field, we prove that gate transition rates at fixed trace distance between the initial and final system states grow at most as the square root of the pulse energy, under pulse-uniformity conditions, without assuming an upper bound on the coupling strength. The bound permits arbitrary pulse states, including squeezed and non-Gaussian states, as well as drive--system entanglement and back action; coherent Gaussian pulses attain its energy exponent. Thus squeezing or other state engineering alone cannot replace the square-root energy law of a conventional linear drive by the linear scaling allowed by general quantum speed limits. Achieving that improvement requires changing the interaction class, in addition to using a suitable nonclassical pulse, thereby identifying interaction nonlinearity as an essential resource for relaxing the practical gate-speed error tradeoff.

authors.name: Pablo Restrepo Gaviria, Mischa P. Woods

papers.title: Efficient detection of spectral cluster states
papers.summary: Multimode entangled states of light are key resources for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum information processing. Exploiting their full capabilities requires detection strategies that can efficiently and simultaneously access a large number of modes and their quantum correlations. Multimode optical parametric amplification (MOPA) provides a promising approach by amplifying multiple quadratures prior to detection, rendering the measurement robust against subsequent optical losses while enabling broadband operation. Here, we demonstrate the spectral multimode capability of MOPA by simultaneously characterizing a broadband 60-node dual-rail continuous-variable cluster state. We reconstruct the cluster-state nullifiers across the spectral modes and observe nearly uniform squeezing of up to -6.9 dB, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the highest level reported for pulsed spectrally multimode squeezed light. Furthermore, by evaluating the van Loock-Furusawa criterion across all relevant bipartitions, we verify genuine multipartite entanglement throughout the 60-node state. These results establish MOPA as a promising platform for scalable high-dimensional quantum information processing in the spectral domain.

authors.name: M. Kalash, U. -N. Han, C. Roh, M. H. M. Passos, Y. -S. Ra, M. V. Chekhova

papers.title: Marginal bunching for \textit{in situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability
papers.summary: We propose an \textit{in situ} method for certifying the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in generic linear interferometers. For particles occupying distinct input ports, the method uses two-particle marginal bunching or anti-bunching probabilities to bound full multiparticle indistinguishability through Aldous' spectral gap theorem. For Haar-random unitary interferometers, the number of experimental runs required to estimate this bound to a prescribed precision, at fixed confidence, is polynomial in the particle number, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability over the choice of interferometer. Losses are incorporated without conditioning on particle survival. The method is particularly suited to certifying photon indistinguishability in large-scale interference experiments, including Boson Sampling experiments targeting quantum computational advantage.

authors.name: Valery Shchesnovich

papers.title: Linear Response in the $\mathcal{PT}$-Broken Phase: Conductivity of Fermions with Complex Conjugate Masses
papers.summary: We examine the linear response of the $\PT$-broken phase of a BRST invariant model whose fermion masses form the complex conjugate pair $m_{\pm}=N\pm iav$. It splits into two channels, kept apart by an exact $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$, and one Euclidean correlator decides both. In the diagonal channel it oscillates in Euclidean time, so that channel admits no positive-norm realization: we exhibit a test function of negative norm and close every repair, the choice of boundary value among them. In the mixed channel the same correlator is completely monotone, which proves the spectral density positive; there we obtain the vacuum conductivity in closed form, with a real threshold at $\omega=2N$, and positivity survives at finite temperature below a bound whose onset we give exactly. The longitudinal density of that channel is negative by the square of the mass splitting; an antisymmetric derivative removes it, and the resulting field-strength composite has a positive one-particle space and a causal commutator --- at the level of the two-point function only, since a four-point reflection form on the original composite comes out negative. The positive realization is therefore not a sector of the fermion model.

authors.name: V. E. R. Lemes, D. G. Tedesco

papers.title: Meet biform singletons in your area! Topological actions for edge modes
papers.summary: We present topological field theories propagating biform singleton fields as edge modes. In even spacetime dimensions $D=2p$, these are irreducible representations of the conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,2p)$ with two-column Young diagrams of height $p$. Their duality properties depend on the parity of $p$: They propagate chiral degrees of freedom for odd $p$, and exhibit electric--magnetic duality for even $p$. We are able to construct the topological actions by realising the hidden conformal symmetry inherent to singletons geometrically in terms of an auxiliary bulk $\text{AdS}_{2p+1}$ geometry. Using these as a starting point, we are able to apply a recently established covariant boundary reduction procedure to yield novel action formulations with manifest Lorentz covariance. We also show how, breaking manifest Lorentz covariance, we recover known formulations of biform singletons.

authors.name: Calvin Y. -R. Chen, Euihun Joung, Karapet Mkrtchyan

papers.title: Worldsheet functional RG and the $\alpha'$-tower
papers.summary: We apply the functional renormalization group to the worldsheet theory of the bosonic string. Imposing the Weyl anomaly cancellation as a condition on the local renormalization group flow, we derive flow equations for the background couplings and the corresponding effective spacetime equations of motion, first in a two-derivative truncation, on a general curved background. We then consider a truncation to all orders in $\alpha'$, which captures only a subset of the possible tensor structures but is analytically tractable, in analogy with $f(R)$-like approximations. Within this truncation, we obtain Tseytlin's spacetime effective action, and we use it to study solutions to all orders in $\alpha'$, including black holes. Our results show that the functional renormalization group can be implemented on the string worldsheet and provide a framework to access the strong-curvature regime. As a longer-term goal, this may allow one to test the scenario of effective asymptotic safety in string theory, in which an approximately scale-invariant regime lies between the low-energy effective field theory and a stringy completion.

authors.name: Ivano Basile, Francesco Ferrarin, Alessia Platania, Matteo Zatti

papers.title: A New Holographic Duality for Conformal Mass Deformations
papers.summary: We construct a space-dependent conformal mass deformation of ABJM on the half-space $z>0$ and show that the vacua of this theory are dual to a large class of half-BPS bubbling solutions of the form $AdS_3\times S^3\times S^3\times\Sigma$, with superalgebra $D(2,1|\gamma)^{\oplus2}$, parametrized by $\gamma<0$. The conformal symmetry of a plane is preserved provided that the mass deformation scales as $m(z)=\frac{c}{z}$. We give the first field-theory explanation of the exceptional superalgebra parameter $\gamma$ in M2-brane field theory in terms of the coefficient of the inverse-distance mass deformation of ABJM: $\gamma=\frac{1-2c}{1+2c}$. We demonstrate this using the methods of Polchinski and Strassler, which we first apply to the Janus interfaces of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills and ABJM to relate localized mass sources to scalar matching conditions.

authors.name: Rapha\"el Dulac

papers.title: Chaos on the mass shell
papers.summary: We study particle production in high-energy states for theories given by an RG flow between an asymptotically free or conformal theory in the UV and a massive theory in the IR. Using the framework of detector matching, we argue that distributions of produced particles satisfy universal evolution equations with energy, determined by the spectrum of light-ray operators of the UV theory. In particular, we interpret the UV Chew-Frautschi plot as a wave equation for particle densities on the mass shell, evolving with energy. (When the UV theory is a CFT, this wave equation is the same one that controls the spread of chaos in hyperbolic space at a particular temperature.) We test these ideas for integrable flows in 2d CFTs, finding an independent derivation of the evolution equations in terms of the thermodynamics of a Feynman gas. We also discuss consequences for 4d gauge theories, including the presence of a BFKL contrail produced by an outgoing wave of hadron number density.

authors.name: Alexandre Homrich, David Simmons-Duffin, George Yuzhe Zhou

papers.title: Inner Product of Closed Universe from Gravitational Path-integral
papers.summary: We construct the Hilbert space of a closed universe of fixed topology in anti-de Sitter (AdS) and de Sitter (dS) Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity from the gravitational path integral. Quantizing gravity involves several subtleties, including the choice of lapse contour, path-integral measure, operator ordering, global structure of the gauge group, the implementation of gravitational constraints and the gauge symmetries at initial and final timeslices. We develop a formalism that addresses these issues and determines the inner product of physical states, providing a framework to assign probabilities to cosmological wavefunctions. For a fixed topology and a lapse contour, we compute the inner product exactly and obtain the corresponding resolution of the identity in JT gravity. We demonstrate that the co-invariant and invariant Hilbert spaces in refined algebraic quantization arise from particular gauge fixing at the initial and final timeslices. In particular, the formalism provides precise meaning for a gravitational wavefunction with fixed geometric data as a co-invariant state, including its integral measure. These constructions can be formulated within the Hamiltonian BFV-BRST formalism. We also discuss the global structure of the Hilbert space, which differs from that of BF theory and depends on the prescription adopted near the big bang/crunch. Our results imply that the cylinder geometry captures the gravitational inner product for all perturbative states, including the Hartle-Hawking no-boundary state.

authors.name: Masamichi Miyaji, Sunil Sake, Kotaro Shinmyo

papers.title: A Sojourn Through $c=1$ String Theory
papers.summary: We revisit the $S$-matrix, the thermal $S$-matrix and the thermal free energy of $c=1$ string theory from the worldsheet perspective. By numerically integrating Virasoro conformal blocks with DOZZ structure constants, we compute the scattering amplitudes and thermal amplitudes up to 6-point at tree level and up to 3-point at one loop, in addition to the genus two thermal free energy. All results are in agreement with the predicted answers from the $c=1$ matrix model.

authors.name: Sam Christian, Yuchen Wang, Xi Yin, Yutai Zhang

papers.title: Compact holography via polarized IKKT
papers.summary: The polarized IKKT matrix model is a $U(N)$ supersymmetric matrix integral proposed to be dual to an $N$ D-instanton sector of Euclidean type IIB string theory. We show a direct path from matrix model saddles to supergravity saddles: matrix model resolvent $\to$ holomorphic function $\to$ 2D Coulomb potential $\to$ 4D Coulomb potential $\to$ supergravity fields, where the last step was previously described. Here, the 2D electrostatics picture is an exact finite $N$ reformulation of a localization deformation of the matrix model that gives a constrained gas of dipoles in a background field. We show a matching between supergravity and matrix model on-shell actions and protected observables for all saddles. We show that the supergravity saddles have a compact and non-singular metric in string frame with the Einstein frame asymptotic region replaced by a pointlike D-instanton source. We provide evidence that the physics of particular gravity saddles can be obtained through restricting the domain of the matrix model integral to a basin associated with the corresponding matrix model saddle. We describe certain large $N$ decoupling limits where families of the saddles decouple from the rest to give the gravity duals of certain higher-dimensional field theories.

authors.name: Arsam Najafian, Mark Van Raamsdonk, Alejandro Vilar L\'opez

papers.title: Resonant electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes
papers.summary: We construct nonlinear electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes in the bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory. These configurations are supported by harmonically time-dependent charged gauge fields, while their energy-momentum tensor remains static. Regularity at the horizon imposes a resonance condition relating the field frequency to the horizon electrostatic potential. Unlike linear clouds, these solutions exhibit a finite mass and electric charge gap, and exist only up to a maximal horizon size. We obtain both magnetic and electric clouds, including spherically symmetric and dipolar configurations, which reduce to electroweak balls in the vanishing-horizon limit. We also report a new family of dipolar electroweak balls, which can be energetically favoured over their spherical counterparts at fixed electric charge. Our results, obtained in the probe limit for electroweak couplings away from their measured values, establish a new realization of nonlinear resonant vector hair in a non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theory.

authors.name: Carlos Herdeiro, Eugen Radu

papers.title: Reconstruction of the conformal algebra from a critical groundstate on the (fuzzy) sphere
papers.summary: Recently, we found a method to reconstruct the dilatation operator (sphere Hamiltonian) from a regulated conformal field theory groundstate. In this paper, we explore methods to construct the whole global conformal algebra, and test our construction using fuzzy sphere regularization. Starting from a groundstate of the same Hamiltonian, these methods perform better than constructions of the conformal generators based on a Hamiltonian density, are model-independent, require no additional tuning, and improve with system size. One purpose of reconstructing the conformal algebra is to identify conformal primary states, which we do with some success. We also find further evidence supporting the model of the short-distance corrections to the entanglement Hamiltonian proposed earlier and use it to make systematic improvements.

authors.name: Rolando Ramirez Camasca, Xiang Li, Ting-Chun Lin, John McGreevy

papers.title: A lattice construction of the Kormos-Runkel-Watts defect flows in minimal models
papers.summary: Kormos, Runkel, and Watts (KRW) showed that a topological defect of a diagonal minimal model $M(p,p+1)$, perturbed by a weakly relevant defect field, flows to a new conformal interface. We study the flow of the $(2,1)$ Verlinde defect $D_{(2,1)}$ driven by the spinful defect field $\phi_{(1,3)}\otimes\bar\phi_{(3,3)}$ on the lattice. The flow preserves the $(r,1)$ Verlinde lines. This preserved symmetry makes a dilute RSOS realisation possible. We study this flow numerically using both exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG). At $p=4$, the flow ends on the invertible line $\eta=D_{(3,1)}$. At $p=5$ it ends on a non-trivial conformal interface $C_5$ with $g=1.503(2)$ and transmission coefficient $T=0.665(10)$. We report its spectrum, leading irrelevant dimension, and lattice $\beta$-function. Gauging $\eta$ maps $C_5$ to an interface of the three-state Potts model, which breaks $\mathbb{Z}_3$ but is a stable interface once the Fibonacci line $\tau_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ and charge conjugation are imposed. A loop-model formulation allows us to follow the family $C_p$ at continuous $4\le p\le5$: it moves smoothly from $C_5$ to $\eta$ as we lower $p$.

authors.name: Junchen Rong

papers.title: From off-shell strings to entropy flows
papers.summary: Bit threads express holographic entropy as the maximal flux of a divergenceless vector field subject to a local capacity bound, but do not identify a physical carrier of that flux. In our previous work, we identified the projected string charge density with a bit-thread flow, reproduced the entropies of BTZ and ten-dimensional three-charge black holes, and showed that the maximal entropy flux is preserved under S- and T-dualities. However, the norm bound was imported from the bit-thread prescription, while the string-current configurations were prescribed along known bit-thread lines. In this paper, we give a stringy foundation for the local capacity and construct dynamical probe-string representatives of maximal flow. At genus zero and two-derivative order, the conical variation of the target-space action derived from the off-shell sphere fixes the string-frame entropy density. The gravitational replica construction and weighted flow-cut duality then yield the string-frame norm bound. We next find regular stationary F1 solutions in an NS-NS supported BTZ black hole whose spatial parts are logarithmic spirals. A uniform ensemble produces a conserved, constant-norm projected string charge density and realizes a maximal flow whose flux equals the BTZ entropy. We finally extend the construction to BTZ backgrounds with mixed NS-NS and RR flux. Varying the flux fraction changes the stationary F1 configurations at fixed metric and dilaton, while the corresponding conserved flows reproduce the same leading BTZ entropy. Thus, both the norm bound and its physical maximal-flow representative arise from string theory, with stationary strings providing physical channels for the entropic flux represented geometrically by bit threads.

authors.name: Houwen Wu, Shuxuan Ying

papers.title: Exotic Pauli spinors and magnetic flux quantization in a superconducting ring
papers.summary: We develop the formalism of the exotic Pauli equation and establish an effective symmetry between standard and exotic Pauli spinors to describe magnetic flux quantization in a superconducting ring within the nonrelativistic framework. We show that, once the signs of the spatial and temporal topological terms are fixed consistently by the covariant exotic Dirac equation, this symmetry is exact at the level of the equations of motion, Lagrangians and currents, with no truncation of the exotic term and no condition on the time dependence of the topological phase. Upon deriving the flux quantization condition, we explicitly construct the composite matter-gauge unitary operator acting on the Hilbert space, which implements the symmetry at the quantum level (the gauge sector requiring the usual regularization).

authors.name: L. Ibrain Cohen Iskandar, J. M. Hoff da Silva, R. T. Cavalcanti

papers.title: Hamiltonian of open string field theory for time-dependent solutions
papers.summary: Using the recently introduced expression for conserved charges of $L_\infty$ theories, we give an explicit form for the Hamiltonian of Witten's bosonic open string field theory. We evaluate it on the Erler-Maccaferri analytic solution, describing any D$p$-brane configuration associated to a BCFT. We use the expression to compute the energy of the rolling tachyon solution and find exact agreement with the boundary state result by Sen.

authors.name: Vin\'icius Bernardes, Riccardo Poletti

papers.title: Obstruction to local entropy laws on arbitrary black-hole cuts in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
papers.summary: We study local entropy laws on arbitrary cuts of event horizons in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, treated as an exact theory. No covariant local entropy can both reproduce the stationary black-hole entropy and be nondecreasing between every ordered pair of cuts, provided its density is smooth on an invariant open set of off-shell metric and cut jets containing a flat planar cut and every cut used in the argument. No global bound on derivative order is assumed. The counterexamples to the second law are vacuum black holes perturbed by a gravitational wave, with a strongly hyperbolic formulation near the relevant horizon interval and its stationary future. Shear makes the intrinsic curvature of a cut depend on its bending. The stationary entropy fixes the coefficient of this curvature term, and local corrections cannot cancel its response to cut bending. The obstruction appears at second order in wave amplitude on a smooth horizon, without a merger or topology change.

authors.name: Cendikiawan Suryaatmadja, Robert B. Mann

papers.title: Hermitian matrix-valued nonlocal deformation of the SU($N$) Thirring model at large $N$
papers.summary: We investigate a Hermitian matrix-valued nonlocal deformation of the two-dimensional $SU(N)$ Thirring model at leading order in $1/N$. We impose $f(\slashed{\partial})^\ddagger=f(\slashed{\partial})$ directly on the original action; for real nonlocality scale the admissible exponential choice is $f(\slashed{\partial})=\exp[-i\slashed{\partial}/\Lambda]$. We construct and analyze the even-in-mass (paired) large-$N$ effective potential and derive its radial kernel, weak-coupling dimensional-transmutation scale, and formal Lambert-$W$ zeros. Its radial gap integral possesses a conditionally convergent infinite-cutoff limit. The pairing prescription, however, differs from the unpaired determinant of the original Hermitian action, so the reported gap and spectral zeros must be understood as properties of this explicitly defined mean-field functional. We identify the further derivation needed to obtain physical mass gaps and fermion poles from the unpaired theory.

authors.name: J. R. Nascimento, P. J. Porf\'{\i}rio, C. Furtado

papers.title: A Ghost-Free dS/AdS Correspondence in $\mathcal{N}=1$ Supergravity
papers.summary: Reversing the sign of the scalar potential exchanges de Sitter and anti-de Sitter vacua and, through the domain-wall/cosmology correspondence, maps flat domain walls onto flat FLRW cosmologies, but its supersymmetric version has ghosts on the cosmological side. We show that this pointwise correspondence is realized between two ordinary, ghost-free four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravities with spontaneously broken supersymmetry. Within a single superconformal K\"ahler cone, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ reflection of the nilpotent goldstino K\"ahler metric through the flat limit $V=0$ reverses $V\leftrightarrow-V$ pointwise while preserving the visible K\"ahler metric, the superpotential, and the unitary-gauge fermion Lagrangian. The paired vacua obey a sharp dictionary with $H=1/L$, $m^2_{\rm dS}=-m^2_{\rm AdS}$, equal conformal weights, and $m_{3/2}>H$, and are simultaneously stable precisely within the window $0\le m^2_{\rm dS}\le\frac94H^2$ set by the Breitenlohner--Freedman bound. Applied to string compactifications and cosmology, this correspondence pairs over-uplifted with under-uplifted anti-D3-brane vacua, confines the de Sitter swampland conjecture to the goldstino (anti-brane) sector, and maps slow-roll inflation onto a healthy AdS domain wall obeying the holographic $c$-theorem.

authors.name: Omer Guleryuz

papers.title: Negative Junction Logarithms in Scalar Multipartite Entanglement
papers.summary: A three-region junction in a free real relativistic scalar vacuum in $2+1$ dimensions yields a strictly negative logarithmic contribution to genuine tripartite R\'enyi multi-entropy for every integer $n\geq3$ and all nondegenerate sector angles. The replica subtraction exactly removes loop classes associated with a single interface. Surviving loops have positive, scale-independent weight, yielding a logarithm whose sign is fixed by the negative R\'enyi prefactor. The selector is empty at $n=2$. The flat-sheet Friedrichs prescription fixes the scalar operator at the nonmanifold replica apex. It yields a convergent angular spectral formula for the coefficient.

authors.name: Chen-Te Ma

papers.title: On the universality of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory
papers.summary: The standard definition of entanglement entropy in quantum field theory requires regularizing the entangling surface and factorizing the Hilbert space, which in turn involves a choice of boundary conditions at the regularized surface. This raises two natural questions which are open at present. The first is under what conditions there is a choice of boundary conditions that leads to a unitary map between the original Hilbert space and the factorized one, which is a necessary condition for a well-defined entanglement entropy. The second concerns the situation where there are multiple such choices, in which case the question is whether they all yield the same entropy, or at least the same terms usually referred to as universal. Focusing on topological theories and using three-dimensional Chern-Simons theory as a concrete illustration, we show under specified assumptions that different such choices affect only the non-universal terms in the entropy, such that the remaining terms are universal in this sense as well, while we explicitly demonstrate that boundary conditions corresponding to non-unitary maps can change these terms. We then explain how a similar argument applies to two-dimensional conformal field theories and discuss a condition for universality in general theories.

authors.name: Orr Sela

papers.title: Gauge-invariant thermodynamic description of rotating black strings in 5D minimal supergravity via Kaluza-Klein reduction
papers.summary: We develop a gauge-invariant formulation of the thermodynamics of rotating black strings in five-dimensional minimal supergravity through Kaluza-Klein reduction. At the two-derivative level, we consistently reduce the bulk action and the Gibbons-Hawking-York boundary term, carefully accounting for the surface contributions induced by the Chern-Simons coupling.
