The resulting four-dimensional theory is $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity coupled to a single vector multiplet, with prepotential $P=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{3}}\frac{X_1^3}{X_0}$. Employing the Hamiltonian formalism, we establish the quantum statistical relation between the Euclidean on-shell action and the Gibbs free energy. We further compute the leading four-derivative corrections to the thermodynamics of a rotating magnetic black string using the Reall-Santos method. The resulting corrections are in precise agreement with previous results obtained directly for the Kerr-Newman black hole in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity.

authors.name: Yang Yu, Peng-Ju Hu

papers.title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
papers.summary: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet inflation. Starting from the quadratic perturbation actions, we construct the two-mode Hamiltonians and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing amplitudes and angles. Although the tensor speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss--Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We track the squeezing dynamics from the subhorizon to the superhorizon regime and evaluate the Nielsen wave-function complexity of the resulting two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation in the squeezing amplitudes, while the unwrapped squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Consequently, the circuit complexity is controlled mainly by the amplitude evolution. A positive coupling enhances the scalar complexity but slightly suppresses the tensor complexity for the benchmarks considered. These opposite trends show that scalar and tensor Gaussian states retain distinct information about the same modified inflationary background even when tensor propagation is luminal.

authors.name: Tao Li, Hai-Bing Fu, Lei-Hua Liu

papers.title: Regge bounds and eikonal scaling in a four-dimensional scalar EFT
papers.summary: Positivity bounds rest on twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which assume that the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partial\phi)^4/\Lambda^4$ and $g_6(\partial\phi)^6/\Lambda^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. The same construction is applied in the forward limit required by the dispersion relation, and we use the one- and three-loop absorptive parts below the cutoff to constrain $g_4$ and $g_6$.

authors.name: Ji Li

papers.title: Modular properties of correlators in generalised Gibbs ensembles
papers.summary: We study the modular properties of torus correlators in a generalised Gibbs ensemble (GGE) of a two-dimensional conformal field theory. For the free fermion with KdV charges, we compute the exact two-point function and derive its modular $S$-transformation as a formal power series in the chemical potential. The transformed correlator admits a factorised description: an effective charge deforms the ensemble, while a local dressing operator acts on the external fields. Both are determined by nested operator product expansions involving the deforming current. Motivated by this result, we conjecture an analogous transformation law for $n$-point functions in rational chiral conformal field theories. Using Zhu's recursion, we establish the conjecture at the lowest explicit power of the modular parameter to all orders in the chemical potential, thereby determining the dressing operator. We also verify the full conjectured transformation through cubic order in the chemical potential, retaining all explicit powers of the modular parameter. These results extend the nested-OPE description of modular transformations of GGE partition functions to local correlation functions.

authors.name: Tanmoy Sengupta

papers.title: Scalar radiation from circular orbits in D3 brane spacetimes: a Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi-like approach
papers.summary: We study scalar perturbations in a ten-dimensional D3 brane spacetime, developing a (higher-dimensional) Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi-like formalism adapted to the present case leading to a sourced modification of a Mathieu equation. As an application, we compute the energy loss both at infinity and at the horizon in terms of scalar waves due to a scalar charge moving along a circular "equatorial" geodesic.

authors.name: Donato Bini, Giorgio Di Russo, Veronica Fantini

papers.title: The Stringy Origin of Kerr Multipoles
papers.summary: We construct a new family of exact open and closed bosonic string solutions in flat spacetime that reproduce the root-Kerr and Kerr multipoles at every fixed multipole order in the large-mass and large-angular-momentum limit. These solutions provide explicit classical data for identifying associated quantum string states and testing their correspondence with rotating black holes.

authors.name: Maurizio Firrotta

papers.title: Fortuitous BMN Operators from Multiple Cores
papers.summary: We develop a systematic construction of fortuitous cohomology classes in the BMN sector of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory from multiple lower-rank building blocks. For arbitrary partitions of colour space, we construct corrected effective letters that obey the supersymmetry transformations of the corresponding lower-rank theories. These allow us to build gauge-invariant, $Q$-closed polynomial operators. A restriction map recovers the constituent cohomology classes, establishing non-exactness and fortuity without brute-force computations. As an explicit example, we combine two fortuitous $SU(2)$ cores to construct a fortuitous class in $SU(4)$. Our results provide a systematic approach to the structure of fortuitous cohomology at finite $N$.

authors.name: Robert de Mello Koch, Sarthak Duary, Minkyoo Kim, Sinong Liu

papers.title: Crossover from Schwarzian dynamics to rotational soft modes in near-extremal Lovelock black holes
papers.summary: Near-extremal black holes are controlled by a small set of soft modes, and counting these modes fixes the coefficient of $\log T$ in the entropy. We ask whether genuine six-derivative interactions change that count, working in seven-dimensional third-order Lovelock gravity, the simplest setting where the cubic Lovelock term is dynamical. The multiplicities stay the same, but the naive count fails. At fixed charge the Maxwell mode is frozen out, and the fifteen rotational modes of the $S^5$ act as a quantum rotor that only switches on above the scale $K_J^{-1}$. As a result, the coefficient of $\log T$ runs from $3/2$ at the lowest temperatures to $9$ above that scale, and never reaches the naive Gaussian value $19/2$. We compute the moment of inertia $K_J$ from the charged slow-rotation solution and find that the Lovelock couplings move the crossover without changing the multiplicities. Only large AdS black holes have a wide window in which the full rotational contribution competes with the classical entropy. Adding a probe charged scalar, we derive an analytic near-horizon Schwinger threshold in the cubic coupling. Its large-AdS limit tells us when the broad rotational crossover window can coexist with the absence of a charged-scalar Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound violation.

authors.name: Ankit Anand, Aditya Singh, Kimet Jusufi

papers.title: Interpolating between 4d $\mathcal{N}= 1$ SCFT supercurrent multiplet anomalies
papers.summary: A renormalized SCFT can be coupled to a number of background off-shell supergravity multiplets, defining different current multiplets and superconformal anomalies. We focus on the relation between the conformal and Ferrara-Zumino multiplets of generic $\mathcal{N}= 1$ SCFTs in four dimensions, defined respectively by $\mathcal{N}= 1$ conformal and old-minimal supergravity. We show that the conformal super-gravity partition function, when lifted to a functional of the old-minimal background fields through a suitable Wess-Zumino action, is related to the old-minimal partition function by a local counterterm that we determine explicitly in components. This counterterm interpolates between two different old-minimal supergravity schemes with different superconformal anomalies. Part of the counterterm depends on the old-minimal auxiliary scalar and provides the explicit component form of the super-space counterterm constructed in [1]. However, the full counterterm that interpolates between the two multiplets contains additional terms, independent of the old-minimal auxiliary scalar, which are not present in this superspace counterterm. These additional terms play a key role in the comparison of physical observables between the two multiplets.

authors.name: Pantelis Panopoulos, Ioannis Papadimitriou

papers.title: Weyl Rescalings: A First Order Approach
papers.summary: Weyl transformations, --local rescalings in which the metric transforms as $g_{\mu\nu}(x)\longrightarrow \Omega^2(x)\, g_{\mu \nu}(x)$--, are expected to be a symmetry of nature at extremely high energy, that should be (spontaneously) broken at low energy. In Cartan's first order formulation of gravity this translates into the condition that the local frames (vielbein) scale as $e^a(x) \longrightarrow \Omega(x) e^a(x)$. In this construction, the Lorentz connection one-form fields $\omega^a{}_b$ are independent from $e^a$, and since Lorentz transformations and dilatations commute, $\omega$ and $R(\omega)$ must be Weyl invariant, while in the second order metric formalism the Ricci tensor undergoes a non-homogeneous transformation. This generates a tension between the two formulations, which should be equivalent in the vanishing torsion limit. Here we show how the puzzle can be resolved taking into account the role of torsion. This also sheds some light on the conformal coupling of matter fields to gravity.

authors.name: L. Andrianopoli, J. Zanelli

papers.title: Hecke Relations from Self-Duality
papers.summary: Hecke operators can be used to relate characters of rational conformal field theories with different central charges, but it has remained a mystery how to interpret these relations physically. We offer a simple explanation in terms of self-duality under asymmetric orbifolds. Self-dual orbifolds also give more general identities beyond the familiar Harvey-Wu construction, which we illustrate through examples.

authors.name: Justin Kaidi

papers.title: Horizon exchange and the universal all-spin response of Kerr
papers.summary: The radial Teukolsky equation is invariant under exchange of the outer and inner horizons, although the physical boundary condition is not. We derive an exact monodromy relation between the corresponding Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi (MST) near-zone responses. At leading order in frequency and to all orders in spin, this relation yields, for every multipole, an expression for the leading horizon-exchange-odd response. For gravitational perturbations, it determines the exchange-odd contribution to quadrupolar absorption and organizes the exchange-even dynamical response into a digamma function whose expansion accounts for the odd- and even-zeta structures found in Kerr-Compton calculations. The exact relation, rather than the individual previously known small-spin coefficients, is the central result.

authors.name: Pierre Vanhove

papers.title: A Holographic Weyl Semimetal in an Effective Gauss--Bonnet Geometry
papers.summary: We study how an effective Gauss--Bonnet deformation of the thermal geometry changes the competition between the conducting Weyl-semimetal and insulating flavour phases of the probe D3/D7 model. The phases are represented by horizon-reaching and smoothly capped D7 embeddings, respectively, whose free energies exhibit a first-order transition. At the temperatures examined, positive Gauss--Bonnet coupling shifts coexistence toward larger flavour mass and expands the thermodynamically preferred Weyl-semimetal region, while negative coupling shifts the boundary in the opposite direction. The normalized zero-temperature transition remains unchanged. An on-shell analysis shows that the leading finite-temperature shift is largely explained by an effective rescaling of the thermal scale, opposed by an intrinsic fixed-horizon geometric contribution. The enlargement of the conducting phase does not imply stronger electrical response: the longitudinal and anomalous Hall conductivity jumps at coexistence can decrease, and the coupling response of the longitudinal jump reverses with temperature. The mass-dependent maximum of the longitudinal DC conductivity can also cease to occur on the thermodynamically preferred branch. Thus the geometric deformation changes both which phase is favored and how the Weyl-semimetal phase conducts.

authors.name: F. Mousavi, K. Bitaghsir Fadafan

papers.title: From Z to all: cyclic sum rules for thermal CFT partition functions
papers.summary: The high-temperature expansion of twisted $S^{d-1}\times S^1$ partition functions of CFT$_d$, $d = 2\kappa$, has recently been shown to obey an infinite tower of universal constraints. We determine these constraints explicitly and demonstrate that they can be packaged into a single equation involving a large conformal diffeomorphism isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_{\kappa+1}$, which cyclically permutes the thermal circle and the rotation angles. Our equation asserts that the $\mathbb{Z}_{\kappa+1}$-invariant part of $\ln Z/\beta$ is a constant fixed by the a-anomaly. Our derivation assumes CP-invariance and locality of the thermal effective action, whose structure we constrain using an algebraic formalism starting from embedding space.

authors.name: Arnav Advant, Harsh Anand, Nathan Benjamin, Abhijit Gadde, Vipul Kumar, Shiraz Minwalla, Jyotirmoy Mukherjee, Sridip Pal, Asikur Rahaman, Pabitra Ray

papers.title: An Exact QFT/Lattice Map for Fermions
papers.summary: We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions. This map rewrites a continuum Hamiltonian as a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and an infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space. The resulting lattice model reproduces exactly the energy spectrum, global operator algebra, chiral symmetries, and anomalies of the continuum QFT on any finite lattice. Unlike domain wall fermions, truncating the local Hilbert space introduces no extra massless modes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval converges as the truncation is removed. The lattice local algebras are of type I and lie between the type III continuum algebras of nested spatial regions, in accordance with the split property. We demonstrate this construction explicitly for $N$ Majorana fermions, realizing the $\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{L}\times\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{R}$ lattice chiral symmetry. We also construct an exact lattice model for the Schwinger model and numerically reproduce the mass gap $e/\sqrt{\pi}$.

authors.name: Shu-Heng Shao, Nikita Sopenko

papers.title: Boundary $c\leq1$ Liouville CFT from the Bootstrap
papers.summary: We construct boundary Liouville conformal field theory at central charge $c\leq1$ with FZZT-type boundary conditions and show that it satisfies the Cardy--Lewellen sewing constraints on the disk and the annulus. Using the analytic bootstrap we derive the so far missing boundary three-point and bulk-to-boundary structure constants and a consistent disk one-point function as explicit meromorphic functions of the Liouville momenta. In sharp contrast to $c\geq25$, the open-string spectrum between two ``timelike'' FZZT boundaries is \emph{discrete}, yet non-trivially consistent through open-closed duality with the \emph{continuous} closed-string spectrum of Ribault and Santachiara.

authors.name: Panos Betzios, Paul Ghiringhelli, Olga Papadoulaki, Ioannis Tsiares

papers.title: Dynamics of random recurrent neural networks: colored noise and sublinear activations
papers.summary: We study the dynamics of recurrent neural networks with random couplings, sublinear odd activation functions, and temporally correlated noise. Using large N methods, we determine stationary correlations and distinguish the loss of local linear stability from the onset of chaos, characterized by a positive largest Lyapunov exponent. These thresholds delimit an intermediate regime in which local instability coexists with asymptotic stability under a common noise history. Their separation depends on both the noise correlation time and the asymptotic growth of the activation function. We show that internal noise with any finite correlation time cuts off the divergence of the network's intrinsic correlation time tau_corr at the edge of chaos; it exhibits a critical scaling tau_{corr,max} propto 1/sqrt{D_0}, where D_0 is the integrated noise strength. Static random input instead produces coincident thresholds and a divergent correlation time. We also calculate the frequency-dependent participation dimension from a four-point correlation function. Its zero-frequency value is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the network correlation time, predicting a smooth minimum at the weak-noise chaos threshold. Numerical simulations support the large-network predictions and reveal appreciable finite-size effects.

authors.name: German Mato, Facundo Rigatuso, Gonzalo Torroba

papers.title: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
papers.summary: We give an explicit construction of all ALF and ALE toric gravitational instantons in terms of certain rational matrix functions of one complex variable on the Riemann sphere; these provide patching matrices for their corresponding twistor holomorphic vector bundles. The reconstruction of the instantons arises from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert splitting problem and we show how this can be solved via linear algebra, resembling but not equivalent to the Belinski--Zakharov ansatz. This construction gives a complete classification together with an explicit form for all toric gravitational instantons up to the resolutions of conical and orbifold singularities. We illustrate the formalism by computer--assisted numerical construction of two new ALF (but not AF) gravitational instantons with five nodes.

authors.name: Maciej Dunajski, Lionel Mason, Paul Tod

papers.title: Coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes I: (3,2)-Kinematical Lie algebras with $d\geq 3$
papers.summary: This is the first of several papers devoted to the classification of coisotropy-one homogeneous spacetimes. It is the first step in extending the classification of spatially isotropic homogeneous spacetimes of kinematical Lie groups to the much vaster context of homogeneous spacetimes that are not spatially isotropic; that is, where the rotations no longer act transitively on the space of directions in each tangent space. In this first paper we classify (up to isomorphisms preserving the rotational subalgebra) a class of the relevant transitive Lie algebras, the so-called (3,2)-kinematical Lie algebras, for the coisotropy-one case in spatial dimension at least 4. As a by-product of this classification, we classify two-dimensional real representations of Bianchi Lie algebras up to a suitable notion of equivalence.

authors.name: Jos\'{e} Miguel Figueroa-O'Farrill, Juan Manuel Lorenzo-Naveiro

papers.title: From MHV Gravity Amplitudes and Hodges map to Pentad Varieties
papers.summary: We study some geometric aspects behind the Hodges matrix appearing in the context of scattering amplitudes for the $\mathcal N=8$ supergravity. Through a vector bundle construction, we show that the Hodges matrix gives rise to a canonical rational map from the two-step flag variety to symmetric matrices, called the $\textit{Hodges map}$. This construction allows to define the amplitude geometrically: its vanishing locus is a divisor - the $\textit{MHV gravity divisor}$. Inspired by the Hodges map, we introduce the notion of Hadamard ratio of two varieties. In the case relevant to gravity, this is the ratio of two Grassmannians, which we call the $\textit{pentad variety}$, connecting it to the pentad constraint from algebraic statistics. Moreover, we show that the pentad variety is closely related to the combinatorial algebraic geometry of Martin's affine slope variety, and the phirotopes of Below, Krummeck, and Richter-Gebert.

authors.name: Joris Koefler, Emanuele Ventura, Hongmiao Yu

papers.title: Gauge-invariant non-universal scalar couplings in teleparallel gravity
papers.summary: We develop a gauge-invariant teleparallel framework in which the universality of the gravitational coupling is relaxed for a scalar field, while the gravitational sector retains the form of the teleparallel equivalent of General Relativity. The non-universal interaction is encoded in a scalar-sector tetrad whose coupling to the universal translational gauge potential is controlled by a field-dependent gravitational charge. A St\"uckelberg completion preserves local translational gauge invariance, and we derive the gravitational, scalar-field, and St\"uckelberg equations, together with the antisymmetric constraint and their consistency relations. As a first application, we investigate homogeneous and isotropic cosmology, where the St\"uckelberg constraint provides a first integral governing the evolution of the non-universal coupling. In the kination-dominated regime, the standard stiff-fluid behavior is recovered asymptotically, whereas in the potential-dominated regime, accelerated expansion requires additional conditions beyond potential domination. We identify compatible expanding solutions in which departures from universality are dynamically suppressed, including examples approaching power-law inflation or asymptotically de Sitter expansion. Including a universally coupled perfect fluid and a constant scalar potential, we obtain a late-time solution exhibiting a subdominant matter-like contribution to the background Friedmann equation and an asymptotic de Sitter limit. These results provide a gauge-theoretic realization of non-universal scalar couplings and highlight their potential implications for early- and late-time cosmology.

authors.name: Giovanni Otalora, Rudranil Roy

papers.title: Effective Optical Geometry and Holographic Phase Structure of a Magnetic AdS Black Hole
papers.summary: We study circular null orbits, thermodynamic topology, and the holographic thermodynamic description of a four-dimensional magnetically charged AdS black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics. The background orbit structure is classified using Duan s phi-mapping construction and compared with the extraordinary electromagnetic characteristics. The latter defines an effective optical metric with an additional radial factor that modifies the orbit condition and introduces explicit dependence on the AdS radius. For four representative configurations, the local indices of the five isolated orbits are unchanged while their radii shift by up to 5.187 %. The background mass thresholds vary smoothly across sigma = 1/4 when the total mass is used, whereas the fixed-m0 parametrization is singular there. Regularity at the center requires sigma > 1 and m0 = 0. The thermodynamic analysis separates local stability indices from equilibrium coexistence: stable Gibbs-free-energy branches cross only in model-dependent parameter intervals. The boundary canonical ensemble exhibits critical behavior consistent with mean-field exponents, and the examined grand-canonical ensemble has a Hawking-Page crossing. In the mixed ensemble, the free-energy branches have a finite endpoint discontinuity, but the sampled competing states do not satisfy the full local-stability criterion

authors.name: Mohammad Ali S. Afshar, Mohammad Reza Alipour, Saeed Noori Gashti, Jafar Sadeghi

papers.title: GUT Color-Triplet Around the Corner: The Story of an Overlooked Lightness
papers.summary: In traditional approach to the doublet-triplet splitting problem in grand unified theories (GUTs) it is assumed that color-triplet partner of the Higgs doublet must be superheavy in order not to mediate proton decay. However, it has been proposed [1] that the splitting, instead of the mass sector, can occur among the Yukawa couplings. In this scenario the color-triplet emerges as a long-lived $T$-particle with the mass around the TeV scale. This framework provides a direct low-energy window into GUT physics. In the present paper, we study an explicit supersymmetric $SO(10)$ GUT which realizes this mechanism, including effects of gravity-mediated supersymmetry breaking. We show how the shift of the heavy fields, triggered by supersymmetry-breaking, generates a tiny coupling between the $T$-particle and the Standard Model fields and explore the resulting phenomenology. Depending on the order of gravitino mass in which the coupling emerges, the lifetime of the $T$-particle is either around a second or exceeds the age of the Universe. In our analysis, we validate some earlier constraints on (super)gravity vacua imposed by the $S$-matrix: based on the Goldstino Argument, we show that none of the GUT vacua have positive energy densities, whereas the Minkowski vacua are safe against tunneling. We also highlight the role of the species scale cutoff in sensitivity of the low energy observables towards the GUT physics.

authors.name: Gia Dvali, Manuel Ettengruber, Anna Jankowsky, Tongxuan Zhang

papers.title: Bouncing and QNM convergence in Kerr
papers.summary: We show that the convergence region of the QNM representation of the retarded Green's function of the Kerr spacetime is set by complex-time bouncing singularities, as in our previous work for the Schwarzschild case. The main difference between Kerr and Schwarzschild is that there are two distinct QNM families, prolate and oblate, which have different convergence regions. We provide explicit analytical formulae for the bounce radii and corresponding convergence regions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates. We also provide an analysis of convergence in the Reissner-Nordstr\"om spacetime.

authors.name: Paolo Arnaudo, Benjamin Withers

papers.title: Electrically charged black holes with electroweak hair
papers.summary: We construct electrically charged black holes in Einstein's gravity coupled to the bosonic sector of the electroweak theory, focusing on static, spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat solutions, with the weak mixing angle fixed to its Standard Model value. Horizon regularity imposes a resonance condition relating the charged-vector frequency to the electromagnetic potential at the horizon, corresponding to the threshold of charged superradiance. A perturbative analysis further shows that nonextremal Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes do not support regular, exponentially localized, spherically symmetric electroweak clouds satisfying such condition. Thus, the hairy solutions cannot emerge via a bifurcation from this electrovacuum family. Moreover, our numerical investigation reveals two apparently disconnected families of bosonic stars. Within the explored parameter space, the hairy black holes are connected to the strongly gravitating one.

authors.name: Etevaldo dos Santos Costa Filho

papers.title: Confining strings in the reconfined phase of trace deformed three dimensional $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills theory
papers.summary: Adding a trace deformation to the Yang-Mills action keeps the theory confining above the standard deconfinement temperature, in the so-called reconfined phase. We study the confining flux tube of the trace-deformed $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ theory in three dimensions with lattice simulations of Polyakov loop correlators. As the deformation increases, the ground state energy departs from the usual Nambu-Got\=o effective string description, and deep in the reconfined phase the data are accurately described by the Polchinski-Yang rigid string, an effective string dominated by an extrinsic-curvature term.

authors.name: Claudio Bonati, Michele Caselle, Alessio Negro, Dario Panfalone, Lorenzo Verzichelli

papers.title: Quasi-Normal Modes of Covariant Loop Quantum Black Holes
papers.summary: We investigate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) and time-domain response of a massless, minimally coupled test scalar field on static, spherically symmetric covariant loop quantum black hole (cLQBH) backgrounds. Focusing on a phenomenological, Gaussian-localized holonomy profile, we obtain a localized deformation of the scalar effective potential containing both positive and negative parts. This provides a geometric realization of the bump effect, with the potential deformation and tortoise-coordinate mapping determined consistently by the same background. We characterize the deformation by its location, amplitude, and width, and study its effects using frequency-domain shooting and time-domain evolution, supplemented by matrix-pencil mode extraction and waveform reconstruction. The QNM spectrum exhibits spiral trajectories as the bump location varies, enhanced sensitivity of the overtones, and mode overtaking, whereby the branch continued from the first Schwarzschild overtone becomes longer-lived than the continued fundamental branch. Despite substantial spectral changes, the early response can remain close to its Schwarzschild counterpart, with more pronounced differences emerging later. To quantify this behavior, we introduce a local waveform-deviation time and compare it with a relative-amplitude faintness time, thereby defining an operational observation window. The deviation time depends nonmonotonically on the bump location, and suitable parameter choices allow appreciable departures to emerge before the adopted faintness threshold is reached. These results connect localized holonomy corrections with spectral sensitivity and waveform evolution, providing a basis for future gravitational-perturbation studies and assessments of gravitational-wave detectability.

authors.name: Chao Zhang, Sushant G. Ghosh, Anzhong Wang

papers.title: Binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
papers.summary: We study fully non-linear binary black hole mergers in massive Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity with a linear Gauss-Bonnet coupling function. In the absence of a well-developed initial data solver for EsGB gravity, we demonstrate that the conventional workaround solution for massless scalar fields results in confined junk radiation that contaminates late-time dynamics in the massive theory. We propose a solution to this problem by suitably modifying the equations of motion at the early stages of the simulation to tame such junk radiation, thereby allowing us to study the dynamics of the scalar field during the process of a black hole merger. This is followed by a preliminary analysis of the frequency content in the ringdown of the scalar and tensor modes. In particular, the quadrupole scalar mode exhibits a rich ringdown structure: while it is dominated by the spin-2 ``contamination'' frequency in the early stages, its late time morphology becomes primarily determined by the scalar mass frequency.

authors.name: Harry L. H. Shum, Llibert Arest\'e Sal\'o, Miguel Bezares, Thomas P. Sotiriou

papers.title: Comment on "Long-range magnetic fields in the ground state of the Standard Model plasma"
papers.summary: We revisit the two-loop parity-odd photon polarization analyzed by Boyarsky, Ruchayskiy, and Shaposhnikov [Phys. Rev. Lett. 109, 111602 (2012)]. The original calculation neglected opposite- fermion-flow partner diagrams for the tadpole and exchange-bubble topologies alike. We quantify the impact of the properly restored exchange-bubble coefficients on the static magnetic response.

authors.name: Jingwei Wang, Yiming Liu, Ligong Bian

papers.title: Vertex-resummed kinetic theory of dipole-symmetric bosons from 2PI effective action
papers.summary: The formalism of non-equilibrium dynamics for the dipole-symmetric $U(N)$ model involving $N$-component charged scalar fields is studied on the Schwinger-Keldysh contour by a systematic $1/N$ expansion of two-particle-irreducible (2PI) effective action to the next-to-leading order (NLO). The differential equations describing non-equilibrium evolution equations of two-point functions and field expectation values related to the symmetry breaking in the dynamics are derived, which encompass scatterings between modes essential in the late-time evolution and thermalization beyond the scope of the mean field. At the late-time regime of the evolution, the leading-order (LO) gradient expansion is performed to construct the vertex-resummed kinetic theory by encoding non-perturbative effects in the vertex through the resummation, which is distinct from the standard kinetic theory written by the weak-coupling expansion.

authors.name: Chun-Wei Su

papers.title: Motional Decoherence of the internal state of an atom by vacuum and thermal fluctuations of a quantum field: Necessity of a fully relativistic treatment
papers.summary: We consider a massive object, such as a neutral atom or an Unruh-DeWitt detector, moving at constant speed in a quantum field and investigate how motion affects the quantum coherence of its internal degrees of freedom, manifesting as quantum dispersion in the absence of a quantum field, and decoherence in its presence. Our investigation aims to serve two purposes: One is to obtain the correct results for these effects, which are essential for the design of quantum information processing schemes where the quantum coherence of an atom's internal degrees of freedom is of major concern. The other is to expose the fallacies in commonplace approaches, which start with a non-relativistic calculation and then add on relativistic ``corrections". We first show a fully relativistic calculation of the internal dynamics based on covariance principles, and then one which ignores these principles, often justified by the atom's slow motion. By a direct comparison of results from these two approaches, we identify {significant discrepancies} in a non-relativistic treatment, even at low atomic speeds. The proper procedure, and a much safer one in terms of accuracy, is recommended here: first derive the dynamics and the necessary regularizations within a fully covariant relativistic framework. Only after the exact, internally consistent equations of motion are established should low-velocity limits be extracted from them. Only in this way can all the relativistic effects which matter: time dilation, aberration, non-inertial mass shifts, be systematically preserved, and accurate results obtained.

authors.name: Jen-Tsung Hsiang, Bei-Lok Hu

papers.title: Late-time echoes from planar wave-packet scattering by an ultracompact star
papers.summary: We simulate the propagation and scattering of an incident plane scalar wave in the spacetime of an ultracompact, horizonless constant-density star using a time-domain multipole mode-sum method. By reconstructing the coherently superposed time-domain waveforms, we compare the star's dynamical response with that of a Schwarzschild black hole. We find that the early-time response closely mimics a black-hole ringdown due to wave scattering near the exterior unstable photon sphere. Conversely, the late-time signal develops a sequence of delayed echoes originating from wave trapping near the interior stable light ring and subsequent leakage through the exterior potential barrier. While individual multipoles exhibit regular echoes, their coherent superposition induces interference, producing complex waveforms with irregular profiles that nonetheless retain an underlying temporal organization with alternating peak separations. Finally, as a proof of concept, we perform a signal-to-noise ratio analysis using an assumed strain normalization, demonstrating that these weak, late-time signatures can be resolved by third-generation gravitational-wave detectors.

authors.name: Shanshan Deng, Jian-hua He

papers.title: An Excursion into Grassmannian Spectra
papers.summary: We revisit the classical spectral problem for the Laplace-Beltrami and Laplace-Bochner operators on complex Grassmannians. After reviewing the standard approach based on non-commutative harmonic analysis, we develop two complementary methods originating from the quantization of the corresponding one-dimensional sigma model, both with and without a magnetic monopole field. The first is based on $\mathbf{SU}(n)$-equivariant first-order GLSM formulation and gives explicit eigenfunctions in terms of projectors and Pl\"ucker coordinates. The second uses a spin-chain realization of free particles on manifolds and describes the space of square-integrable functions, or sections in the magnetic case, through limiting tensor products of long rectangular $\mathbf{SU}(n)$ representations. Together, these approaches provide a more explicit picture of the spectral geometry of Grassmannians and clarify the relation between harmonics, Young diagrams, magnetic bundles, and Laplacian spectra.

authors.name: Dmitri Bykov, Viacheslav Krivorol

papers.title: Closed- and open-system characterization of the Yukawa-SYK model in real time
papers.summary: Strongly correlated matter without quasiparticles is central to many-body physics, quantum chaos, and quantum gravity, motivating a considerable effort toward its realization in tabletop experiments. Two challenges remain: laboratory platforms are open systems, so conformal behavior must survive dissipation, and it must be identified through measurable quantities. We address both challenges in the Yukawa-Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (YSYK) model, in which bosons and fermions interact as in, e.g., light-matter systems, but through random all-to-all couplings that drive the boson to criticality without fine tuning. Solving the model in real time using the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we treat closed and open systems within a unified framework and, in both cases, consider a thermal steady state to map their phase diagrams. In addition to the known conformal and impurity (or SYK$_2$) regimes, we identify novel high-temperature regimes in which the fermions are driven by an essentially bare boson and show that their dynamics is captured by a quadratic model with time-dependent random hopping. Across all regimes, the fermionic softening of the boson is bounded by a ``criticality budget'' determined only by the Yukawa coupling and the temperature. Coupling the boson with a thermal environment induces a mass shift that deforms the boundaries between different regimes and exhausts the criticality budget, thus imposing a bound on temperature and dissipation rate compatible with self-tuned criticality. We further introduce a set of markers built from the two-point functions that separate all identified regimes, are accessible in linear response, and require no fit of the conformal exponents. We complement them with the quantum Fisher information, deriving upper bounds with and without dissipation. These results may help characterize holographic quantum matter beyond the closed setting.

authors.name: Alex Windey, Christian H. Johansen, Philipp Hauke, Andrea Legramandi

papers.title: dSIBP: a package for generating IBP seeds for QFT in de Sitter spacetime
papers.summary: Recent studies show that in addition to the flat spacetime, Integration-by-parts (IBP) relations and differential equations can also provide a systematic approach to Feynman integrals in de Sitter spacetime. dSIBP is a Mathematica package for the automated construction of IBP systems and differential equations. For dS integral families with massive and massless propagators, it generates a complete set of IBP seeds, assembles linear systems for external reduction, and constructs differential equations for the reduced master integrals. The implementation combines equations of motion, remaining terms and parity constraints, and provides reliable checks. We describe the conventions and public interface through worked examples.

authors.name: Jiaqi Chen, Yi-Xiao Tao

papers.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
papers.summary: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.

authors.name: Deyou Chen, Chuang Yang

papers.title: On Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers
papers.summary: We prove Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers for each $m \geq 3$ on the normalized logarithms of Euler characteristics of moduli spaces. Also, we state a log-concavity conjecture on Euler characteristics near slope one for the 3-Kronecker quiver.

authors.name: So Okada

papers.title: Mixed-Order Parity-Violating Corrections to Rotating Black Holes in Combined Scalar Gauss-Bonnet and Dynamical Chern-Simons Gravity
papers.summary: We construct the leading mixed-order $\mathcal{O}(\zeta_{\rm GB}\zeta_{\rm CS})$ deformation of rotating black holes in a combined scalar Gauss-Bonnet and dynamical Chern-Simons effective theory, the sector in which the parity-even and parity-odd corrections act simultaneously. Using a pseudospectral solution of the coupled mixed scalar and metric equations, we compute horizon and equatorial-geodesic observables--the horizon angular velocity, surface gravity, area, and Wald entropy; the innermost stable circular orbit and photon-ring radii; and photon-ring eikonal estimates of the ringdown--at fixed mass and angular momentum over the spin range $0.1\le a\le0.9$, where the solution is numerically convergent and the perturbative expansion is controlled for sufficiently small dimensionless couplings. We verify the exact Kerr and Schwarzschild limits, reproduce available pure-sector benchmarks, and quantify spectral, residual, and extraction uncertainties. The mixed solution satisfies every component of the field equations, including the one that is not imposed in its construction, and its Wald entropy satisfies the first law to about one part in $10^{5}$. The mixed coefficients exhibit spin dependence qualitatively distinct from the individual sectors within this EFT truncation. All four horizon quantities, and several orbital and eikonal ones, change sign as functions of spin. The ringdown results are leading photon-ring eikonal estimates; a full coupled finite-$\ell$ perturbation calculation is left to future work.

authors.name: Abhishek Rout, Brett Altschul

papers.title: Probing the Spatial Coherence of Chiral-Imbalance Fluctuations with Hyperon Spin Correlations
papers.summary: Topological fluctuations in the quark-gluon plasma can generate local chiral imbalances whose spatial coherence remains difficult to access with conventional charge-separation measurements. We propose differential hyperon-pair spin correlations as a probe of both the strength and spatial organization of these fluctuations. Fluctuations of the axial chemical potential $\mu_5$ can induce pair correlations even when the mean helicity polarization vanishes. Using the AMPT model, we find that the magnitude of the hyperon spin correlation probes the magnitude and spatial coherence scale of $\mu_5$, while the ratio of short- and long-range correlations varies strongly with the spatial coherence scale, but only weakly with $\mu_{5}$ over the range of explored parameters. These observables provide an experimentally testable strategy for constraining the spatial structure of chiral-imbalance fluctuations.

authors.name: Guangyu Zheng, Zilin Yuan, Mei Huang, Guannan Xie

papers.title: The integer spectrum of a superintegrable quantum field theory
papers.summary: In our previous article CMP 407 (2026) 131, we explored the rich algebraic structures arising from a specific quantum many-body Hamiltonian quartic in the bosonic creation-annihilation operators. This Hamiltonian originated from the works of G\'erard and Grellier on classical turbulent energy transfer in a Lax-integrable setting, and its quantum version respects hierarchies of polynomial conservation laws all of which possess purely integer spectra, as does the Hamiltonian itself. The latter feature, known from numerical studies, has previously remained unproved. Here, we present an elementary solution of the quantum G\'erard-Grellier Hamiltonian. The eigenstates are labelled by partitions and the corresponding eigenvalues admit simple explicit expressions in terms of the principal hook lengths. The key ingredient in this construction is a specific basis we introduce, inspired by the classical multisoliton coherent states, in which the Hamiltonian is upper-triangular. The expressions for the eigenvalues then immediately follow, while the full eigenbasis can be recovered via a Gram-Schmidt procedure.

authors.name: Marine De Clerck, Oleg Evnin

papers.title: Gravitational-wave lensing beyond the diffraction integral: proper-time methods and the bound lens
papers.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) can have wavelengths comparable to the Schwarzschild radius of their lenses, and detectors record their phase, so lensing requires wave optics. Its standard tool, the diffraction integral, follows from the particle path integral of a scalar wave on a static weak field, under the eikonal (one-way) and paraxial approximations, plus the thin-lens limit. We give a self-contained account of how the proper-time (worldline) representation overcomes these steps. An auxiliary proper time makes the wave equation exactly first order, with frequency as $1/\hbar$, so geometric optics and, for paraxial thin-lens paths, the diffraction integral follow from stationarity of an exact integral. For a point mass, the Duru-Kleinert (DK) gauge and Kustaanheimo-Stiefel map give the exact propagator; for a distant observer the DK time and fibre angle become the radius and azimuth of a lens plane, the result is the point-lens amplification factor with the offset set by the excess path, and geometric optics requires $w\gg1$ and $wy\gg1$. This agreement reflects the Coulomb potential, not the approximations: the exact eikonal condition, $\varepsilon_E\simeq\bar\lambda/d+GM/c^2d+\mathcal O(\sin^2\theta/2)$, fails near the lens and at large angles, and the one-way step is a non-relativistic limit. We then treat the bound lens, a GW source orbiting its lens, which emits a backscattered echo and moves during the lensing delays. Its exact time-domain signal gives each worldline its own retarded time and Doppler factor, so no single amplification factor describes it. In the diffraction regime the Shapiro phase alone misses all lensing beyond it, geometric optics misses 46-100% of it near conjunction at $w=0.3$, the paraxial geometry fails on the far side, and the static amplification factor along the orbit errs by $\approx(1-2)\,wM/R$ near conjunction and by the echo amplitude elsewhere.

authors.name: Ginevra Braga, Raul Jimenez

papers.title: Cosmological evolution and late-time attractors in axion-monopole interacting dark energy
papers.summary: We investigate the cosmological dynamics of axion-monopole interacting dark energy, examining whether a microscopically motivated dark-sector interaction can sustain stable late-time acceleration. In particular, magnetic monopoles constitute dark matter and an ultralight axion contributes to dark energy, with their interaction arising from the Witten effect through field-dependent dyon masses. We formulate the autonomous system, classify its critical points and stability, and investigate the evolution analytically and numerically. We find that stable de Sitter attractors at finite positive Hubble parameter require a positive cosmological constant and correspond to axion-potential minima, whereas those at maxima are unstable. Nevertheless, transient axion-driven acceleration remains possible without an explicit cosmological constant. Furthermore, the interaction induces matter-era tracking, namely an attracting slow-drift regime rather than an exact critical point. The interaction-effective dark-energy equation of state can cross the phantom divide, although the physical equation of state remains non-phantom. Extending the analysis to the full Bogomol'nyi-Prasad-Sommerfield dyon mass, we find that the main dynamical features persist, while the field evolution and interaction strength depend on the microscopic dyon properties. Our results demonstrate how a microscopically motivated dark-sector interaction can give rise to distinctive cosmological evolution and effective dark-energy behavior.

authors.name: Emmanuel N. Saridakis

papers.title: Two examples in amplituhedron tilings
papers.summary: We give an example of a tiling of the $m=4$ amplituhedron that has fewer cells than that of the magic number conjecture. The tiling uses an injective degree two cell.

authors.name: Evgeniya Akhmedova, Thomas Lam, Calvin Yost-Wolff

papers.title: Crossover duality for the quantum long-range Ising chain: perturbation theory around the short-range endpoint and a DMRG test
papers.summary: We propose a weakly coupled description of the long-range transverse-field Ising chain near its short-range crossover at $s_*=7/4$, where the couplings decay as $r^{-1-s}$. The Ising conformal field theory is coupled to an instantaneous Gaussian field through $\sigma\chi$, extending the classical long-range Ising duality to quantum chains. The equal-time interaction generates a stress-tensor deformation that causes the velocity to run and renormalizes the dynamical critical exponent $z$. Conformal perturbation theory gives $z=1-0.720\,\delta+O(\delta^2)$, $1/\nu=(1+z)/2+O(\delta^2)$, and $\omega=\delta+O(\delta^2)$, with $\delta=s_*-s$. DMRG calculations on periodic chains of up to $128$ sites provide a consistency test using theoretical inputs for $1/\nu$ and $\omega$. After accounting for slow finite-size corrections, static and dynamical estimates of $z$ agree, supporting the crossover expansion at $s=1.5$ and a two-sided Pad\'e interpolation at $s=1$, $1.25$, and $1.5$.

authors.name: Junchen Rong

papers.title: Deconfinement Confined to the Heaviest Neutron Stars: Strange Quark Matter from a Flavor-Dressed Contact Interaction
papers.summary: We study cold, electrically neutral, beta-equilibrated quark matter with u, d, and s quarks described by a symmetry-preserving contact interaction whose parameters are fixed in vacuum. The vector repulsion is varied as a fraction 0 < eta < 3/2 of the scalar coupling, and results are given with and without the flavor dressing of the effective coupling. Pure quark matter is not self-bound in this model, and no value of eta produces a star that reaches two solar masses while satisfying the tidal constraint from GW170817; the heaviest configurations owe their mass to an envelope of constituent quarks. We then construct hybrid stars with a relativistic mean-field hadronic phase fitted to GM1 saturation properties, using both Maxwell and Gibbs constructions and a deconfinement bag shift. Tying deconfinement to chiral restoration and requiring a continuous pressure yields an upper bound on this shift. Within that bound, quark matter appears inside stable stars only for eta < 1/2, never below about 4 n0, and only in stars between 2.2 and 2.35Msun, over a stable mass window of at most 0.02Msun. The vector strength that pure quark stars need to become massive prevents deconfinement in hybrid stars. Radii and tidal deformabilities of intermediate-mass stars are therefore set by the hadronic EoS alone; with the softer SLy4 EoS the transition moves to the maximum-mass configuration itself.

authors.name: Aftab Ahmad, Noreen Akhter, Alfredo Raya

papers.title: Analytic approaches to anisotropic holographic superfluids in asymptotically hyperscaling violation geometry
papers.summary: We explore anisotropic holographic superfluidity and find analytic solutions near critical point where superfluid/normalfluid phase transition appears in a holographic dual fluid system. In arXiv:hep-th/1109.4592, the authors obtained such an analytic solution in 5-dimensional Einstein-SU(2)Yang-Mills system, and it is asymptotically AdS$_5$. What is more in this note is that we get analytic solutions near the critical point in 3- and 4- dimensional Einstein-Scalar-U(1)$\times$SU(2)Yang-Mills systems, which become asymptotically hyperscaling violation geometry. We also get leading order back reactions to the background geometry, which clearly shows spatial anisotropy of the bulk geometry. To explore the properties of the spacetime, we compute holographic entanglement entropy and confirm that the superfluid/normalfluid phase transition must occur at the critical point.

authors.name: Gitae Kim, Yeong Seok Choi, Jae-Hyuk Oh

papers.title: Bootstrapping transport in the Drude-Kadanoff-Martin model
papers.summary: The Drude-Kadanoff-Martin model is a simple low energy and long wavelength description of charge transport, parameterised by the current relaxation timescale $\tau$, charge diffusivity $D$ and charge compressibility $\chi$. We obtain sharp constraints on these parameters in terms of the microscopic energy and length scales of any underlying lattice model with local and bounded interactions. Our primary tools are upper bounds on the retarded Green's function for the charge density in such a setting. We first note that the Drude-Kadanoff-Martin model cannot pertain at microscopic energy scales because it is inconsistent with the exponential suppression of spectral weight at the highest frequencies in a lattice model. Secondly, under the assumption that the low energy dynamics is captured by the model, we obtain a lower bound on the collective mean free path $\ell \equiv \sqrt{\tau D}$. This bound is shown to imply a version of the Mott-Ioffe-Regel bound: systems with $\ell$ much shorter than the lattice length scale cannot have conventional Drude peaks, in the sense of being captured by the DKM model.

authors.name: Subham Dutta Chowdhury, Sean A. Hartnoll, Aditya Hebbar, Ruby Khondaker

papers.title: Building far-from-equilibrium effective field theories using shift symmetries
papers.summary: Contemporary understanding of thermalization in quantum field theory stems largely from understanding properties of transient excitations of equilibria. These nonhydrodynamic excitations are known to structurally differ between weakly- and strongly-coupled quantum field theories with no known results at intermediate values of the interaction strength. We demonstrate that all the known behaviors of transient excitations can be understood as a consequence of different realizations of a symmetry principle, the shift symmetry, applied at the level of the far from equilibrium generalization of the hydrodynamic effective action that we explicitly construct. Our approach naturally includes the effects of stochastic fluctuations outside the hydrodynamic regime and allows to explicitly construct hybrid models interpolating between weak- and strong-coupling behavior. We study properties of one such model motivated by thermalization in nuclear collisions in light of the QCD running coupling.

authors.name: Xin An, Robbe Brants, Michal P. Heller, Yi Yin

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of the proton in the improved holographic QCD model
papers.summary: We compute the gluonic contribution to the gravitational form factors of the proton using the improved holographic QCD model, in which the proton is described in terms of bulk Dirac fermions. Model parameters are constrained using lattice and phenomenological input, allowing us to obtain estimates for the gravitational form factors and to compare them with results from other approaches. Using the extracted form factors, we analyze mechanical properties of the proton, including pressure and shear distributions. We obtain estimates for the mechanical and mass radii of the proton, $\rho_{\text{mech}} \approx 0.63$ fm, $\rho_{\text{mass}} \approx 0.65$ fm, and compare these values with radius estimates from other nonperturbative studies.

authors.name: Antti Hippel\"ainen, Niko Jokela, Matti J\"arvinen

papers.title: Lightcone Bootstrap for Multipoint Defect Correlators
papers.summary: We initiate the lightcone bootstrap analysis of multipoint correlators in a defect conformal field theory. The setup we consider is the three-point function of two bulk and one defect operator. Requiring consistency of the crossing equation in the lightcone limit, we find constraints on the defect spectrum at large transverse spin. Specifically, to reproduce the exchange of the leading-twist operator in the bulk channel we find two twist-accumulating families of defect operators at large transverse spin and we compute their defect CFT data in this limit.

authors.name: Lorenzo Bianchi, Andrea Mattiello, Lorenzo Quintavalle

papers.title: Oscillons from $Q$-balls in generalized models
papers.summary: We study the oscillon/$Q$-ball relation in an extended model with non-canonical kinematics. The model contains a single real scalar field whose kinetic term is enlarged to include a generalizing function. We approximate the real sector up to the third order in a book-keeping parameter. In this context, we implement the Renormalization Group Perturbation Expansion (RGPE), from which we conclude that the relation between oscillons and underlying $Q$-balls holds even in the presence of nontrivial kinematics. We apply our results to the study of three different effective cases. In all of them, our expressions mimic the numerical evolution of nonstandard oscillons with great accuracy, especially for small and moderate amplitudes. As the initial amplitude increases, the numerical profile develops a modulated behavior, and we use a two $Q$-balls solution to seed our analytical oscillon. We discuss how our non-canonical construction allows the existence of a well-behaved oscillon in connection to the simplest $\phi^2$-potential. This novel profile behaves in the same general way as the previous ones. So, we argue that they belong to the same universality class. Finally, we extend our analysis to consider those contributions up to the fifth order in the approximation expansion. We explore an exotic $\phi^6$-scenario, and conclude that the relation between generalized oscillons and underlying $Q$-balls now belongs to a different universality class.

authors.name: E. da Hora, Fabiano C. Simas

papers.title: Symmetries and Conservation Laws in Lie-Poisson Electrodynamics
papers.summary: Lie-Poisson electrodynamics (LPE) is a non-Abelian and nonlinear deformation of usual electrodynamics, where the gauge algebra is defined through a Lie-algebra-type Poisson bracket on space-time. This field-theoretical model arises from noncommutative U(1) gauge theory in the semiclassical limit. We focus on the geometric approach to LPE in the absence of charged matter. We establish a non-trivial field redefinition which, under mild technical assumptions, maps the LPE dynamics to that of Maxwell theory. We emphasise that despite the dynamical equivalence, these two theories are not physically equivalent, since the corresponding local gauge-invariant observables are different. We show that our field redefinition is actually a Seiberg-Witten map between LPE and Maxwell theory. Using this map, for any symmetry of the Maxwell action, we construct generators of LPE symmetries and the corresponding conserved currents. In particular, we obtain deformed Poincar\'e transformations, thereby solving the problem of constructing space-time symmetries in LPE. The deformed symmetries are constructed as active transformations of the gauge field. In the outlook, we propose a natural quantization prescription for LPE based on our field redefinition.

authors.name: M. A. Kurkov

papers.title: Circuit and Krylov complexity of primordial perturbations of modified gravity in inflation
papers.summary: Taking canonical scalar field inflation as the reference case, we investigate the circuit and Krylov complexities of primordial curvature perturbations in an \(f(\phi,R)\) modified gravity inflation. We derive the evolution equations for the squeezed strength \(r_k\) and squeezed angle \(\varphi_k\), and calculate the circuit complexity, Krylov complexity, Krylov entropy, Lanczos coefficients, and effective dissipative contribution. Compared with the canonical model, the squeezed strength \(r_k\) grows more slowly in the modified gravity inflation and continues to exhibit oscillations after horizon exit. Consequently, the spreading in Krylov space is suppressed and modulated through the relation \(K=\sinh^2 r_k\). Modified gravity also changes the squeezed angle, thereby modifying the phase-space correlations and enhancing the oscillatory behavior of the circuit complexity. In the presence of modified gravity effects, information loss is suppressed before horizon exit, whereas it barely affects information loss after horizon exit. For the parameters considered, the Lyapunov exponent and Lanczos coefficients indicate that modified gravity has little effect on the effective degree of quantum chaoticity. These results show that \(f(\phi,R)\) modified gravity primarily reorganizes the amplitude, phase, complexity, and information loss dynamics of primordial quantum fluctuations.

authors.name: Tao Li, Hai-Bing Fu

papers.title: Freezing Swampland: A Krylov Complexity Diagnostic for the Weak Gravity Conjecture
papers.summary: We propose a quantum-information-theoretic perspective on the Weak Gravity Conjecture through the behavior of Krylov spread complexity. For a charged thermofield double state holographically dual to an AdS Reissner--Nordstr\"om black hole, we show that the extremal limit on the black-hole side is accompanied by an effective freezing of Krylov spreading. In this regime, the return amplitude becomes effectively a pure phase, and the corresponding Krylov spread is suppressed. We then incorporate charged matter and study the effect of Schwinger pair production in the near-horizon region. Within this semiclassical near-extremal analysis, the frozen behavior is lifted once an allowed discharge channel is opened, and the dynamics become nontrivial again. This suggests a possible complexity-based diagnostic of a characteristic physical consequence of the Weak Gravity Conjecture: the availability of a superextremal charged state that can mediate discharge. More broadly, our results point to a connection between the swampland program, black-hole physics, and quantum information theory.

authors.name: Amin Faraji Astaneh, Reza Ghomi Shurkaie

papers.title: Local subtractions and renormalization-group monotonicity: exact defect and sphere flows
papers.summary: We ask when local subtractions of the sphere free energy yield a function that decreases monotonically along a renormalization-group flow. The subtractions are polynomials in $D=R d/dR$ that remove the local counterterms and leave fixed-point values unchanged, in a fixed renormalization prescription. We prove that if the subtracted free energy $C$ approaches its infrared value from below, with ordered endpoints and a power-law approach to both fixed points, no such subtraction is monotone, and that further factors with real zeros cannot remove a nonmonotonicity already present. For a three-dimensional flow to a gapped phase, $C-C_{\rm IR}=4\pi^2(M_2-3M_0)/R+\dots$, where $M_0$ and $M_2$ are spectral moments of the flat-space stress-tensor two-point function, so every subtraction fails when $M_2<3M_0$, as for a free conformally coupled massive scalar. In two dimensions the leading term is always negative, so no unitary flow to a gapped phase whose subtracted free energy starts at $c_{\rm UV}/3$ admits a monotone subtraction; the massive Dirac fermion on $S^2$ is an exact example. In the conformally coupled massive $O(N)$ model, $M_2-3M_0$ is negative at leading order in $N$ for every finite nonnegative quartic coupling. At criticality it vanishes at that order and its first correction is negative. At weak positive coupling it is negative for every curvature coupling and every finite $N$. For the Gross--Neveu flow from an interacting fixed point, it is negative already at leading order. In contrast, we prove monotonicity for Robin boundary flows on every sphere $S^p$ with $p\ge2$ and for massive Dirac fields on every odd sphere $S^d$ with $d\ge3$. For two solvable double-trace families we find exact thresholds: a monotone subtraction exists if and only if $\widehat\Delta\ge1/2$ on a spherical surface defect, and $\Delta\ge(3-\sqrt{37/13})/2$ on $S^3$ at leading large $N$.

authors.name: Francesco Scardino

papers.title: Matter Swapping between Two Branes: A Local Type IIB D3--D7--D3 Mechanism for Charged-Fermion Mixing via E3 Instantons
papers.summary: Effective infrared two-sheeted descriptions of fermion mixing between braneworlds have emerged in several distinct realizations and lead to testable matter-swapping effects, motivating low-energy searches and cosmological applications. The recurrence of the same low-energy fermion operator motivates investigating whether this structure can also arise from a D-brane mechanism. We investigate a local Type IIB D3$_+$--D7--D3$_-$/E3 mechanism for generating perturbatively forbidden interbrane mixing. Under explicitly stated microscopic conditions, the E3 instanton generates fermion mixing with both scalar and pseudoscalar components. The pseudoscalar component reproduces the characteristic mixing structure of the two-sheeted fermion operator, while D7 Wilson transport supplies the gauge-invariant relative connection between the two brane sectors. We establish the corresponding gauge matching for transitions between stationary states at resonance. The analysis also provides a model-building roadmap toward a compact phenomenological realization. Such a realization requires electromagnetic sequestering of the two fermion sectors and a sufficiently light non-uniform D7 gauge mode capable of mediating a long-range relative interaction. In such a compactification, the mixing parameter $g$ would be determined by microscopic instanton data and matter-field normalization, providing a connection to low-energy constraints.

authors.name: Micha\"el Sarrazin

papers.title: Deterministic Hypergraph SYK: Melonic Dominance and Maximal Chaos Without Disorder Averaging
papers.summary: We show that the leading melonic structure of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model can be realized by a single sparse Majorana Hamiltonian, without disorder averaging. In our deterministic hypergraph SYK model (hSYK), $N$ Majorana fermions interact through $O(dN)$ terms with uniform couplings, arranged on a fixed $q$-uniform, $d$-regular hypergraph. If the hypergraph is linear, has few short cycles, and is a spectral expander, then at large $d$ the two-point function obeys the melonic Schwinger-Dyson equation site by site. The leading thermodynamics are therefore those of SYK, and at leading order in $1/d$ every bilocal fluctuation other than the Schwarzian is gapped. The four-point ladder splits into scrambling modes labeled by eigenvalues of the site adjacency operator. At strong coupling, the uniform mode is maximally chaotic, and a non-uniform mode grows only if its eigenvalue exceeds $1/(q-1)$. Exact diagonalization of single instances with $N\le24$ agrees with the melonic two-point function and thermodynamics more closely than dense SYK of the same size, shows Wigner-Dyson level statistics, and reproduces the predicted mode structure of out-of-time-order correlators. Numerically, random linear hypergraphs typically satisfy these conditions, and for $d>q$ also avoid emergent symmetries. The model is a natural candidate for quantum simulation.

authors.name: Shiroman Prakash

papers.title: On the quantum statistical relation and the covariant phase space Hamiltonian
papers.summary: We show how the covariant phase space Hamiltonian can be constructed in theories in which some of the fields have gauge freedoms. The addition to the action of boundary terms that guarantee the well-posedness of a variational principle and its exact gauge invariance for the prescribed boundary conditions turn out to be essential in this construction. The same ingredients are essential in the use of the action in the framework of Gibbons and Hawking's Euclidean approach to Quantum Gravity and we show how the on-shell action constructed with a Lagrangian with those properties can be expressed in terms of the covariant phase space Hamiltonian. We compute the Hamiltonian of several theories, one of which has Chern--Simons terms, using our prescription and show that, in black-hole backgrounds, the Hamiltonian gives directly the quantum statistical relation including terms related to non-gravitational charges and chemical potentials, as expected.

authors.name: Jos\'e Luis V. Cerdeira, Tom\'as Ort\'in

papers.title: New analytic Janus and $S^4$ solutions for $\mathcal{N}=2^*$
papers.summary: We construct a three-parameter family of regular analytic supergravity solutions which are dual to (a) the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ gauge theory on the four-sphere, and (b) $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$-invariant Janus interfaces in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM with or without the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ mass turned on. To this end we employ a five-dimensional supergravity model coupled to six scalars which arises as a certain consistent truncation of type IIB supergravity on $S^5$. The curved domain wall solutions feature a hidden integral of motion which allows for their analytic treatment. We relate the three parameters of the solution to field theory sources and vevs and show how regularity of the solutions restricts their range. We briefly discuss the holographic evaluation of the one-point function of the field theory Lagrangian for our family of Janus solutions.

authors.name: Fridrik Freyr Gautason

papers.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
papers.summary: We present a Wilsonian framework, globally controlled across the holonomy space, for determining the perturbative data governing the vacua of chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on a circle. This allows lifting the Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua in 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ Chern--Simons-matter theories to $\RR^3\times S^1$. The framework is showcased by finding a rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple $\U(1)$ model and by reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction (first diagnosed on $S^3\times S^1$) of an $\SU(2)$ Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory.

authors.name: Arash Arabi Ardehali

papers.title: Drinfeld J Presentation of Twisted Yangians
papers.summary: We present a quantization of a Lie coideal structure for twisted half-loop algebras of finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebras. We obtain algebra closure relations of twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for all symmetric pairs of simple Lie algebras and for simple twisted even half-loop Lie algebras. We provide the explicit form of the closure relations for twisted Yangians in Drinfeld J presentation for the ${\mathfrak{sl}}_3$ Lie algebra.

authors.name: Samuel Belliard, Vidas Regelskis

papers.title: Highest weight vectors, shifted topological recursion and quantum curves
papers.summary: We extend the theory of topological recursion by considering Airy structures whose partition functions are highest weight vectors of particular $\mathcal{W}$-algebra representations. Such highest weight vectors arise as partition functions of Airy structures only under certain conditions on the representations. In the spectral curve formulation of topological recursion, we show that this generalization amounts to adding specific terms to the correlators $ \omega_{g,1}$, which leads to a ``shifted topological recursion'' formula. We then prove that the wave-functions constructed from this shifted version of topological recursion are WKB solutions of families of quantizations of the spectral curve with $ \hbar$-dependent terms. In the reverse direction, starting from an $\hbar$-connection, we find that it is of topological type if the exact same conditions that we found for the Airy structures are satisfied. When this happens, the resulting shifted loop equations can be solved by the shifted topological recursion obtained earlier.

authors.name: Rapha\"el Belliard, Vincent Bouchard, Reinier Kramer, Tanner Nelson

papers.title: The Primakoff effect: The Axion-Photon Mixing in the Context of Stellar Plasma Physics
papers.summary: We propose in this work the study of the production of axions in stellar plasma medium through an external magnetic field. In the background field approximation, we can show that the presence of the external magnetic field induces a mixing between the photon and the axion, i.e. the so called Primakoff effect. Since the axion is one of the greatest candidates for dark matter, for being a neutral pseudo-scalar field, the Primakoff process constitutes a mechanism (or portal) to access the dark sector, which in turn provides us new perspectives beyond the standard model. In the high energies limit, observables like probabilities transitions and particles production rates were computed.

authors.name: Bernard Teles de Menezes

papers.title: Phase-space description of photon emission
papers.summary: Interactions between charged particles and light occur in real space and time, yet quantum field theory usually describes them in momentum space. Whereas this approach is well suited for calculating emission probabilities and cross sections, it is insensitive to spatial and temporal phenomena such as, for instance, radiation formation, quantum coherence, and wave packet spreading. These effects are becoming increasingly important for experiments involving electrons, photons, atoms, and ions, particularly with the advent of attosecond spectroscopy and metrology. Here, we propose a general method for describing the emission of photons in phase space via a Wigner function. Several effects for Cherenkov radiation are predicted, absent in classical realm or in quantum theory in momentum space, such as a finite spreading time of the photon, finite duration of the flash and a quantum shift of the photon arrival time. The photon spreading time turns out to be negative near the Cherenkov angle, the flash duration is defined by the electron packet size, and the temporal shift can be both positive and negative. The characteristic time scales of these effects lie in the atto- and femtosecond ranges, thereby illustrating atomic origins of these macroscopic phenomena. The near-field distribution of the photon field resembles the electron packet shape, thus making ``snapshots'' of the emitter wave function. Our approach can easily be generalized to the other types of radiation and extended to scattering, decay, and annihilation processes, bringing tomographic methods of quantum optics to particle physics.

authors.name: D. V. Karlovets, A. A. Shchepkin, A. D. Chaikovskaia, D. V. Grosman, D. A. Kargina, U. G. Rybak, G. K. Sizykh

papers.title: Gauge Symmetry in Quantum Simulation --- Redundancy Is All You Need ---
papers.summary: Quantum simulation of non-Abelian gauge theories requires careful handling of gauge redundancy. We present universal principles for treating gauge symmetry that apply to any quantum simulation approach. Our main result is that enforcing gauge-singlet constraints is conceptually and practically unnecessary for extracting physical observables. Physical states need not be represented by gauge singlets; singlet and non-singlet representations are both valid, with distinct practical trade-offs that we elucidate using analogies to BRST quantization, and the non-singlet approach is likely more efficient toward the continuum limit. As in classical electrodynamics and the path-integral formulation, gauge redundancy simplifies things. We demonstrate these principles within a complete quantum simulation framework based on the orbifold lattice, which enables explicit and efficient circuit constructions relevant to real-world QCD. We show how non-singlet approaches yield gauge-invariant observables through wave packets and string excitations, and that this approach is universal and efficient. For the limited situations where a singlet representation is genuinely required, we introduce a Haar-averaging projection implemented via linear combinations of unitaries and analyze its cost and truncation errors; its post-selection cost makes it a fallback rather than the default. We also introduce a penalty term in the Hamiltonian that eliminates non-singlet states from the low-energy spectrum. Working in temporal gauge, we map lattice Yang-Mills dynamics to Pauli-string Hamiltonians suitable for Trotterization. Classical simulations of small systems validate convergence criteria, quantify truncation and Trotter errors, and yield concrete resource estimates and scalable circuit recipes for SU$(N)$ gauge theories.

authors.name: Masanori Hanada, Shunji Matsuura, Andreas Schafer, Jinzhao Sun

papers.title: Universality of Primordial Anisotropies in Gravitational Wave Background
papers.summary: We investigate the general structure of primordial anisotropies in the stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB). Many mechanisms generating primordial SGWB anisotropies, including fossil and propagation effects, exhibit similar multipole dependences despite their distinct physical origins, implying the presence of a common underlying structure. To characterize this structure, we introduce a model-independent framework, the Cosmological Form Factor (CFF), that describes how long-wavelength perturbations modulate short-scale SGWB statistics. Within this broad class of mechanisms, we show that the allowed angular and polarization structures of SGWB anisotropies are universally determined by general principles, including statistical isotropy, locality, and the basic properties of long-wavelength perturbations. In contrast to these universal structures, observables such as amplitudes and frequency dependence retain information about the origin. Our results provide a unified and effective description of primordial SGWB anisotropies, clarifying which aspects are universal and which are model dependent, and therefore offer a theoretical foundation for interpreting future gravitational-wave observations.

authors.name: Boyuan Jiang, Ryo Saito, Ying-li Zhang

papers.title: Unconventional magnetoelectric conductivity and electrochemical response from dipole-like sources of Berry curvature
