papers.summary: The 3D distribution of dust and gas in the Milky Way's Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) is key to understanding gas inflows towards the Galactic Centre (GC), the process of star formation in this extreme environment, and the propagation of energetic cosmic rays originating from Sgr A*. However, while recent efforts have combined datasets in a Bayesian framework to estimate the near/far positions of individual molecular clouds in the CMZ, conflicts between different methodologies still remain and we are still lacking a comprehensive, model-independent map of all of the gas and dust in the CMZ, which is critical to address key science questions. Here we develop a new methodology to infer the 3D dust distribution of the CMZ. The key idea of the method is to use stellar proper motions to get probabilistic information about the unknown stellar distances through a model of the distribution of star positions and velocities of the nuclear stellar disc (NSD), co-spatial with the CMZ. Taking stellar proper motions and extinctions as input, the latter adopted as a proxy of the dust column density, the method returns the 3D dust distribution. It is non-parametric, makes no assumptions on the functional form of the dust distribution, and is fundamentally distinct and largely independent of all existing methods. We show that the method can robustly and effectively reconstruct the mock 3D CMZ structure by testing it on a range of mock dust distributions, both analytically generated and taken from hydrodynamical simulations. Finally, we discuss the prospects for applying the method to real data.

authors.name: Arianna Vasini, Mattia C. Sormani, Jason L. Sanders, Adam Ginsburg, Cara Battersby, Francisco Nogueras-Lara, Rainer Sch\"odel, Evangelia Deliporanidou, Marco Donati, Zi-Xuan Feng, Karl Fiteni, Savannah Gramze, Xingchen Li, Dani R. Lipman, Perry H. Hatchfield

papers.title: Relativistic hydrodynamics of a charged fluid from Myers-Pospelov Lorentz-Violating Electrodynamics
papers.summary: We derive the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics for a charged fluid from Lorentz-violating Myers--Pospelov electrodynamics. Starting from the modified fermionic and electromagnetic equations of motion, we employ the covariant Wigner formalism to establish the semiclassical spectral constraints and distribution function, which, combined with Noether's theorem, yield the energy-momentum tensor, particle current, and corresponding conservation laws in the presence of Lorentz violation. The resulting hydrodynamic description contains Lorentz-violating corrections to the thermodynamic quantities and to the fluid currents. In the purely timelike sector, these corrections can be absorbed into effective thermodynamic quantities, preserving the isotropic structure of the fluid equations. In contrast, spacelike backgrounds introduce explicit contributions along the preferred direction, which cannot be absorbed into the standard hydrodynamic variables and give rise to anisotropic forces and torques. These effects lead to departures from standard relativistic charged-fluid hydrodynamics and provide a direct macroscopic manifestation of the Lorentz-violating background. Our results establish a first-principles framework for investigating the macroscopic consequences of Lorentz violation in relativistic charged fluids and provide a starting point for the development of a consistent Lorentz-violating relativistic magnetohydrodynamic theory.

authors.name: Matheus Duarte, Vitor de Souza

papers.title: Geometrical and Optical Design of the GUEST Laser-Ranged Test Masses for the Detection of Gravitational Waves in the $\mu$Hz range
papers.summary: The GUEST (Gravitational Universe Exploration with Satellite Tracking) mission aims at detecting gravitational waves in the yet almost unexplored $\mu$Hz frequency range through high-precision orbital tracking. The unprecedented scientific objectives of this experiment demand equally advanced optical solutions: the highly eccentric orbit imposes dual measurement regimes; a low-velocity, long-range scenario at apogee and a high-velocity, short-range scenario at perigee. The substantial disparity between these conditions is addressed through a novel optical architecture incorporating two distinct types of Corner-Cube Retroreflectors (CCRs) with 1" and 2" apertures (CCR1 and CCR2, respectively). The proposed layout has been designed to ensure isotropy and homogeneity of the optical response while maintaining efficient packing over the spherical surface of the spacecraft. The resulting Optical Cross-Section (OCS) has been evaluated using a custom reduced-order model, which captures the behavior of individual CCRs under varying illumination conditions. This model has been calibrated by reconstructing the optical response of the LARES-2 satellite and has enabled a detailed assessment of the contributions of each CCR type along the GUEST orbit. Finally, sensitivity analyses have been conducted to investigate the impact of key design parameters, including the ratio between CCR types, laser wavelength, spacecraft diameter, Dihedral Angle Offsets (DAOs), and mechanical configurations.

authors.name: Dario Vetrano, Giada Bargiacchi, Nicol\`o Burzill\`a, Roberto Campagnola, Francesco Del Ferraro Iacobelli, Luca Porcelli, Simone Dell'Agnello, Diego Blas

papers.title: Multiwavelength Classification of Chandra Sources in Omega Centauri
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive study of X-ray sources in the globular cluster NGC 5139 to date. Over 200 Chandra sources are cross-matched to multiwavelength catalogs from HST, JWST, and MeerKAT. We employ a machine-learning classification pipeline (MUWCLASS) for the first time in such a crowded stellar environment and introduce the globular-cluster-specific training dataset, which compiles previously classified sources from 25 Galactic globular clusters. Given the challenges presented by the high-density environment, we compare the MUWCLASS results with traditional classification methods. We confirm counterpart associations suggested in previous works and also identify new confident and candidate associations. We discuss the implications of our classification results in light of models of cluster dynamical evolution and binary formation/destruction.

authors.name: Steven Chen, Oleg Kargaltsev, Jeremy Hare, Hui Yang, Oleg Smirnov, Ian Heywood, Talon Myburgh

papers.title: The origin and distribution of diffuse HI in the close interacting MHONGOOSE galaxy systems
papers.summary: We present the deepest HI observations of the two systems with Dproj < 100 kpc, and $\Delta$ vsys < 200 km/s in the MHONGOOSE survey. The MeerKAT observations are characterised by 3$\sigma$ NHI = 10$^{17.9}$ cm$^{-2}$ over 16 km/s at 4 kpc scales. The new data have enabled us to detect HI in seven galaxies: the interacting NGC 3511/3513 pair, and an interacting triplet (NGC 4781, NGC 4790 and UGCA 308) along with two new (2MASX J1255 and MKT 25413) dwarf satellites. Six galaxies lie on the star-forming main sequence, and their HI gas fractions are typical for such systems. In contrast, MKT 25413 exhibits a log(MHI/Msun) = 5.7, which is the lowest MHI detected of a galaxy that is not a Milky Way satellite. This low surface brightness dwarf galaxy shows an anomalously low level of star formation and low HI fraction for its stellar mass. We also found ubiquitous low column density HI surrounding the galaxies, which is likely a consequence of mild tidal interactions from fly-bys in the past few hundred megayears. We derive the stellar and H$\alpha$ kinematics from VLT/MUSE observations and the H2 kinematics from ALMA observations. The kinematics of the stellar and multiphase interstellar medium of the interacting galaxies display ordered rotation, and the atomic-to-molecular gas ratios are indistinguishable from star-forming field galaxies. The stellar morphology of all the interacting galaxies (apart from the low-mass dwarf UGCA 308) does not show any major disruptions, and there is no stellar component associated with the HI tails, bridges or clouds in the intra-group mediums, down to $\mu_{g}$ = 29 mag arcsec$^{-2}$. We surmise that the mild environmental interactions in the close systems have the capacity to pull the diffuse HI out of the disc and redistribute it. The gas is not in equilibrium, although it remains bound and is in the process of falling back onto the disc.

authors.name: D. Kleiner, W. J. G. de Blok, J. Healy, F. M. Maccagni, E. M. Di Teodoro, A. Fraser-McKelvie, A. Marasco, S. Veronese, S. Kurapati

papers.title: Inferring the Total Mass of Galaxy Halos Using Photometry
papers.summary: Galaxy size, as defined as the radius at which the stellar surface density reaches $1~\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{pc}^{-2}$ ($R_1$), has been shown to correlate more tightly with stellar mass than the effective radius. Cosmological simulations further predict a tight relation between $R_1$ and dark matter halo mass ($M_{200}$), but this prediction has not yet been tested observationally. We present the first observational test of the predicted $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation and assess whether galaxy size, defined through $R_1$, can serve as a robust estimator of dark matter halo mass. We analyze galaxies from the SPARC database, combining high-quality rotation curves to infer dark matter halo masses with stellar surface density profiles derived from photometric data to measure $R_1$. We then compare the observed relation with the predictions from state-of-the-art cosmological simulations. We find good agreement between observations and simulations: galaxies follow the same tight $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation predicted by numerical models across the explored mass range, with low intrinsic scatter. We provide the first observational validation of the $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation, demonstrating that $R_1$ is a simple, physically motivated, and robust estimator of dark matter halo mass. Because $R_1$ is determined entirely from photometric observations, it provides a tool for inferring halo masses from imaging data alone, with applications to studies of galaxy formation and evolution.

authors.name: Chris Brook, Arianna di Cintio, Claudio Dalla Vecchia, Salvador Cardona Barrero, Elena Arjona-G\'alvez

papers.title: 2:1 Harmonics in the Radio Light Curves of Supermassive Black Hole Binary Candidates
papers.summary: We present evidence of 2:1 harmonic periodicities in two supermassive black hole binary (SMBHB) candidates (PKS J0805-0111 and PKS 2131-021) in the Owens Valley Radio Observatory (OVRO) + University of Michigan Radio Astronomical Observatory (UMRAO) monitoring programs. This potential discovery follows the previous detection of a 2:1 harmonic periodicity in the SMBHB candidate J1309+1154 from these programs. If confirmed, these suggest a physical origin of blazars exhibiting strong periodicities favoring 2:1 commensurabilities in their light curves. There are significant differences between the 2:1 harmonics in these three blazars, which may be due to differences in their central engines. These three SMBHB candidates demonstrate the importance of careful dissection, i.e. cutting apart and close examination, of blazar light curves, to reveal underlying evidence of coherence between different aspects of the periodicities observed in blazars in the presence of correlated random noise variations. This is particularly important for blazar SMBHB searches, given that the observed periods thus far are all longer than 2 years, and can disappear for long timespans. Harmonics may therefore be crucial in confirming the reality of periodicities and identifying blazar SMBHB candidates. We discuss four models that can account for 2:1 commensurable periodicities in blazar light curves and explain how future detections of shorter period SMBHB candidates, or the lack thereof, may be used to discriminate among the models. Arguments for and against the reality of these periodicities are presented.

authors.name: A. C. S. Readhead, M. F. Aller, R. D. Blandford, T. Surti, P. V. De la Parra, A. G. Sullivan, P. Mr\'oz, N. Murray, M. C. Begelman, B. Molina, M. L. Lister, E. R. Most, S. O'Neill, V. A. Diamantopoulos, N. Globus, T. Hovatta, I. Liodakis, T. J. Pearson, S. E. Tremblay

papers.title: On the Proper 3D Modeling of Orbits in Wide Binary Gravity Tests
papers.summary: A gravitationally-bound system of wide binary stars with precise 3D relative displacement $\mathbf{r}$ and velocity $\mathbf{v}$ can allow a Keplerian orbit reconstruction for an assumed gravitational parameter $G$. A sufficiently large sample of such systems can also be used to directly infer $G$ specific to the sample. A recent study argued that treating the semi-major axis ($a$) explicitly free with an empirical prior imposed on it can dramatically change the inference of $G$ in the Chae et al. sample of 36 wide binaries. Here we introduce and test a Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that allows $a$ to be explicitly free (with or without a prior on $a$), and find using the $\alpha$-Cen AB - proxima system and the Chae et al. sample that the explicit-$a$ algorithm with an observational constraint is fully equivalent to the implicit-$a$ algorithm with an internal consistency relation involving the sky-projected separation $s$. For the $\alpha$-Cen AB - proxima system, we present orbits in Milgromian (MOND) as well as Newtonian gravity models. We show that a recent claim of Newtonian gravity from the Chae et al. sample is a consequence of a fatal error in the code or arbitrarily enlarged errors. We discuss how wide binaries can be properly analyzed and modeled to probe gravity at low acceleration and test gravity models, including the necessity of deriving individual-specific parameters, the importance of follow-up observations for anomalous systems, and the relevance of Bayesian MCMC approaches.

authors.name: Kyu-Hyun Chae, Hyoseok Park, Youngsub Yoon

papers.title: Developing Environments: Formation and Quenching at Cosmic Noon Traced by the Large-scale Distribution of Gas and Galaxies
papers.summary: Environmental density correlates with galaxy properties in the local Universe, but how and when these trends emerge is unclear: at cosmic noon, large-scale structures are still assembling and galaxies quench rapidly for debated reasons. We study how the formation and quenching histories of massive galaxies at 1.7$1$), mostly in massive quiescent galaxies showing both. About 65\% of the sample follows a correlation between the tracers; two outlier regions stand out. A galaxy-rich, gas-poor region ($\delta_\#>2$, $\delta_{HI}1$), within 60 cMpc of the densest Hyperion cores, hosts rapidly quenched galaxies with a high incidence of AGN and outflows. This \emph{developing environment}, distinct from both mature protoclusters and the field, likely traces massive halos still assembling. Galaxy counts alone cannot capture the environment at cosmic noon: jointly mapping galaxies and cool gas is crucial to understand how environment regulates gas accretion, star formation, and quenching.

authors.name: Amir H. Khoram, Sirio Belli, Trevor Mendel, Letizia Bugiani, Matteo Sapori, Andrew B. Newman, Hossein Hatamnia, Finn Giddings, Rebecca L. Davies, Olga Cucciati, Bianca Poggianti, Amirnezam Amiri, Minjung Park, Anita Zanella, Tianmu Gao, Gabriel Maheson, Stefano Sotira, Caterina Liboni, Giulia Papini

papers.title: Origin of homochirality in peptides: The first milestone at the origin of life
papers.summary: Living organisms have some common structures, chemical reactions, and molecular structures. The organisms consist of cells with cell division; they have homochirality of protein and carbohydrate units, metabolism, and genetics, and they are mortal. The molecular structures and chemical reactions underlying these features are common to all, from the simplest bacteria to human beings. The origin of life is evolutionary, with the emergence of a network of spontaneous biochemical reactions, and evolution has taken place over a very long time. The evolution contains, however, some ``landmarks'' and bottlenecks, which in a revolutionary manner directed the evolution, and the article establishes an order of some of these events. Recent articles show that peptides in living organisms are long-time unstable, with loss of their secondary homochiral conformations and with D-amino acids. Based on these observations and an extensive scientific literature on Abiogenesis, we argue that the first milestone in the prebiotic evolution is at the emergence of homochiral peptides in an aqueous solution with a high concentration of amino acids and a lower water activity than in the cytosol in living organisms. The homochiral peptides in cytosol are unstable, and the long-time aging of peptides in the cytosol causes mortality of living organisms. The metabolism and genetics are established in an environment with homochiral peptides in the Earth's crust for $\approx$ 4 Gyr ago at a lower water activity than in the cytosol in living organisms. Finally, the cells with cell division are established in the Hot Springs environment at the interface between the crust and the Hadean Ocean.

authors.name: S{\o}ren Toxvaerd

papers.title: Bayesian Inference of the Landau Parameter $G'_0$ from Joint Gamow-Teller Measurements
papers.summary: $G'_0$ is the leading-order Landau-Migdal parameter that characterizes the spin-isospin dependent nucleon-nucleon interaction. Consequently, the $G'_0$ is closely related to the Gamow-Teller resonance (GTR), the beta and double-beta decay rates of finite nuclei, the response of hot and dense nucleonic matter that modifies the neutrino-nucleon absorption rates in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) and binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, and finally the critical density for pion condensation in neutron stars. In this letter, for the first time, we report the $G'_0$ with quantified uncertainty in the framework of Bayesian inference, using a self-consistent standard Skyrme Random Phase Approximation (RPA) model and joint constraints from experimental GTR measurements on $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$, $^{132}\mathrm{Sn}$, $^{90}\mathrm{Zr}$. Our extracted $G_0'$ at saturation density is $0.48\pm0.034$, which is close to the prediction of a few existing Skyrme models that consider spin-isospin observables but smaller than the traditional ones extracted from pion-exchange models. The reasons for this deviation, like the value of the nucleon effective mass $\frac{m^*}{m}$ and the density dependence of $G'_0$, are investigated. The density-dependent $G_0'$ values extracted in this work may guide the construction of new energy density functionals that aims to self-consistently describe the dense matter properties in the spin-isospin channel.

authors.name: Zidu Lin, Gianluca Col\`o, A. W. Steiner, Amber Stinson

papers.title: Parity-dependent wave absorption and optical characteristics of a cored magnetic black hole
papers.summary: We study light propagation and coupled gravitational--electromagnetic waves around a black hole supported by a nonlinear magnetic field. The same field action fixes the geometry, the mass--charge relation, and the wave potentials. We calculate two critical impact parameters for light and solve the coupled scattering equations in both parity sectors. In eight solutions of one action, the two optical scales differ by $3.6$--$7.2\%$. The wave absorption also depends on parity. For $\ell=2$, the gap between the larger absorption eigenvalues reaches about $9.0$ percentage points. A wider frequency scan reveals a stronger effect in the second eigenchannel. The difference between the two absorption traces reaches $24.3$ percentage points. The trace equals twice the absorption of an equal incoherent mixture of incoming gravitational and electromagnetic fields. A controlled test of the wave operator shows that the nonlinear electromagnetic factor $\kappa$ plays an important role in the parity gap. We also examine four $\ell=3$ cases and use charge-matched Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes as a separate control. The optical and wave calculations provide two complementary properties of the same magnetic source.

authors.name: Mohsen Fathi, Faizuddin Ahmed

papers.title: Medium effects on neutron star modified and direct Urca cooling rates
papers.summary: We study the effects of in-medium modification of the elementary cooling processes on observable properties of isolated neutron stars. We then deduce the neutron star mass distributions compatible with the cooling analysis and compare with current theoretical models. We conclude that current cooling data require fast direct Urca (DU) cooling, moderated by proton superfluidity, to be active in most neutron stars, and that the DU onset threshold must lie below canonical masses. In that case medium modifications of modified Urca (MU) rates are practically insignificant, but the $nn$ Bremsstrahlung rate plays a dominant role.

authors.name: B. X. Zhou, Jin-Biao Wei, Z. H. Li, G. F. Burgio, H. -J. Schulze

papers.title: Evolved Spiking Neural Networks for EEG Seizure Detection: Calcium Dynamics and Delay Mechanics
papers.summary: Neuroevolution can discover compact network designs that are hard to specify by hand. The EONS framework evolves the topology, weights, thresholds and delays of neuromorphic spiking networks without gradients. We tested whether giving integrate-and-fire (IF) neurons an activity-dependent calcium current (Ca-IF neurons) improves evolved networks for EEG seizure detection, with calcium parameters fixed, shared across a network, or evolved for each neuron. On 10 held-out CHB-MIT patients never seen in training, per-neuron calcium raised the record-level Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) from 0.592 to 0.726 over 20 independent runs (p = 0.008) and lowered the false-alarm rate from 0.17 to 0.10. Fixed or per-network calcium gave no significant benefit. IF networks with evolved synaptic delays of 1-3 ticks gave a similar gain (p = 0.005), whereas axonal delays did not. On Siena, with unchanged settings, per-neuron calcium gained +0.096 MCC over IF in one patient-disjoint split (p = 0.011) and +0.059 in the other (p = 0.052). These results suggest that calcium and delays may make the evolutionary search more effective, and motivate testing on more data and in neuromorphic hardware.

authors.name: Tuba Aksoy

papers.title: Fly Whiskers Meet LiDAR: Robust Navigation under Sensor Failure
papers.summary: We extend FLYNN, a leaky integrator recurrent network wired on the Drosophila melanogaster connectome, with a 32-ray 2D LiDAR interface that requires no learned fusion layer beyond a scalar input gain. A 270 degree frontal scan at 8 m range is injected as inverted proximity into the 37 BM Vib head-bristle neurons. Across 24 paired comparisons in a four- state vision matrix with LiDAR on or off, FLYNN-LiDAR has 17 significant wins, 5 nonsignificant comparisons, and 2 significant losses against three LiDAR-capable baselines. Both losses are to MobileNet with the left eye off. With full vision, FLYNN- LiDAR reaches 96.6% success. Under total vision loss, the scan raises success from 45.2% to 64.6%; the baselines reach 44.6% to 56.6% with the scan on. Under out of distribution textures, it is the only LiDAR-capable model whose success improves with the scan (44.2% to 58.4%); both CNNs score 0%, and SmallWorld declines from 26.8% to 7.4%. Under periodic vision dropout, FLYNN-LiDAR achieves 93.6% and 89.6% success at 25% and 50% duty with fewer collisions. Profiling the evaluated forward paths gives 3.93M multiply accumulate operations per step; EfficientNet and MobileNet require 4.60x and 2.94x as many. Final- state analysis shows near-linear sensory superposition (cosine 0.9955).

authors.name: Ali Mahzarnia, Homayoun Jamshidi

papers.title: Visualization and Characterization of Gene Group Distribution Patterns Across Genomes
papers.summary: Genes of the same family often lie close together on a chromosome, yet how far apart family members sit, and whether their spacing follows any pattern, has rarely been measured consistently across genomes. We built an interactive web application that places the members of any of the 1,396 FlyBase gene groups on the banded ideogram of the fruit fly (Drosophila melanogaster) and lists each member's neighbours. While browsing it, we found strikingly symmetric gene sets in which consecutive members are almost evenly spaced. In the RAB GTPases, two 5.08 Mb spacings differ by only 634 bp. We also found that distances between neighbouring members fall into two populations: short-range (median 1.8 kb) and long-range (median 2.4 Mb). Although an arm-matched random control suggests that the even spacing (without a minimum-distance filter) as well as the long-range population arise largely by chance, the short-range population turns out to be a genuine clustering signal. We then extended the analysis to human and six other model organisms (mouse, zebrafish, Caenorhabditis elegans, Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Arabidopsis thaliana and maize), and every genome showed the same two populations. The mixture curve of the two is nearly constant across chromosomes in some genomes (Type I: fly, maize, Arabidopsis, C. elegans) but varies across chromosomes in others (Type II: human, mouse, zebrafish, yeast). Thus, across eight eukaryotes, family members lie in two distance populations. The scale of the short-range population follows the spacing of genes in each genome, and the long-range population matches random placement in fly and is consistent with it in the other genomes. Our results also show that visual patterns such as even spacing must be tested against chance before they are interpreted. Our tool and approach give a simple way to explore and compare gene clustering across species.

authors.name: Yanying Wu

papers.title: GINsim 3.1: Qualitative modelling and dynamical analysis of logical regulatory networks
papers.summary: GINsim is a software for the definition and dynamical analysis of qualitative (Boolean and multi-valued) models of biological regulatory networks. Building on its modular architecture, based on the MDDlib decision-diagram and bioLQM model-manipulation libraries, GINsim version 3.1 introduces new functionalities aimed at the analysis of large logical models: the symbolic computation of trap-spaces, the Booleanisation of multilevel models and the reversal of model dynamics. GINsim 3.1 also extends the estimation of attractor reachability (Monte Carlo and Avatar algorithms), the computation of stable states, as well as model reduction functionalities. Analyses can be applied to perturbed models, and scripted, in particular from the CoLoMoTo interactive notebook. We illustrate the main functionalities of GINsim on a reference multilevel model of regulatory network that control the mammalian cell cycle, including the computation of its stable states and cyclic attractor, the assessment of their reachability, and the identification of the regulatory circuits driving multistability and oscillations. GINsim is freely available under GPL-3.0 at https://ginsim.github.io/, runs on any platform supporting Java, and is interoperable with the other tools of the CoLoMoTo community. Its website provides installation instructions and reference documentation, as well as a repository of Boolean and multilevel logical models.

authors.name: Laurent Tichit, Dominique Benielli, Olivier Chabrol, Denis Thieffry, Claudine Chaouiya, Pedro T. Monteiro

papers.title: Evolving view on phylogenetic networks
papers.summary: Reticulate processes such as hybridization, introgression, and horizontal gene transfer cannot be fully represented by a bifurcating tree. Enter phylogenetic networks: first as split graphs to visualize tree discordance, then as explicit probabilistic models that capture biological phenomena. Here, we describe the broad taxonomy of network representations, distinguishing the principal classes of explicit networks, their biological interpretability and our ability to accurately estimate them from empirical data. We also trace the evolution of the main network inferential methods from hybrid detection tests, distance- and subgraph-based amalgamation methods, probabilistic approaches under the multispecies network coalescent, composite-likelihood and divide-and-conquer frameworks, while highlighting the selective pressures of statistical identifiability and computational scalability that have shaped this evolution. As we move towards a network thinking paradigm, previously isolated methodological lineages from population genetics, phylogenomics, and mathematical network theory are now introgressing, uniting diverse network models into a shared framework that can integrate sequence- and species-level reticulate processes, increase robustness to systematic errors, and refine algorithms for genome-scale data, expanding the tree of life into a richer, more entangled yet clearer picture of evolution.

authors.name: Claudia Solis-Lemus

papers.title: Basic Reproductive Numbers in Host-Parasite Systems with Demographic Bistability
papers.summary: The basic reproductive number, $\mathcal{R}_0$, is widely used to determine whether an infectious disease can persist in a population. However, its interpretation may become unclear when the underlying disease-free demographic dynamics exhibit multiple types of stable attractors. In this study, we investigate how demographic bistability between fixed points and periodic cycles affects the calculation and interpretation of $\mathcal{R}_0$. We consider two discrete-time host-parasite models with infection: a tick-host model motivated by Borrelia burgdorferi transmission and a Nicholson-Bailey host-parasitoid model with intraspecific competition and infection. For each model, we calculate reproductive numbers associated with different disease-free attractors using the next-generation operator method and compare their invasion thresholds. In the tick-host model, the reproduction number calculated on the stable demographic cycle differs from that calculated at the positive coexistence fixed point, resulting in parameter regions where infection can invade at one demographic attractor but not the other. In contrast, in the host-parasitoid model, the host-driven invasion threshold is necessarily the same at the positive coexistence fixed point and on the host-only periodic cycles. These contrasting results demonstrate that demographic bistability alone does not necessarily produce attractor-dependent invasion thresholds. Rather, the effect of demographic dynamics on invasion depends on the structure of pathogen transmission. In particular, a complete host--vector--host transmission pathway can allow differences between demographic attractors to alter the invasion threshold. Our results emphasize the importance of considering both demographic dynamics and transmission structure when interpreting $\mathcal{R}_0$ in populations with multiple stable disease-free states.

authors.name: Carli Peterson, Erika Gallo, Christopher Kribs

papers.title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
papers.summary: Real-time phase estimation on stimulus-aligned transient EEG is critical for closed-loop neuromodulation systems targeting the theta-band, yet most real-time phase estimation methods have been developed and validated on resting-state, high-fidelity signals in the alpha band. Recent work has pursued deep learning architectures, while individualized classical bandpass filter tuning remains underexplored. This study characterizes the spectral and temporal properties of non-anticipative bandpass filtering and demonstrates the performance gains achieved through individualized tuning. We present a Bayesian-Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg (BOB) model evaluated on EEG recorded during peripheral vibrotactile stimulation of the left median nerve (theta, N=20 healthy subjects) and on resting-state recordings from the Max Planck Institute's LEMON dataset (alpha, N=20 healthy subjects). BOB was benchmarked against the Deep Dual-Branch Complex Neural Network (DBCNN), EEG Phase Prediction Network (EPN), Phastimate, and Phase Estimation with Autoregressive Padding (PEAP) under matched testing conditions: channel selection, individualized optimization, evaluation time points, and an offline reference phase obtained through zero-phase filtering and the Hilbert transform. Under these testing conditions, BOB achieved matched or better performance than these models at a fraction of the calibration time.

authors.name: Ivan Martinez-Kay, Tatiana Kardashina, ShiNung Ching, Eric C. Leuthardt, Benjamin T. Acland

papers.title: BEAGLE in Action: Phylogenetic Likelihoods for Very Large State Spaces
papers.summary: Computing phylogenetic likelihoods becomes challenging when the continuous-time Markov chain has a large state space. At each branch, pruning algorithms require terms of the form $e^{Q t}\cdot B$, where $Q$ is an $S \times S$ rate matrix (e.g., for $S$ states), $t$ is a branch length, and the columns of matrix $B$ (e.g., $B \in \mathbb{R}_{+}^{S \times L}$) are partial-likelihood vectors for $L$ site patterns. Many implementations calculate the dense transition matrix $P(t)=e^{Q t}$ via eigendecomposition and multiply it by $B$. This strategy is efficient for small state spaces, but it can be inefficient for large sparse rate matrices because forming $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices destroys sparsity and its cost may not be well amortized when $L$ is small. We implement an alternative likelihood kernel based on the Al-Mohy and Higham (2011) algorithm for computing the action of the matrix exponential directly, avoiding explicit construction of $P(t)$ or its eigen vector matrices. The resulting method takes full advantage of the sparsity of $Q$. We implement this method as a CPU-based extension to the BEAGLE library and evaluate it on two large-state molecular models: a Markov-modulated codon model of heterotachy with $M$ selective regimes and $61\cdot M$ possible states, and a codon-pair model of interlocus gene conversion between two paralogs with $61^2=3\,721$ possible states. Our results characterize when action-based likelihood computation improves performance over calculating $e^{Q t}$ directly. We show that this method enables fast, scalable inference for complex models, removing a key computational barrier to the study of evolution with large state space models.

authors.name: Benjamin D Redelings, April Wright, Karthik Gangavarapu, Yucai Shao, Filippo Monti, Wu-Min Deng, Shuo Su, Andrew Rambaut, Guy Baele, Philippe Lemey, Marc A. Suchard, Xiang Ji

papers.title: Trail systems self-organize through individual route optimization
papers.summary: As animals, including humans, walk, they compact the vegetation and ground beneath them, reducing the cost of movement for subsequent travelers. From this positive feedback emerge networks of trails which allow for efficient movement and store generational-scale information about the environment. Models simulating this process show how individuals following local cues produce trail systems with many of the features of real-world networks. However, little has been done to investigate walkers with more complete knowledge of their environment and the abilities to plan their behavior intelligently. Here we introduce a simple general model for trail formation, based on minimizing cost of movement by individuals. As in real environments, our simulations produce a striking variety of complex trail networks. We show that these trail systems optimally connect space according to the spatial needs of the walkers, that the geometry of those trail systems matches theoretical predictions and that the systems they generate may fall into multiple attracting states. As technological advances allow us to quantify trail systems across diverse habitats and species, our model provides a theoretical foundation for empirical research on animal trails and for understanding the emergence of human transportation networks, with implications for urban design.

authors.name: Brendan Wallace, Andrew Berdahl

papers.title: A model for cholera with infectiousness of deceased individuals and vaccination
papers.summary: A cholera transmission model is formulated that incorporates waterborne and horizontal transmissions as well as infectivity of deceased individuals. The model includes an Allee effect for the bacteria in the environment and imperfect and waning vaccination. Mathematical properties of the model are investigated, with an environmental bistability shown to combine with a vaccine-driven one, although a computational search for the latter fails to detect its presence in realistic parameter ranges. The computational analysis also considers the interplay between vaccination strategy, vaccine efficacy and waning, as well as the effect of transmission of the disease during funeral rites. The effect of control scenarios such as water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) or Safe and dignified burials are assessed.

authors.name: Annour Saad Abdramane, Julien Arino, Patrick M Tchepmo Djomegni, Mahamat S Daoussa Haggar

papers.title: Physical disturbance expands the climatic envelope of annual plant dominance
papers.summary: Disturbance regimes and nutrient inputs are changing worldwide, with consequences for the structure and functioning of plant communities. Life-history theory predicts that disturbance should shift communities from long-lived perennials toward short-lived annuals, and that nutrient enrichment may amplify this shift. However, these predictions have not been tested experimentally across broad environmental gradients. Here, using a global grassland experiment spanning 37 sites, we tested how severe physical disturbance (vegetation removal and shallow soil tillage) and fertilisation alter the annual-perennial balance, and whether disturbance expands the climatic envelope of annual dominance. Disturbance increased annual species share from 15% to 29% and relative annual cover from 9% to 29%, whereas fertilisation had little influence and did not interact with disturbance. The disturbance-driven shift arose through contrasting pathways: in graminoids and legumes, perennial cover declined, while in forbs, annual cover expanded. In the absence of disturbance, annual dominance was restricted to systems with extremely hot and dry summers, yet disturbance consistently increased annual prevalence across climatic gradients and doubled the extent of climate space in which annuals dominated. During repeated disturbance, annuals may help maintain vegetation cover, but their expansion also signals loss of perennial cover and associated ecosystem functions.

authors.name: Niv DeMalach, Roberto Salguero-Gomez, Oded Hollander, Jane Lucas, Alexander T. Strauss, Tilak Chaudhary, Y. Anny Chung, James K. McCarthy, Bruno Moreira, La\'is Petri, Rachael Thornley, Ingrid J. Slette, Elizabeth T. Borer, Eric W. Seabloom, Joe Atkinson, Karen H. Beard, Lars A. Brudvig, Christopher P. Catano, Jane A. Catford, Aimee Classen, Adam Thomas Clark, Ciara Dwyer, Charles Fenster, Oscar Godoy, Or Gross, Elizabeth Gusm\'an-Montalav\'an, W. Stanley Harpole, Erika Hersch-Green, Petr Holub, Anke Jentsch, Gaurav Kandlikar, Kevin Kirkman, Sally E. Koerner, Andrew Kulmatiski, Daijiang Li, Andrew S. MacDougall, Pierre Mariotte, Jason P. Martina, Pablo A. Meglioli, Jonathan Millett, Lydia O'Halloran, Ra\'ul Ochoa-Hueso, Rom\`a Ogaya, Brooke Osborne, Kalpana K. Patabendige, Josep Pe\~nuelas, Pablo Peri, Steven C. Pennings, Anita C. Risch, Christiane Roscher, Nathan J. Sanders, Carly Stevens, Lauren Sullivan, Pedro M. Tognetti, Diego V\'elez-Mora, Cameron Wagg, Chhaya Werner

papers.title: Maternal Anxiety During Pregnancy and Offspring Information Processing Across Development: A Theory-Guided Predictive-Processing Reappraisal of Two Longitudinal Cohorts
papers.summary: Prenatal maternal distress has been associated with differences in offspring brain and behavioural development, but is rarely framed computationally. Predictive-processing (PP) accounts propose that perception, cognition, and action arise from interactions between input and internally generated predictions, partly governed by precision. We reappraised eleven publications from two non-clinical prospective cohorts, selected using prespecified criteria, to assess whether they form a coherent PP-compatible developmental pattern. Eight Leuven publications spanned adolescence to adulthood. Externally cued response inhibition showed no detectable group differences in modestly powered samples, whereas differences emerged when task goals, stimulus relevance, expected outcomes, and response policies had to be generated or maintained endogenously. At age 28, higher prenatal anxiety was associated with lower radial and mean diffusivity in the left superior posterior corona radiata, lower Vocabulary scores, weaker medial prefrontal-left inferior frontal and prefrontal-left supramarginal gyrus connectivity, and greater unpleasantness of induced dyspnoea. In three Tilburg ERP publications (infancy and early childhood), higher prenatal anxiety was associated with increased processing of repeated standard tones, fearful relative to happy vocalizations, and neutral rather than pleasant or unpleasant pictures. Maternal mindfulness showed the opposite association for the repeated standard. Across cohorts, findings were compatible with differences in how relevance and processing resources are allocated to predictable, threat-related, ambiguous, contextual, feedback-related, and bodily information. Because the publications did not estimate precision, prediction errors, or priors, this is a theory-guided, post-hoc reappraisal that generates discriminating hypotheses rather than a formal computational test.

authors.name: Bea R. H. Van den Bergh, Martin G. Frasch

papers.title: Do agents need to sleep?
papers.summary: LLM-based agents, which increasingly operate persistently across sessions and accumulate memory through interaction, already exhibit the familiar symptoms of unchecked plasticity: semantic drift, degraded retrieval precision, propagation of stored errors, and saturation of memory capacity. Drawing on the selectionist "ringing, resonance and renormalization" (RRR) account of sleep, we propose that each of its three phases maps onto an operation feasible in digital memory architectures. Engineers building stateful agents, meanwhile, are independently rediscovering the problems sleep evolved to solve: what to forget, and when to do the forgetting. From this we derive the falsifiable prediction that selectionist consolidation will outperform instructionist alternatives as memory stores grow large. The core claim concerns the nature of continuous learning itself: plasticity has a price, and for any system that learns continuously under finite capacity while coupled to its environment, that price is sleep.

authors.name: Ido Haber, Giulio Tononi

papers.title: Quantum banking system for secure cash withdrawal
papers.summary: A quantum-secure withdrawal framework is presented by replacing reproducible classical credentials with quantum tokens for authentication. The protocol integrates token generation, authentication, and verification into the existing banking workflow using experimentally motivated quantum control techniques. This mitigates card cloning, credential theft, and counterfeiting.

authors.name: Vineet Kumar

papers.title: Optimised finite key for satellite up-link entangled quantum key distribution
papers.summary: Entanglement-based quantum key distribution from ground to satellite has been proposed as a scalable primitive for global quantum networks and will be demonstrated as part of the imminent QEYSSat mission. Both theoretical studies and experimental emulations have shown that a significant asymptotic key rate can be expected. In this work we investigate this scenario with a more rigorous security analysis taking into account the finite size effects that arise from short block lengths common in satellite transmission. Our findings suggest a slight alteration of the optimal source operation when informed by finite statistics as opposed to the asymptotic regime, notably that the pump power should be slightly lowered. We quantify the annual key rate based on a dynamically optimised source operation for the Heriot-Watt ground station and several satellite parameters. We find an improved annual key rate when accumulating all raw key material before extracting a secure key instead of doing so for each overpass. We ultimately show that QEYSSat will be able to generate a significant secure annual key with both strategies.

authors.name: Thomas Jaeken, Faris Redza, Stefan B\"auml, Daniel K. L. Oi, Alessandro Fedrizzi, Jasminder S. Sidhu

papers.title: Long-range entangled criticality from coherent errors
papers.summary: We find that coherent error can induce a phase transition from the clean surface code phase into an extended long-range entangled critical regime with diverging Markov length. To demonstrate this, we establish two general results of independent interest. The first relates topology and quantum information to mixed-state entanglement: we show that when a noise channel acting on a topological code preserves a higher-form symmetry and nonzero coherent information, the noisy state for generic logical input is long-range entangled. The second generalizes the local recovery construction based on finite Markov length to any locally parameterized family, thus encompassing local Lindbladian evolution, coherent errors followed by syndrome dephasing, and thermal states. We apply these results to the honeycomb surface code, in which we find an extended long-range entangled critical regime that is a quasi-long-ranged counterpart of 1-form strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking. As a byproduct of these studies, we relate the conditional mutual information to conductance in a Majorana network model.

authors.name: Amir-Reza Negari, Subhayan Sahu, Jan Behrends, Benjamin B\'eri, Timothy H. Hsieh

papers.title: Entanglement-Aware Quantum Circuit Optimization through Globally Optimal Partitioning
papers.summary: We introduce a scalable framework for globally optimal quantum-circuit partitioning and entanglement-aware block resynthesis. The partitioning problem is formulated as an integer linear program over qubit-feasible convex subcircuits, supporting objectives such as minimizing the number of partitions or a weighted execution cost. The resulting partition selection is exact over the enumerated feasible candidates and their computed costs when the ILP is solved to proven optimality. The selected partitions are resynthesized using an operator-Schmidt rank (OSR) based synthesis technique, which exploits their internal entanglement structure. We compare the end-to-end integer linear programming (ILP)--OSR workflow with BQSKit while identifying their different routing methods, and separately compare local OSR and BQSKit synthesis on matched three- and four-qubit unitaries. On the frozen sample of 772 local unitary targets, OSR produces 741 verified syntheses versus 617 for BQSKit, and matches or improves the CNOT count in all 617 jointly verified pairs. These results demonstrate that globally optimal partition selection combined with entanglement-aware resynthesis improves circuit quality and extends block-based optimization to problem sizes that are impractical for existing optimization workflows.

authors.name: Gregory Morse, Muhammad Al Farizi, Jakab N\'adori, L\'aszl\'o Hajas, Tam\'as Kozsik, Peter Rakyta

papers.title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks
papers.summary: We propose a physics-informed neural network (PINN) approach for high-fidelity quantum gate learning in both one- and two-qubit systems. We train a PINN using the time-dependent Schr\"{o}dinger equation, where smooth control fields with fixed boundary conditions are obtained by minimizing a loss function that considers model dynamics, gate error, physical constraints, regularization terms, and multiple initial conditions. Training considers pairs of mutually unbiased bases, while independent validation combines Haar-random input states with the average gate fidelity. Unitary simulations yield an average gate infidelity of $8.49\times10^{-8}$ for Hadamard and values between $3.39\times10^{-7}$ and $4.96\times10^{-6}$ for controlled-NOT under $XX$, $YY$, and $ZZ$ interactions. We examine how the learned control fields depend on the coupling, training configuration, and available local fields, including five exchange-type dipolar scenarios. We test the learned control fields under the Lindblad master equation with dephasing and amplitude damping, theoretically reproducing the expected first-order fidelity loss in the weak-dissipation regime. Finally, boundary-adapted Chebyshev expansions represent 139 learned controls with a minimum common count of $K_\ast=24$ coefficients per control for all eleven family-averaged mean squared errors to fall below $10^{-6}$. Separately, square-pulse and Strang propagation at $K=30$ preserve all 31 continuous polynomial references within infidelity $10^{-5}$ at $N=128$ and all larger tested resolutions, under both sampling rules. These results connect multi-state gate synthesis, control-resource characterization, and compact square-pulse playback.

authors.name: Luis Fabra, Cristian E. Susa, Alcides Montoya, Ariel Norambuena

papers.title: Unital qubit channels are $3$-noisy
papers.summary: The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated. It is established that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is itself n-noisy, and this n-noisy property is shown to be an invariant under unitary equivalence. Furthermore, by utilizing majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, we demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated using a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment. Together, these results advance the classification and physical realization of noisy quantum channels.

authors.name: Indu Bala, Preeti Parashar, Swapan Rana

papers.title: Analog quantum simulation of paraparticle statistics
papers.summary: Bosonic and fermionic quantum statistics describe all known elementary and emergent particles in three dimensions, although many attempts have been made to discover other valid quantum statistical frameworks. One recent formulation proposes "$R$-paraparticles," indistinguishable particles with nonlocal internal degrees of freedom governed by generalized exchange rules [Wang and Hazzard, Nature 637, 314 (2025)]. Here, we emulate a species of paraparticle that exhibits a generalized Pauli exclusion principle using a superconducting qubit lattice. We confirm its unique quantum statistics by measuring a $180^\circ$ phase shift under paraparticle exchange, observing antibunching independent of internal degrees of freedom under two-particle interference at a beamsplitter, and finding a thermal occupation inconsistent with both Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac statistics. These results demonstrate that parastatistics are observable on quantum simulation platforms, further motivating their use to explore theorized new phases of matter.

authors.name: Gyunghun Kim, Cora N. Barrett, Sarah E. Muschinske, Junyoung An, Helin Zhang, Ilan T. Rosen, Rabindra Das, Michael A. Gingras, David K. Kim, Bethany M. Niedzielski, Meghan Schuldt, Jonilyn L. Yoder, Mollie E. Schwartz, Kyle Serniak, Jeffrey A. Grover, Max Hays, William D. Oliver

papers.title: Non-Hermitian effective dynamics from post-selection protocols
papers.summary: Multiple seemingly distinct frameworks are commonly proposed to explain the emergence of effective non-Hermitian dynamics in quantum systems coupled to an environment. Furthermore, it remains contested how to properly calculate expectation values or whether thermal equilibrium states exist in non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we show that Feshbach projection, the Lindblad master equation, and the ancilla approach can all be understood through the Kraus map formalism, leading to non-Hermitian time evolution if an appropriate post-selection procedure is enforced. After first deriving an exact expression for the conditional system dynamics, we discuss the approximations employed in each approach and the classes of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians that can be obtained. Within this framework, we physically justify the consistency of the right-right formalism (as opposed to the biorthogonal one) for calculating expectation values. Finally, we demonstrate that the traditional notion of thermodynamic equilibrium is not applicable to general non-Hermitian systems. Consequently, stationary states are characterized as non-equilibrium steady states, which should not be conflated with system-projected thermal states of the system-environment composite.

authors.name: Apostolos Siskou, Volker Meden

papers.title: The Impact of Internal Electric Fields on Accurate Diamond Magnetometry
papers.summary: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center spin ensembles are a promising platform for accurate vector magnetometry, as they offer measurements referenced to a spin Hamiltonian in an anisotropic crystal with native vector sensing capabilities. However, charged dopants within the diamond produce random internal electric fields (RIEFs) that shift NV spin-transition frequencies, and their impact on the accuracy of NV magnetometry has not been investigated. Here, we characterize RIEFs' effect on NV spin-transition spectra and propose an analytical fitting function to improve accuracy in their presence. We build a Monte Carlo RIEF model that reproduces the asymmetric lineshapes observed in experimental optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra, and use it as a testbed to quantify RIEF-induced errors by simulating ODMR spectra including RIEFs and comparing reconstructed magnetic fields to the known model input. With standard analysis approaches, we observe systematic errors exceeding the g-factor uncertainty in fields below $\sim$ 5 mT, while the proposed fitting function reduces the error by nearly an order of magnitude. Our results demonstrate that RIEFs can play a significant role in the systematic error budget for NV magnetometry, and offer a path towards improved accuracy in NV quantum sensing.

authors.name: Jack Faller, Daphne Freda Gavras, Andrew Lowther, Romain Ruhlmann, Lilian Childress

papers.title: Tight Quasiprobabilistic Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Discrete Quantum Systems
papers.summary: It was conjectured by Wehrl and proven by Lieb that the Shannon differential entropy of the Husimi function of a continuous-variable quantum state is lower bounded by the value it takes on coherent states. This corroborates the intuition, familiar from Heisenberg's uncertainty relations, that coherent states are minimal uncertainty states. The analogous statement for the Wigner function would be that the Wigner differential entropy of states with a positive Wigner function is bounded below by the entropy of pure Gaussian states. This was conjectured a decade ago, but recently disproven. Here, we prove the analogous statement for Kirkwood-Dirac distributions with mutually unbiased bases and for the Gross-Wigner distributions. For these discrete systems, the entropy-minimizing role is played by the pure states with positive quasiprobability distributions. Further, we prove that Kirkwood-Dirac distributions with large nonpositivity have large uncertainty.

authors.name: Jonathan J. Thio, Stephan De Bi\`evre, Crispin H. W. Barnes, David R. M. Arvidsson-Shukur

papers.title: Gaussian Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
papers.summary: We consider a quantum integrated sensing and communication problem over an optical link in which a low-power transmitter simultaneously communicates with a receiver and identifies the range of a defect producing a backscattered signal. We model the system as a lossy thermal-noise bosonic channel, in which the target, modeled as a beamsplitter, affects the timing of the backscattered signal through its location. Motivated by the envisioned deployment of entanglement-enabled quantum networks, we develop two protocols that allow the transmitter to leverage shared Gaussian entanglement, in the form of independent two-mode squeezed vacuum states or coupled three-mode squeezed vacuum states, to assist both sensing and communication. Since entanglement is known to enhance sensing, as demonstrated in quantum illumination, and to increase communication rates through entanglement-assisted communication, the transmitter faces a trade-off in allocating its entanglement resources between the two tasks. Our main results characterize these trade-offs under the proposed protocols in terms of achievable communication rate/sensing error-exponent regions, which outperform time-sharing schemes and demonstrate a quantum advantage.

authors.name: Tuna Erdo\u{g}an, Shi-Yuan Wang, Shang-Jen Su, Matthieu R. Bloch

papers.title: Runtime Compilation for Quantum Circuits with PQF-Enabled $R_z$ Synthesis
papers.summary: In Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing (FTQC) using surface codes, reducing $T$-count is critical for efficient computation due to the high cost of $T$-state distillation. Probabilistic Quantum Circuit with Fallback (PQF) synthesis significantly lowers $T$-counts compared to standard protocols like Gridsynth, but introduces high circuit dynamism through extra gates inserted at runtime. This dynamism invalidates static compile-time routing, as these new $T$ gates require dynamic lattice surgery routing to establish non-intersecting ancilla paths to $T$-state factories while minimizing total execution time. To address this, we introduce $\text{R}^2$-PQF, a Runtime Routing protocol for PQF-synthesized quantum circuits. $\text{R}^2$-PQF dynamically routes gates layer-by-layer, computing paths during the execution of the previous logical timestep. To satisfy the strict computational window of $\sim t_{lattice\_surgery} + t_{reaction}$ and non-intersectionality constraints, we implement a Wavefront Breadth-First Search (W-BFS) and synthesise it on a 500MHz FPGA and 2 GHz ASIC. For a clock cycle of 2GHz, we achieve a median logical time-step of $1.51 \mu s$ for a 300 qubit Ising Hamiltonian circuit, demonstrating that $\text{R}^2$-PQF successfully resolves the vast majority of paths (with rare exceptions) within the execution window and enables the $T$-count benefits of PQF without latency penalties. Compared to a baseline stalling-based solution (the only no-runtime-recomputation solution), $\text{R}^2$-PQF speeds up circuit execution by $1.34\times$ on average and up to $1.76 \times$.

authors.name: Siddharth Dangwal, Christopher Kang, Jad Habhab, Ritvik Sharma, Frederic T. Chong, Gokul Subramanian Ravi

papers.title: Anti-distinguishability of quantum channels
papers.summary: We study single-query perfect anti-distinguishability/exclusion tasks of finite quantum channel ensembles, primarily using associated Choi operators and process POVMs. Weak perfect anti-distinguishability requires each measurement outcome to exclude an ensemble candidate with certainty, whereas the strong form additionally requires every candidate to have an exclusion outcome occurring with non-zero probability. For pairs of channels, both coincide with perfect distinguishability, whereas larger ensembles exhibit separations. We derive Choi-operator-support-based obstructions: weak exclusion requires at least two rank-deficient Choi operators, while strong exclusion requires the support of every candidate Choi operator to be strictly contained in the joint Choi support. The common Choi support must also lie in the kernel of the PPOVM normalisation. For commuting Choi operators, this condition is sufficient for weak exclusion when the normalisation also commutes with them. Conversely, a nonzero admixture of the same noise channel into every candidate precludes weak exclusion for any probe. We apply these results to measure-and-prepare, state-space contraction, Pauli, and replacer channels. In particular, the full permutation-channel ensemble of an unlabeled POVM is strongly anti-distinguishable exactly when some POVM effect is rank-deficient, while replacer-channel exclusion reduces to state exclusion. A Choi-commuting ensemble exhibits strong exclusion with an unassisted probe although no positive-definite PPOVM normalisation permits even weak exclusion. In contrast, commuting qubit phase gates, whose Choi operators need not commute, admit exact convex-hull criteria for weak and strong exclusion, both attainable without assistance.

authors.name: Ardra Ajitha Vijayan, Nidhin Sudarsanan Ragini

papers.title: Entanglement Allocation for Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
papers.summary: Jointly supporting communication and distributed sensing over a shared, limited pool of entanglement resources is an attractive prospect for future quantum networks. We develop a network-level quantum integrated sensing and communication (Q-ISAC) framework in which a quantum base station dynamically allocates elementary Bell pairs between communication users and distributed sensing. Sensing resources are adaptively partitioned among multiple GHZ probes with dynamically selected sizes and sensing-node assignments. We derive an effective quantum Fisher information model accounting for probabilistic fusion, transmission loss, and memory decoherence, and formulate a finite-horizon allocation problem subject to communication QoS, expected sensing-information, sensing-reliability, and hardware constraints. A hierarchical constrained proximal policy optimization (HC-PPO) framework combines learned discrete sensing allocation with analytical continuous communication allocation. Numerical results show that GHZ probing requires approximately $27$--30% fewer sensing qubits than separable probing under modest probe-size caps and 65-67% fewer at the highest considered target under the same sensing requirements. Adaptive multi-GHZ partitioning provides greater robustness than single-GHZ sensing, while adaptive communication--sensing sharing outperforms the evaluated fixed splits. The proposed HC-PPO framework satisfies the joint requirements in at least 99.9% of test instances across the considered sensing targets and fusion probabilities. Monte Carlo evaluation separately shows that realized terminal information reached its target in 96-98% of realizations, distinguishing expected-information satisfaction from realized sensing performance.

authors.name: Shiva Kazemi Taskooh, Mehdi Monemi, Ekram Hossain, Georges Kaddoum, Mehdi Rasti

papers.title: Quantum identity authentication protocol via perturbed probability amplitudes
papers.summary: Quantum identity authentication is an effective solution for establishing mutual trust between communicating parties in the post-quantum era. To address the risk of partial secret information leakage under special measurements, this paper designs a quantum identity authentication protocol based on perturbed probability amplitudes. The protocol first proposes a method of encoding a random sequence onto the probability amplitudes of quantum entangled states, forming perturbed probability amplitudes, thereby reducing the involvement of shared information between the sender and receiver. Furthermore, it presents a method for generating n-bit random authentication information based on the n-bit pre-shared information, enhancing the randomness of the authentication information relative to an attacker. The proposed protocol can resist impersonation attack, CNOT attack, and entanglement measurement attack, and ensures backward security. Under equivalent security conditions, the amount of shared information is 1/n that in Chen et al.'s scheme and half that in Dutta et al.'s scheme. And each bit of the secret message has no risk of leakage under special measurements. It can also be extended to a bi-directional quantum identity authentication protocol.

authors.name: Xiangqun Fu, Zheng Han, Hongwei Li, Chun Zhou, Shuo Zhang, Jianhong Shi, Tan Li, Wansu Bao

papers.title: Initialization-controlled fault sensitivity and force-balance plateaus in noisy variational quantum optimization
papers.summary: We study deep variational circuits for a periodic Heisenberg chain under local gate depolarization, at depths where noiseless training is coherently exact. Full-width initializations reach low coherent error faster than circuits with confined transverse generators, but incur a larger noise shift and need an order of magnitude more updates for noisy convergence. In many-body-localization-inspired initialization, bounding the initial transverse generator amplitudes keeps the operator support localized and suffices for low-fragility optimization, so longitudinal disorder and Floquet layer repetition are unnecessary. The fault-erasure fraction, the mean fraction of coherent energy removed per fault, sets the effective visibility through a parameter-free exponential model. Full-width circuits start with delocalized operator support, and once coherent energy builds up, each fault erases nearly all of it. Initially, their noise-induced gradient almost uniformly attenuates the coherent gradient, so coherent descent proceeds at the noiseless rate. They then stall on a high-noise force-balance plateau, where finite coherent and noise-induced gradients cancel to first order. At late times all initializations reach the same fault-erasure fraction and noisy-error band, but operator support contracts more slowly, at a rate set by the plateau residence time.

authors.name: Longhui Shen, Fangzhou Jin, Bin Guo

papers.title: Information-Geometric Representation of Upper Bounds on Fluctuation Growth in Open Quantum Systems
papers.summary: Building on our earlier results for closed quantum systems, we investigate the dynamical evolution of quantum fluctuations and their connections to Fisher information and the quantum operations describing open-system dynamics. Starting from a general expression for the time derivative of an observable's uncertainty, we derive an alternative upper bound on fluctuation growth in an open quantum system using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. The resulting bound separates contributions from the evolution of the quantum state and the explicit time dependence of the observable, reducing to a known result for closed-system dynamics. We then establish a connection between fluctuation dynamics and quantum Fisher information by decomposing the density operator and the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) into coherent and incoherent contributions, which leads to a bound relating the evolution of observable uncertainty to the coherent and incoherent components of the Fisher information, providing an information-geometric interpretation of fluctuation growth. To connect fluctuation dynamics with quantum operations governing open-system evolutions, we derive the time evolution of the eigenvalues of the density operator in terms of Kraus operators. Using the infinitesimal-time relation between Kraus and Lindblad operators, we obtain a corresponding expression for the eigenvalue dynamics in terms of Lindblad operators. This formulation directly relates changes in the density operator eigenvalues to the quantum processes acting on the system. We then study the results using some examples. Our results provide a framework connecting observable fluctuation growth, Fisher information, and the Kraus and Lindblad descriptions of quantum evolution, offering a route toward understanding how specific quantum channels influence the information and fluctuations available in an evolving quantum system.

authors.name: Newshaw Bahreyni, Paul M. Alsing

papers.title: Reasoning about Shared-Qubit Concurrency in Quantum Computing
papers.summary: In this paper, we develop a semantic model for the parallel execution of quantum circuits, providing a formal foundation for studying shared-qubit concurrency in quantum computing. As in classical shared-memory concurrency, parallel quantum circuits may interfere with one another through operations on shared qubits. However, quantum entanglement and the noncommutativity of quantum operations introduce additional challenges for reasoning about their correctness. To address these challenges, we generalise the classical Owicki-Gries method to quantum computing at the level of quantum circuits. Our approach enables compositional reasoning about parallel quantum circuits by separating the verification of individual components from the analysis of interference between them. We formulate proof rules for establishing the correctness of parallel quantum circuits and prove their soundness with respect to the proposed semantic model.

authors.name: Mingsheng Ying

papers.title: An example of universal braiding in Links--Gould topological quantum computation
papers.summary: We construct a universal quantum computational encoding via braiding in Links--Gould fusion spaces associated to $U_q^H(\mathfrak{sl}(2|1))$ where $q$ is on the unit circle and is not a root of unity. The construction uses only neglectons and is realized in the morphism spaces $\mathrm{Hom}_{U_q^H}(V(0,\alpha),V(0,-\frac{1}{2})^{\otimes 2N}\otimes V(0,\alpha)).$ Under explicit positivity and arithmetic constraints these spaces admit a $2^N$-dimensional computational subspace with a positive definite Hermitian form. We prove single-qubit density in $\mathrm{U}(2,1)$ and approximate arbitrary unitary operators on $N$-qubit computational subspaces with arbitrarily small leakage. The calculations use explicit inclusions, projections, and Hermitian pairings without requiring $F$-matrices.

authors.name: Matthew Harper, Ben-Michael Kohli

papers.title: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups
papers.summary: How can noncommuting quantum observables retain the geometry of a classical phase space? Motivated by Mumford's question on approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) states and the work of Lin and Wang, we study synthetic spectra of position--momentum and angular-momentum systems. Under the hypotheses of their AMU theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small $\hbar$, the position--momentum spectrum fills the plane, while the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The latter calculation leads to compact Lie groups: we prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound. Function-space representations of $SU(n)$, $SO(n)$, and $Sp(n)$ provide further examples.

authors.name: Junyang Liu, Hang Wang, Houjin Wang, Haoran Xu

papers.title: A Conditional Quantum Kac-Bernstein Theorem
papers.summary: We establish a conditional quantum Kac-Bernstein theorem for mixing of two independent, finite-mode bosonic inputs with quantum memories. We characterize exactly when the outputs are conditionally independent given both memories. Each input then decomposes into orthogonal memory sectors sharing a common Gaussian state on the physical system and a bosonic memory factor, up to sector-dependent physical displacements. In particular, triviality of the common bosonic factor implies separability of the inputs, as occurs whenever either memory has finite-dimensional support.

authors.name: Hesam Hosseini, Jinpei Zhao, Masahito Hayashi

papers.title: On the Hardness of Approximate Quantum Circuit Membership and Optimization
papers.summary: Quantum circuit optimization is an indispensable component of the quantum software stack, used to reduce noise, maximize performance, alleviate costs of quantum error correction, or target specific hardware. A related problem is approximate membership: for a fixed set of unitaries $S$, decide whether a given circuit $C$ is within distance $\varepsilon$ of a unitary in $S$ under some metric $m$. Membership is a special case of optimization, where $S$ is a set of unitaries implementable at no cost (e.g., with noise-minimal circuits, or without magic states). Janzing, Wocjan, and Beth (Int. J. Quantum Inf., 2005) showed that, for the operator metric, the case $S=\{I\}$ (approximate identity) is QMA-complete when $C$ is promised to be either close to the identity or far from it. We generalize this setting in three directions: (i) promise-free inputs, (ii) besides $S=\{I\}$, sets $S$ containing only Clifford unitaries, or only generalized permutation matrices (i.e., no superposition), and (iii) the trace-based, spectral, and operator metrics. We show that, in all cases, approximate membership is PP-hard for wide ranges of $\varepsilon$, provided $C$'s gate-set can implement Clifford+T, as the gate-sets of standard hardware do. If $S=\{I\}$, or if $S$ contains only generalized permutation matrices, $I\in S$, and $m$ is a trace-based distance, PP-hardness holds for all non-trivial $\varepsilon$. If $S=\{I\}$ and $m$ is a trace-based distance, PP-hardness holds even for circuits over classical-reversible gate-sets. Our results indicate that approximate membership is harder over promise-free inputs than the QMA-complete promise version, and that this hardness persists across quantum resources (any gates, non-Clifford, superposition) and distance metrics. They directly imply PP-hardness of circuit optimization when minimizing total, non-Clifford, or superposition gate depth or count.

authors.name: Adam Husted Kjelstr{\o}m, Jaco van de Pol, Andreas Pavlogiannis

papers.title: Reducing the arithmetic cost of quantum derivative pricing with language-model circuit design
papers.summary: Quantum amplitude estimation can estimate expected discounted payoffs with quadratically fewer oracle calls than Monte Carlo, but each call requires coherent computation. We use language-model-assisted circuit design to reduce reversible payoff arithmetic for a three-asset worst-of autocallable and a target accrual redemption forward (TARF). The constructions retain compact integer representations of market paths alongside contract history, reconstructing quantities temporarily for contract decisions and payoff-angle evaluation. Relative to matched internal references, the factor-sum autocallable and windowed TARF circuits reduce the product of Toffoli count and peak logical qubits $(N_{Tof} Q_{max})$ by factors of 2.39 and 4.84, respectively. At a second autocallable setting, fresh search recovers a 1.35-fold saving after the tested fixed adaptation loses its advantage. For the factor-sum circuit, we prove exact coherent execution of its integer specification for every input, incoming accumulator and measurement record, with clean workspace and phase cancellation. A separate lattice calculation gives a numerical angle-tolerance-violation probability of 6.248e-8 and evaluates pricing bias under the declared loading law, with bounded omission but no certified numerical enclosure. The results connect compact representations to lower-cost payoff arithmetic and separately assessed logical and financial correctness. Their resource scope excludes loading, payoff rotation and estimation.

authors.name: Monit Sharma, Hoong Chun Lau

papers.title: Universal Free-Electron-Sideband Control
papers.summary: Advances in free-electron quantum optics are establishing free electrons as a versatile quantum resource. Photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) interactions and free drift provide elementary operations for shaping the longitudinal electron wavefunction, yet their full control capabilities remain unexplored. Here, we prove that a finite sequence of alternating monochromatic PINEM interactions and free drifts can approximate any prescribed inner-product-preserving map from a finite-dimensional input subspace into the full ideal electron-sideband Hilbert space to arbitrary accuracy. We therefore call the protocol PINEMAD (PINEM And Drift). This framework encompasses state preparation, unitary gates, and isometric encoding. We further show numerically that parameter optimization enables high-fidelity state preparation at finite electron energy spreads, using experimentally accessible coupling strengths and tabletop-scale total drift lengths. These results establish electron energy sidebands as a programmable quantum resource.

authors.name: Tong Shen, Zhexin Zhao, Meng Xiao

papers.title: Long-lived quantum memories with rare-earth ions doped in crystals
papers.summary: Quantum memory is a core enabling device for large-scale quantum networks, serving as the fundamental building block for quantum repeaters and transportable quantum memories. Among various physical platforms, rare-earth-ion-doped crystals stand out as one of the most promising solid-state candidates for long-lived photonic quantum memories, owing to their exceptionally long spin coherence time and their compatibility with integration. In this review, we first introduce the physical mechanisms underlying long-lived spin coherence in rare-earth systems, with particular emphasis on the zero-first-order-Zeeman transition and dynamical decoupling techniques. We then review the experimental progress in this field, highlighting three distinct lifetimes--the spin coherence time, the light storage time, and the quantum storage time--and covering experiments that have achieved hour-scale spin coherence, minute- to hour-scale light storage, and minute-scale single-photon-level quantum storage. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges that hinder the realization of practical long-lived quantum memories, explore potential strategies to overcome these obstacles, and outline the prospects for their future applications in quantum networks.

authors.name: Yu-Yu Sa, Pei-Xi Liu, Zong-Quan Zhou, Chuan-Feng Li

papers.title: Decoy-state quantum key distribution with a leaky Mach-Zehnder receiver
papers.summary: We prove the security of phase-encoded decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution for a Mach-Zehnder receiver with imbalanced beam splitters and two threshold detectors that leak fine-grained information about the detection patterns. For this, we derive a lower bound on Bob's single-photon contributions and combine it with the decoy-state method and a recent phase-error framework for leaky receivers. The leakage-induced correction to the phase-error rate is independent of channel loss, providing a loss-tolerant treatment of receiver leakage even in the presence of beam-splitter imbalance. Our results provide a practical route toward loss-tolerant security proofs for imperfect QKD receivers in the presence of receiver leakage.

authors.name: Ryohei Mizusawa, \'Alvaro Navarrete, Akihiro Mizutani, Kiyoshi Tamaki

papers.title: Wigner-Function Fingerprints of Collective Excitations in Mirror-Terminated Waveguide QED
papers.summary: We investigate the emission profiles of singly excited collective states and propose a matched-mode witnessing protocol in a mirror-terminated waveguide quantum electrodynamics system. The amplitudes and relative phases of the initial collective excitation are encoded in the temporal mode of the emitted single-photon wavepacket, providing a route to state verification through the common waveguide output. We identify the emission mode associated with a chosen target state and employ an auxiliary virtual-cavity representation to evaluate the quantum state of this selected output mode.
