papers.title: Reducing Circuit Resources in Grover's Algorithm via Constraint-Aware Initialization
papers.summary: Grover's search algorithm provides a quadratic speedup over classical brute-force search in terms of query complexity and is widely used as a versatile subroutine in numerous quantum algorithms, including those for combinatorial problems with large search spaces. For such problems, it is natural to reduce the effective search space by incorporating problem constraints at the initialization step, which in Grover's algorithm can be achieved by preparing structured initial states that encode constraint information. In this work, we present a systematic framework with a simple preprocessing procedure for constraint-aware initialization in Grover's algorithm, focusing on problems with linear constraints. While such structured initial states can reduce the number of oracle queries required to obtain a solution, their preparation incurs additional circuit-level costs. We therefore offer a conservative circuit-level resource analysis, showing that the resulting constraint-aware initialization can improve resource efficiency in terms of gate counts and circuit depth. The validity of the framework is further demonstrated numerically using the exact-cover problem. Overall, our results indicate that this approach serves as a practical baseline for achieving more resource-efficient implementations of Grover's algorithm compared to the standard uniform initialization.

authors.name: Eunok Bae, Jeonghyeon Shin, Minjin Choi

papers.title: Post-selection games
papers.summary: In this paper, we introduce post-selection games, a generalization of nonlocal games where each round can be not only won or lost by the players, but also discarded by the referee. Such games naturally formalize possibilistic proofs of nonlocality, such as Hardy's paradox. We develop algorithms for computing the local and Tsirelson bounds of post-selection games. Furthermore, we show that they have an unbounded advantage in statistical power over traditional nonlocal games, making them ideally suited for analysing Bell tests with low detection efficiency.

authors.name: V\'ictor Calleja Rodr\'iguez, Ivan A. Bocanegra-Garay, Mateus Ara\'ujo

papers.title: Accessing Levinson-Smith and Li\'{e}nard equations in a nonlinear framework of quantum mechanics
papers.summary: In this paper, we present the reduction of a recently introduced generalized quantum scheme of Chodos and Cooper to Levinson-Smith and Li\'{e}nard classes of nonlinear system that enable us to furnish a wider class of acceptable solutions. In particular, for the Levinson-Smith equations, we find their relevance to position-dependent mass quantum systems, with an interesting off-shoot that solitonic-like solutions emerge from the condition of the level surface in the system. On the other hand, for the Li\'{e}nard type, which has coefficients of odd and odd symmetry in the present set up, we demonstrate that closed form solutions exist on carrying out conversion to the typical Abel form.

authors.name: Bijan Bagchi, Anindya Ghose-Choudhury

papers.title: GAP Measures and Wave Function Collapse
papers.summary: GAP measures (also known as Scrooge measures) are a natural class of probability distributions on the unit sphere of a Hilbert space that come up in quantum statistical mechanics; for each density matrix $\rho$ there is a unique measure GAP$_\rho$. We describe and prove a property of these measures that was not recognized so far: If a wave function $\Psi$ is GAP$_\rho$ distributed and a collapse occurs, then the collapsed wave function $\Psi'$ is again GAP distributed (relative to the appropriate $\rho'$). This fact applies to collapses due to a quantum measurement carried out by an observer, as well as to spontaneous collapse theories such as CSL or GRW. More precisely, it is the conditional distribution of $\Psi'$, given the measurement outcome (respectively, the noise in CSL or the collapse history in GRW), that is GAP$_{\rho'}$.

authors.name: Roderich Tumulka

papers.title: Constructing Arbitrary Coherent Rearrangements in Optical Lattices
papers.summary: Coherent control of motional degrees of freedom of ultracold atoms in optical lattices offers a promising route towards programmable quantum dynamics with massive particles. We propose and analyze a scheme for implementing coherent rearrangement of ultracold atoms, corresponding to arbitrary unitary transformations on single-particle motional states. Exploiting an analogy between dynamics in optical superlattices and discrete linear optics, we employ the Clements scheme to systematically construct any global $N$-dimensional single-particle unitary from tunneling and phase shifts in arrays of double wells. Tunneling is controlled globally, while local operations are achieved through site-resolved potential shifts. We numerically investigate the susceptibility of the scheme to intensity noise and addressing crosstalk. We identify key subroutines enabled by this unitary construction, including the Discrete Fourier Transform and the implementation of non-native Hamiltonians. Extending the scheme to two dimensions enables all-to-all atomic rearrangement with a circuit depth that scales sublinearly with the atom number, providing a high-density and highly scalable approach to atom rearrangement.

authors.name: Alexander Roth, Liyang Qiu, Timon Hilker, Titus Franz, Philipp M. Preiss

papers.title: Undecidability of consistency of generalized probabilistic theories
papers.summary: Generalized probabilistic theories (GPTs) provide a unifying framework encompassing classical theories, quantum theories, as well as hypothetical alternatives. We investigate both the problem of extending a system with a finite set of transformations, and the problem of adding to a translation-invariant set of systems a finite set of entangled states and effects, plus all their images under the translation symmetry. We show that determining whether such extensions are consistent with the axioms of GPTs is undecidable. The source of the undecidability is that these finite extensions can generate infinitely many conditions which must be checked: iterating transformations may produce infinitely many new transformations; similarly, entangled states and effects may generate infinitely many new states via the analog of teleportation. Our results show that extending GPTs to include dynamics or entanglement encounters fundamental computability obstructions, which can only be circumvented by introducing additional physical or mathematical assumptions.

authors.name: Serge Massar

papers.title: Topological phase transition of deformed ${\mathbb Z}_3$ toric code
papers.summary: We investigate topological phase transitions in a family of deformed $\mathbb Z_3$ toric-code wavefunctions prepared from a cluster state by local deformations and projective measurements. Their norms map to the $Q=3$ Potts model for single-parameter deformations and to a three-state Ashkin--Teller-like (AT$_3$) construction with two independent four-spin couplings in the general case. Projected entangled-pair-state (PEPS) and variational uniform matrix-product-state (VUMPS) calculations identify the toric-code (TC) phase and phases in which electric ($e$) anyons are confined or condensed. These phases are separated by critical structures with central charges $c=4/5$, $8/5$, and isolated $c=1$ antiferromagnetic (AFM) endpoints. A normalized finite-distance $e$-anyon pair-state norm provides a Fredenhagen--Marcu-type check of the confinement boundary, while the topological data of the quantum double $D(\mathbb Z_3)$ imply a topological entanglement entropy $\gamma=\log3$ throughout the gapped toric-code phase. Relative to the $\mathbb Z_2$ case, the absence of sign-change folding leaves the AFM endpoints unfolded, and the extreme deformation reaches square ice with an emergent $U(1)$ one-form symmetry, Hilbert-space fragmentation, and exact scar configurations.

authors.name: Yun-Tak Oh, Hyun-Yong Lee

papers.title: Quantum Dynamical Entropy and non-Markovianity: a collisional model perspective
papers.summary: Accessing the physical mechanisms behind non-Markovian phenomena in open quantum dynamics requires the study of the statistical properties of the joint system-environment dynamics. This is impossible at the level of the reduced dynamics of the open system alone as the latter is obtained by suitably eliminating the environment. The task is instead made possible by considering multi-time correlation functions involving observables of the open system, only: the open system-environment interactions turn them into global ones thus building up correlations between the two systems. Multi-time correlations form the basis of both the theory of quantum stochastic processes and of the Alicki-Lindblad-Fannes dynamical entropy (ALF entropy for short). This latter quantity provides for quantum systems a measure of the dynamical entropy production as the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy does for classical systems. In the case of a collisional model whereby the dissipative dynamics of a finite-level system is obtained by its coupling to an infinite classical spin chain, the ALF entropy can be explicitly computed. It turns out to depend on the parameters characterizing the statistical properties of the environment and can be related to the activation and super-activation of memory effects in the open quantum system.

authors.name: Giovanni Nichele, Fabio Benatti

papers.title: Quantum Dynamical Entropy and Dissipative Information Flows
papers.summary: The Alicki-Lindblad-Fannes dynamical (ALF) entropy measures the rate at which new information is gathered about a quantum system by inspecting its long-time evolution. We propose an extension of the ALF entropy to open quantum dynamics as a measure of back-flow of information from the environment. Such a proposal is stronger than the existing ones based only on the open system reduced dynamics. In the case of a qubit collisionally coupled to a classical spin chain, we obtain an exact expression for the $\textit{open-system ALF entropy}$ explicitly depending on the environment correlations. An extreme case shows how the information flow from environment to system corresponds to vanishing entropy production as for reversible finite quantum systems.

authors.name: Giovanni Nichele, Fabio Benatti

papers.title: Bell Nonlocality Test on Two-Mode Squeezed Output Generated in Double-Cavity Optomechanical
papers.summary: We explore here how to generate a two-mode squeezed output using reservoir engineering in a double-cavity optomechanical system coupled to a common mechanical resonator. Such hybrid platforms are experimentally accessible in electro-optomechanical interfaces and are relevant for high-fidelity state transfer, quantum communication, and metrological applications. By examining violations of the CHSH Bell inequality, we demonstrate that maximal squeezing does not necessarily imply nonlocality; instead, nonlocal correlations can emerge in states with lower squeezing. Furthermore, by analyzing the CHSH inequality across different cavity finesse values, we find that the parameter region supporting nonlocality can broaden even as the squeezing region shrinks. Across all regimes considered, our results emphasize the crucial influence of the mixedness of the state in determining the relationship between squeezing and nonlocality.

authors.name: Souvik Agasti

papers.title: Competition between contrast and laser noise in laser threshold magnetometry using an external cavity diode laser
papers.summary: The negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy center (NV$^-$) in diamond is a versatile platform for quantum magnetometry under ambient conditions. Recently, laser threshold magnetometry (LTM) has been proposed as a means to significantly enhance the sensitivity of NV-based magnetometers by incorporating a diamond hosting NV$^-$ centers within a laser cavity and operating near threshold. While demonstrations have validated the concept, practical implementations remain technically demanding, requiring high pump powers and precise alignment of free-space cavities. It remains unclear whether the benefits of operating near threshold will outpace increased laser noise. In this work, we integrate an NV-diamond with a high NV$^-$ content into a compact external cavity diode laser and demonstrate singlet infrared absorption optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR). We report a five-fold enhancement in the ODMR contrast by operating near the laser threshold. However, the magnetic-field sensitivity is a factor of two worse near threshold ($17~\mathrm{nT/\sqrt{Hz}}$) than when operating far above threshold ($7.6~\mathrm{nT/\sqrt{Hz}}$). Consequently, on this platform, near-threshold operation currently yields a net negative effect on sensitivity because the threshold-enhanced laser noise outweighs the threshold-enhanced contrast. These results demonstrate that managing this contrast-noise trade-off is a critical challenge that must be addressed to realize the potential benefits of laser threshold magnetometry.

authors.name: Shao Qi Lim, Alexander A. Wood, Brett C. Johnson, Qiang Sun, Jan Jeske, Hiroshi Abe, Takeshi Ohshima, David J. Ottaway, Heike Ebendorff-Heidepriem, Robert E. Scholten, Andrew D. Greentree, Brant C. Gibson

papers.title: Measurement and feedback-driven adaptive dynamics in the classical and quantum kicked top
papers.summary: In classical dynamical systems, stochastic feedback can stabilize otherwise unstable periodic orbits, giving rise to distinct controlled and uncontrolled phases as the rate of control application is varied. In this work, we apply these control protocols in classical, semiclassical, and quantum regimes to the kicked top, a paradigmatic model of quantum chaos. The quantum kicked top, modeled as the dynamics of a spin-S object, naturally interpolates between these regimes with the spin size S acting as an effective Planck constant. We show that the dynamics of the kicked top in classical, semiclassical, and fully quantum limits can all be controlled using stochastic feedback protocols. Comparing the full quantum dynamics to a truncated Wigner approximation that captures quantum noise but neglects interference beyond the Ehrenfest time, we find that low-moment observables are largely accounted for semiclassically, while higher moments retain a discrepancy that peaks at the control transition, consistent with contributions from interference and possibly nonlinearities in rare trajectories that explore the compact phase space. We also find rapid purification in the numerics studied for all rates of control considered, suggesting that control quenches the top's ability to encode a qubit of quantum information even in the uncontrolled phase.

authors.name: Mahaveer Prasad, Ahana Chakraborty, Thomas Iadecola, Manas Kulkarni, J. H. Pixley, Sriram Ganeshan, Justin H. Wilson

papers.title: Sufficient support size of measurements for quantum estimation
papers.summary: In quantum estimation for a $d$-parameter family of density operators on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, an estimator is specified by a pair $\left(M,\hat{\theta}\right)$, where $M$ is a POVM with a finite outcome set $\Omega$ and $\hat{\theta}:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is a classical estimator map. Since the number of outcomes $\left|\Omega\right|$ is a priori unbounded, the space of admissible POVMs is vast, which makes the search for optimal estimators difficult. In this paper, for the minimization of the weighted trace of the mean squared error among locally unbiased estimators, we prove that it suffices to consider POVMs with at most $\left(\dim\mathcal{H}\right)^{2}+d(d+1)/2-1$ outcomes, and that the optimization can be restricted to rank-one measurements. For Bayesian estimation with a general loss function, we show that rank-one POVMs with at most $(\dim\mathcal{H})^{2}$ outcomes are sufficient for the infimum value of the Bayes risk. Furthermore, when the model admits a real sufficient subalgebra, we show that the $\left(\dim\mathcal{H}\right)^{2}$ term in the above support-size bounds can be reduced in both the locally unbiased and Bayesian settings. These bounds substantially reduce the search space for optimal measurements and justify restricting numerical optimization to rank-one POVMs with finitely many outcomes.

authors.name: Koichi Yamagata

papers.title: Measuring the largest coefficients of a quantum state
papers.summary: We introduce a hierarchical algorithm for identifying the indices of the largest Pauli coefficients of an unknown $n$-qubit quantum state, either those exceeding a threshold or the $t$ largest ones. The algorithm traverses a prefix-based tree whose nodes represent partial sums of squared Pauli coefficients, expanding either the nodes of largest estimated weight or all nodes above a threshold, and discarding the rest. Node weights are estimated using Bell sampling on two copies of the state, or alternatively via SWAP tests on subsystems. We prove finite-sample guarantees for the exact recovery of the target set in terms of state-dependent separation margins for the relevant prefix weights, and derive bounds on the number of nodes explored by the corresponding exact traversal. While the same Bell data can be processed exhaustively, the hierarchical strategy can reduce the classical search at the cost of potentially requiring more samples to distinguish the relevant prefix weights. The efficiency of our method depends on the number of nodes of the prefix tree with non-negligible weight as well as on the statistical conditioning of these values. We validate the method numerically on Pauli-singleton states, random stabilizer states, ground states of the transverse-field Ising model, and states with hierarchical Pauli support, illustrating different structural and statistical regimes. We further benchmark the method against alternative approaches for learning Pauli coefficients. Our work addresses the targeted discovery of dominant Pauli components without performing full state tomography.

authors.name: Nicol\'as Ciancaglini, Santiago Cifuentes, Guido Bellomo, Santiago Figueira, Ariel Bendersky

papers.title: Operating a bistable qubit
papers.summary: Parasitic two-level-system (TLS) defects limit the stability and performance of solid-state quantum processors. Their interaction with a qubit can cause discrete, stochastic shifts of the qubit frequency, making the qubit bistable. We experimentally demonstrate an adaptive protocol for operating a bistable qubit with high fidelity using a classical controller powered by a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Our "1-bit feedback" protocol estimates the qubit's bistable frequency and corrects the control frame using only one single-shot measurement, reaching the information limit set by the qubit's intrinsic entropy. We validate the protocol in a superconducting qubit by suppressing TLS-induced Ramsey beating, and deploy it to stabilize gate fidelities over time with approximately 136 kHz estimation bandwidth and a 77% error reduction. Our approach provides a simple, yet fundamentally efficient strategy for mitigating dephasing errors induced by strongly coupled TLS defects, and may enable the operation of large future qubit arrays suffering from few remaining, discrete instabilities.

authors.name: Fabrizio Berritta, Jan A. Krzywda, Tom Dvir, Paul Buttles, Stanislav Eilhart, Jeroen Danon, Ferdinand Kuemmeth

papers.title: Operator-Algebraic Methods for Asymptotic-Preserving Quantum Simulation of Open Systems
papers.summary: We develop a mathematically rigorous framework for simulating \emph{multiscale physical systems} using quantum computational resources, by translating the \emph{language of asymptotic-preserving (AP) schemes} into the formalism of quantum channels and Lindbladian dynamics. For stiff open quantum systems governed by singularly perturbed generators $\cL_\eps = \eps^{-1}\cL_{\mathrm{fast}} + \cL_{\mathrm{slow}}$ with $\eps \to 0$, we prove that a protocol starting in the slow manifold (with the general state case sketched via an initial boundary layer) followed by effective evolution converges uniformly to the reduced slow state of the true stiff dynamics, with an explicit global error bound $\mathcal{O}(\eps^2(1+T) + T\Delta t^p)$ that rigorously captures $\mathcal{O}(\eps)$ physical effects (e.g., Purcell decay) without unphysical dissipation. We establish resource-complexity scaling showing that avoiding the $\Omega(1/\eps)$ stiffness penalty while capturing $\mathcal{O}(\eps)$ dynamics is efficiently achieved via analytic adiabatic elimination to precompute the effective generator, providing dimensional savings amortized against classical precomputation. The framework is illustrated through cavity QED in the bad-cavity limit and a heuristic quantum-inspired AP discretization of linear kinetic equations. This work provides a principled mathematical bridge between classical multiscale numerical analysis and quantum simulation algorithms.

authors.name: M. W. AlMasri

papers.title: Agreement and Compatibility in Wigner's Friend Paradox
papers.summary: There has been an upsurge of interest in the consequences for quantum physics of the so-called Wigner's Friend Paradox. In its original formulation, the paradox has been turned inside out, and virtually every aspect of it has been looked into. Consequently, it is becoming widely accepted that we can find the potentially puzzling consequences of Wigner's thought experiment only in light of its many-parties extensions. Nonetheless, this contribution returns to the source. Reframing the question as an inference problem, we advance a radically Bayesian interpretation that shows no contradiction between Wigner's and Wigner's Friend's descriptions---neither classically nor quantumly. Therefore, with no paradoxical conclusion. In doing so, we flesh out and expose previously untouched aspects of Wigner's thought experiment, in particular, the fact that compatibility and agreement are fundamental to our understanding of it, and that a rigorous notion of compatibility is the key to paving the way for the agents to reach an agreement. Also, by conservatively extending Wigner's original setup and incorporating what we call the 'benefit of the doubt', we see how either Wigner's or his Friend's description can be driven to match one another's---an impossibility if either agent does not keep an open mind.

authors.name: Julio C. F. Silva, B. F. Rizzuti, Cristhiano Duarte

papers.title: Isotropic random walks and Brownian diffusion on complex projective space
papers.summary: We study isotropic random walks on complex projective space in the context of stochastic state-space exploration in open quantum systems. Using results from harmonic analysis on compact rank-one symmetric spaces, first we obtain explicit transition kernels and characterise the evolution of fidelity and geometric observables. Then, we establish the correspondence between the small-step limit and Fubini-Study Brownian motion, and also show that the long-time limit reproduces Haar-random state statistics. At the level of the density matrix, the ensemble evolution formally coincides with an isotropic depolarizing channel at all times. Our main results concern first-passage statistics to high-fidelity target states. In the Brownian limit, we derive a closed-form expression for the mean first-passage time and an explicit spectral representation of the first-passage-time distribution, with decay rates determined by the eigenvalues of the killed Fubini-Study Laplace-Beltrami operator. The resulting asymptotics reveal a strong dependence on target fidelity and Hilbert-space dimension, demonstrating the rapidly increasing difficulty of reaching high-fidelity targets through unbiased isotropic exploration. The model is purely geometric and does not incorporate microscopic Hamiltonians or Lindblad dynamics. Nevertheless, the results suggest that it offers a natural starting point for stochastic models of open quantum systems that incorporate Hamiltonian and dissipative effects, with potential applications to stochastic quantum state preparation and control.

authors.name: Gyula I. T\'oth

papers.title: Equilibration of generalized subsystems: a quantum-channel approach
papers.summary: Quantum systems governed by unitary and reversible microscopic dynamics may nevertheless exhibit equilibration, in the sense that some effective description becomes time-independent. Standard equilibration results usually consider two separate situations: system-environment structures, in which the composite system evolves unitarily while the system of interest equilibrates, and restricted measurements, such as coarse-grained POVMs and observables, in which the measurement statistics equilibrate. Here, we bring these descriptions into a common state-level framework using the concept of generalized subsystems, where the accessible effective state appears as the output of a quantum channel acting on the microscopic state. We derive bounds showing that generalized subsystems equilibrate when their dimension is small compared with the effective dimension of the discarded microscopic information. We further show that this condition is met for typical initial states in large subspaces and that the resulting equilibrium description is largely insensitive to microscopic initial details. The framework recovers the usual equilibration bounds for ordinary subsystems and finite families of POVMs. As an example, we also introduce a finite-resolution energy channel that maps unresolved microscopic energy levels into effective energy levels, thereby making residual effective coherences explicit and showing how spectral multiplicities constrain those coherences while strengthening equilibration. Our results provide a unified state-level formulation of quantum equilibration under general forms of limited accessible information.

authors.name: Pedro S. Correia, Adalberto D. Varizi, Gabriel Dias Carvalho

papers.title: Near-Optimal Learning of Local Lindbladians
papers.summary: We study the problem of learning local Lindbladians from black-box access to the physical evolution, where the goal is to estimate all Hamiltonian and dissipative coefficients. For local Lindbladians with low-intersection dissipators and local dynamical strength at most $\Lambda$, we design an algorithm that learns the coefficients to target accuracy $\varepsilon$, whose experiment count and total evolution time scale as $\widetilde{O}(\Lambda^2/\varepsilon^2)$ and $\widetilde{O}(\Lambda/\varepsilon^2)$, respectively, with only logarithmic dependence on the number of qubits. The algorithm is built directly from finite-time channel probes. It runs the unknown evolution for short times, estimates the corresponding Pauli transfer matrices from classical shadows, and converts these estimates into Lindbladian coefficients by stable local Fourier inversions. The algorithm is non-adaptive, uses no ancillas, and requires only random product states as inputs followed by random Pauli measurements. The method does not require knowing the structure of the Lindbladian in advance. We prove matching lower bounds that establish the near-optimality of the algorithm in both resources. By constructing a family of single-qubit dephasing Lindbladians, we show that any algorithm, even an adaptive one with arbitrary ancillas and measurements, requires $\Omega(\Lambda^2/\varepsilon^2)$ experiments and $\Omega(\Lambda/\varepsilon^2)$ total evolution time. In particular, the lower bounds imply that the Heisenberg-limited scaling achievable for Hamiltonian learning is information-theoretically impossible once dissipative coefficients must be estimated.

authors.name: Itai Arad, Zhili Chen, Naixu Guo, Patrick Rebentrost, Zhan Yu

papers.title: A Single Physical Principle Determines Quantum Relative Entropy
papers.summary: Why does quantum relative entropy occupy such a privileged role among measures of distinguishability? We show that a single operational principle determines it. If one pair of states can be distinguished at least as successfully as another for every prior, when both are assisted by the same auxiliary pair, acting as a catalyst, a distinguishability measure should assign it no smaller value. Remarkably, for a normalized measure, this requirement singles out Umegaki relative entropy under mild classical continuity and expansibility on uniform distributions: adding impossible outcomes leaves their associated entropy unchanged. Qubit catalysts already suffice. No additivity or quantum continuity is assumed. We also prove that, without auxiliary assistance, respecting binary discrimination dominance uniquely determines the quantum extension of every regular classical divergence, including the Hirche--Tomamichel extensions of classical $f$-divergences. For additive classical divergences, these extensions respect classical catalysis; allowing noncommuting qubit catalysts is what singles out Umegaki relative entropy.

authors.name: Gilad Gour

papers.title: Dynamical zero modes and boundary dependence in dynamical quantum phase transitions
papers.summary: Boundary conditions are usually expected to cause only finite-size corrections to bulk quantities, but this expectation can fail for dynamical quantum phase transitions. In this work, we show that such boundary dependence is encoded in dynamical zero modes (DZMs) of the Loschmidt matrix, which are defined as singular vectors whose singular values vanish in the thermodynamic limit. Using the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH), extended SSH, and Kitaev models as examples, we find that the time interval where the Loschmidt rate functions (LRFs) under periodic and open boundary conditions differ coincides with the emergence of DZMs in the open-boundary Loschmidt matrix. These modes carry the boundary-dependent contribution: removing them from the open-boundary LRF recovers the periodic-boundary result. We further show that these DZMs lead to finite-precision numerical instability, since their finite-size singular values decay exponentially with system size and eventually become unresolved in fixed-precision arithmetic. A reliable small-size branch before this loss of precision can be used to estimate the LRF in the thermodynamic limit by linear extrapolation. Our results identify DZMs as both a diagnostic of boundary-dependent LRFs and the origin of the associated numerical instability.

authors.name: Siyan Lin, Xu Feng, Xiuhua Tian, Shu Chen

papers.title: Tunable non-Hermitian skin effect and topological phases in ladders with staggered nonreciprocal interleg hopping
papers.summary: We investigate the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) and topological phases in a ladder model with staggered nonreciprocal interleg hopping, consisting of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain coupled to a normal tight-binding chain. By tuning the system parameters, we show that the direction of the NHSE under open boundary conditions can be reversed and can even become energy dependent. The NHSE is further characterized by the spectral winding number under periodic boundary conditions. We also demonstrate that the interleg coupling significantly enlarges the topologically nontrivial parameter regime. Remarkably, there are two topological phases characterized by winding numbers $W=\pm1$, with the zero-energy topological edge modes residing on different sites in the two legs. Furthermore, increasing the nonreciprocity of the interleg hopping modifies the topological phase boundaries and eventually drives the system into a topologically trivial phase. Our results establish staggered nonreciprocal interleg hopping as an effective mechanism for engineering both the non-Hermitian skin effect and topological phases in ladder systems.

authors.name: Pu-Xuan Li, Qi-Bo Zeng

papers.title: Optimization of multistate STIRAP by pulse shaping
papers.summary: We propose a pulse-shaping method for improving population transfer in multistate stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) with nearest-neighbour couplings only. The method extends the quasiparallel-eigenenergy approach, previously used for two- and three-state systems, to multistate chains without introducing additional shortcut fields. The pump and Stokes fields are shaped so that the eigenenergies closest to the dark state remain nearly parallel to it during the central part of the interaction, where nonadiabatic transitions are most likely to occur. We derive analytic prescriptions for the required pulse shapes and apply them to five-, seven-, and nine-state chains formed by magnetic sublevels of degenerate manifolds with angular momenta $J_g\rightarrow J_e=J_g$ and $J_g\rightarrow J_e=J_g-1$ driven by a pair of right- and left-circularly polarized pulses. Numerical simulations show that the optimized pulses can reduce the population transfer error by several orders of magnitude compared to standard Gaussian pulses. The same shapes also improve robustness against variations of the peak Rabi frequency, the single-photon detuning, and the multiphoton detuning. The comparison between the two angular-momentum families shows that the $J_g\rightarrow J_g$ chains are generally more favourable, because their Clebsch-Gordan coefficients keep the relevant bright-state gap larger in the region where the dark state changes most rapidly. Finally, simulations with spontaneous emission show that the optimized resonant pulses remain advantageous in the lossy regime as well.

authors.name: Julian K. Dimitrov, Nikolay V. Vitanov

papers.title: Tunable Families of Multiqubit Elegant Joint Measurements
papers.summary: We give a closed-form construction of the $n$-qubit Elegant Joint Measurement (EJM) proposed in [PRL \textbf{136}, 190201 (2026)] and show that it is part of a tunable family of measurements with tetrahedrally arranged Bloch vectors. The construction is based on the interference pattern implied by a single phase polynomial built from the elementary symmetric functions. It realises a regular tetrahedral measurement for every $n$, and the corresponding measurement unitary lies at level $n{+}1$ of the Clifford hierarchy. Starting from this measurement, we ask whether the size of the local tetrahedron -- and hence the entanglement of the basis -- can be varied while preserving its symmetry. For every even $n$ the answer is yes, and remarkably the size follows the same one-parameter law that governs the known two-qubit family, interpolating down to a $1$-uniform basis. For $n=3$ the EJM is locally isolated, while for odd $n\ge5$ we do not know an analogous closed-form family. We also give an analogous construction, valid for every $n \geq3$, with square local geometry.

authors.name: Jef Pauwels, Nicolas Gisin

papers.title: Learning Arbitrary Lindbladians from Time Evolution
papers.summary: We study the problem of learning arbitrary $n$-qubit Lindbladians, the generators of Markovian open-system dynamics, from their time evolution. We give the first known efficient algorithm that learns arbitrary Lindbladians without any structural assumptions. For an $n$-qubit Lindbladian of dynamical strength at most $\Lambda$, the algorithm estimates every coefficient to error $\varepsilon$ using $\widetilde O(\Lambda^2/\varepsilon^2)$ experiments and $\widetilde O(\Lambda/\varepsilon^2)$ total evolution time, with classical running time polynomial in $n$ and $\Lambda/\varepsilon$. Both experimental costs match known lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. The algorithm identifies candidate labels through product Pauli experiments and estimates their coefficients using random stabilizer preparations and Clifford measurements. It requires no ancillas or control during the unknown evolution. For constant $k$, our algorithm learns generic $k$-local Lindbladians of local dynamical strength at most $\Lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}$ using $\widetilde O(n^2\Lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}^2/\varepsilon^2)$ experiments and $\widetilde O(n\Lambda_{\mathrm{loc}}/\varepsilon^2)$ total evolution time, improving the upper bounds of prior works in terms of the dependence on $n$. We further improve the lower bounds of Arad, Chen, Guo, Rebentrost, and Yu (SODA 2027) using a family of $3$-local Lindbladians. They already hold when the support is known, and only one Hamiltonian coefficient is requested, even for adaptive protocols with arbitrary ancillas and quantum memory. These lower bounds establish that our algorithm is optimal up to polylogarithmic factors in both experiment count and total evolution time for every fixed $k \geq 3$.

authors.name: Zhili Chen, Zhan Yu

papers.title: Time-Deterministic and Instruction-Dynamic Execution: A field-programmable gate array quantum-control processor
papers.summary: Long-running quantum computations, including error-corrected workloads, demand instruction availability, measurement-dependent control, and calibration updates. We present Time-Deterministic and Instruction-Dynamic Execution, an FPGA quantum-control processor supporting runtime revision at both instruction and parameter levels. Dynamic Instruction Parameter Update supplies one-shot, next-match patches before parameter capture, while Dynamic Instruction Stream Overwrite provides guarded replacement, logical deletion, and out-of-line insertion in eligible future regions of a resident program. A moving fetch-visibility guard coordinates instruction updates with execution, and event commitment isolates complete descriptors for independent hardware-timed dispatch. Revision applicability depends on update timing and execution progress; deterministic service applies to committed events under the stated scheduling conditions. The Xilinx ZCU102 implementation uses a 250-MHz control core and a 425-MHz timing/update domain. FPGA-resident measurements at the registered digital interfaces confirmed programmed-cycle dispatch for all tested descriptors committed at least one timing-domain cycle before their timestamps, with downstream ready and the stated FIFO ordering conditions. Separate tests confirmed post-commit timestamp and payload invariance. The minimum all-success mapped DIPU margin was four control-domain cycles, and a replacement of L instruction words completed in L+5 update-domain cycles under continuous payload delivery. Within the tested guard-distance range, rejected DISO requests reported an error and preserved the resident path, whereas all admitted revisions tested here executed complete revised sequences. These results provide a hardware execution basis for incorporating runtime-generated sequences and parameter corrections into precisely timed quantum computations with feedback.

authors.name: Xiaoqin Luo, Jiayun Song, Xiaolu Su

papers.title: Superposition of dynamics, indefinite causal order, and quantum histories
papers.summary: The process-matrix formalism describes quantum processes without assuming a fixed global causal order, but the physical meaning of indefinite causal order remains open. We address this question within histories theory, where temporal ordering and dynamical evolution are distinct structures. We show that the decoherence functional admits coherent superpositions of dynamics. In measurement settings, under suitable factorization conditions, these generate process matrices. In the bipartite setting considered here, process-matrix indefinite causal order is thereby identified as an operationally restricted realization of the more general phenomenon of superposition of dynamics. Histories theory also admits a distinct kinematical notion of indefinite order, in which the ordering of physical events is itself a history observable. The resulting distinction between event order and intervention order clarifies the relation between indefinite causal order, quantum dynamics, and spacetime structure.

authors.name: Charis Anastopoulos, Ntina Savvidou

papers.title: From Round-Trip State Echo to Error Recovery: Snapshot-Resolved Quantum-Hardware Diagnostics
papers.summary: We examine which conclusions from quantum-hardware benchmarks persist when the same programs are run again. On eight fixed routes of IQM Emerald, round-trip state echo (RTSE), a diagnostic of state return after a round trip, gave mean scores near $0.84$ that differed by only $0.00125$ between two executions. Individual route estimates nevertheless changed by up to $0.06$ in both directions. The mean difference between RTSE and measurement-free teleportation along the same routes shrank from $0.046$ to $0.014$ and was no longer statistically resolved on repetition; none of the four prespecified communication targets met its replication rule. Recovery with an existing four-qubit single-deletion code also changed on repetition: after discarding one encoded qubit in the circuit model, the IQM mean fell from $0.738$ to $0.624$ and failed the replication test against the two-thirds operational reference. In a separate IonQ experiment, recovery means of $0.91$ and $0.92$ passed tests against that reference and against a deliberately incorrect decoder in both executions. These results concern the tested workloads and executions. They show why a nearly unchanged aggregate benchmark score needs to be interpreted alongside individual routes, direct task comparisons, and repeated executions.

authors.name: Isaac Barouch Essayag (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

papers.title: A double-resonator coupler for high-fidelity two-qubit gates between superconducting qubits
papers.summary: Tunable couplers have enabled two-qubit gate fidelities in superconducting quantum processors to approach $99.9\%$, yet simultaneously suppressing residual interactions and maintaining flexible qubit-frequency allocation remain central challenges for scaling. Here, we propose a double-resonator coupler (DRC) consisting of two resonators interconnected by a single Josephson junction and a capacitor. The hybridized resonator modes provide two mediated exchange paths whose interference controls the qubit-qubit interaction. The DRC enables complete cancellation of residual $ZZ$ interaction for qubit-qubit detunings well outside the straddling regime, even without direct inter-qubit capacitance, thereby relaxing constraints on frequency allocation and qubit placement. Away from the idle point, the same circuit provides a strong $ZZ$ interaction of approximately $70\,\mathrm{MHz}$, enabling a $20\,\mathrm{ns}$ controlled-Z gate with simulated coherent infidelity below $10^{-5}$. These results establish the DRC as a flexible single-junction coupler architecture for high-fidelity superconducting quantum processors.

authors.name: Seunghyeon Jin, Seungha Woo, Shinyoung Hwang, June-Young M. Lee, Jeongmin Shim, Sunje Kim, Dae Seok Han, Jaeho Shin, Eunjong Kim

papers.title: Impossibility of One-Way One-Round Quantum 4-Coloring via Matrix-Space Stability
papers.summary: We show that one-way one-round quantum-LOCAL algorithms cannot $4$-color directed cycles with high probability. This is the first lower bound in the high-probability quantum LOCAL setting that goes beyond the non-signaling and bounded-dependence models, exploiting the structure of distributed quantum algorithms. Our proof establishes a bidirectional connection between distributed quantum computing and extremal combinatorics. We obtain our lower bound by proving a Mantel-type stability theorem for weighted matrix spaces.

authors.name: Tom Gur, Longcheng Li

papers.title: Quantum Advantage for Distributed Symmetry Breaking
papers.summary: We present a distributed quantum algorithm that $3$-colors cycles in $O(1)$ rounds, with high probability. It follows that all locally checkable labeling problems (LCLs) that have round complexity $O(\log^* n)$ in the classical LOCAL model can be solved in $O(1)$ rounds in the quantum-LOCAL model, with high probability; this includes problems such as maximal independent set and maximal matching in bounded-degree graphs. This presents the first natural examples of graph problems with an asymptotic distributed quantum advantage for the LOCAL model; all prior examples that separate LOCAL and quantum-LOCAL are artificial problems constructed merely for the sake of demonstrating quantum advantage.

authors.name: Maxime Flin, Longcheng Li, Jukka Suomela

papers.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
papers.summary: We reveal an unexpected connection between two interacting particle systems: Kac's walk and the Kipnis-Marchioro-Presutti (KMP) process. We first establish a mixing-time analogue of Aldous's conjecture for the KMP process on general graphs: the mixing time of the $t$-particle process on any connected $d$-vertex graph is at most $O(\log d)$ times the corresponding single-particle mixing time, uniformly in $t$. As an application, we improve the mixing-time bound for coordinate hit-and-run on the $n$-dimensional standard simplex from $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ [KV26] to $O(n\log n)$, while removing the dependence on the initial distribution. We then show that the twirling channel induced by the parallel Kac's walk on the symmetric subspace can be exactly encoded by a Markov chain on partitions, which naturally lifts to a parallel KMP chain on the complete graph. We prove that $O(\log d+\log(1/\varepsilon))$ repetitions of the parallel Kac's walk suffice to approximate Haar twirling on the symmetric subspace of $(\mathbb{C}^d)^{\otimes t}$ to error $\varepsilon$, uniformly in all $t$. Our main technical contribution is a new structural property of KMP-type dynamics: conditional product structure, which holds for both the standard KMP processes on general graphs and the parallel KMP processes on complete graphs. Conditioned on suitable auxiliary randomness, the evolution of the labeled KMP process factorizes into independent single-particle updates. Combining this structure with an exact coupling, we remove the dependence on the number of particles from the mixing bounds for both unlabeled KMP models. This bypasses the $\log(\pi_{\min}^{-1})$ dependency from spectral-gap arguments, which is often prohibitively large for many-particle systems. Using this framework, we prove mixing bounds that are sharp up to logarithmic factors for both unlabeled KMP models.

authors.name: Qian Chen, Jingcheng Liu, Minglong Qin, Leonard J. Schulman, Fang Song, Penghui Yao, Mingnan Zhao

papers.title: Fast Quantum Algorithms for Learning Linear Threshold Functions
papers.summary: Linear threshold functions (LTFs) are $\{-1,1\}$-valued functions $f_{w,\theta}(x)=\text{sgn}(\langle w,x\rangle-\theta)$, where $w\in\mathbb R^n$ has unit norm, $\theta\in\mathbb R$, and $x\in\mathbb R^n$ or $\{-1,1\}^n$. If $\theta=0$, the LTF is homogeneous, denoted $f_w=f_{w,0}$. LTFs are fundamental linear classifiers. We give three results: one for general LTFs and two for homogeneous LTFs. (1) With real-domain membership queries evaluating $f_{w,\theta}(x)$ at any chosen $x\in\mathbb R^n$, we learn an LTF with classification error at most $\varepsilon$ under the standard Gaussian distribution using $O(\log(n/\varepsilon))$ queries and $\widetilde{O}(n)$ other gates. Classically, $\Omega(n\log(1/\varepsilon))$ queries are required, giving an exponential quantum query speedup. (2) A homogeneous LTF $f_w$ over $\{-1,1\}^n$ whose $k$ nonzero weights are equal and positive is Majority on the support of $w$. We identify this hidden support exactly using $O(\log k)$ queries, exponentially improving Belovs' $O(k^{1/4})$ upper bound. Our algorithm uses $O(n\log n\log k)$ gates and has $O(\log n\log k)$ non-oracle depth. Classical algorithms require $\Omega(k\log(n/k))$ queries. (3) Suppose a unitary $U$ prepares discretized Gaussian quantum examples, corresponding to $\int_x\sqrt{\gamma_n(x)}|x\rangle|f_w(x)\rangle\,dx$. This is weaker than membership queries. Using the efficient quantum Hermite transform circuit, we learn homogeneous LTFs with classification error at most $\varepsilon$ under the Gaussian distribution using $O(n^{1/4}/\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ applications of $U$ and $U^\dagger$ and $\widetilde{O}\!(\frac{n^{5/4}}{\sqrt{\varepsilon}}+\frac{n}{\varepsilon^2})$ other gates. Classically, $\Omega(n/\varepsilon)$ examples are needed, giving a quartic quantum speedup in $n$. We show that the quantum query complexities in all three cases are optimal by proving matching lower bounds.

authors.name: Aleksandrs Krivcenko, Tuyen Nguyen, Ronald de Wolf

papers.title: Robust and leakage-resilient device-independent oblivious transfer in MiniQCrypt
papers.summary: Assuming post-quantum one-way functions, we construct device-independent oblivious transfer and bit commitment that tolerate independent honest faults at a constant rate and adaptive, bidirectional quantum leakage between the laboratories at a constant rate. Honest parties use trusted classical computation to operate untrusted quantum devices, which may share arbitrary entanglement and perform joint measurements without assumptions of independence or identical distribution. Security is simulation-based against quantum polynomial-time adversaries and composes sequentially with efficient simulators. For security parameter $\lambda$ and a prescribed total leakage budget $\ell$, one complete one-bit oblivious transfer uses $\Theta(\ell+\log^2\lambda)$ device coordinates in at most three single-use device windows, including preprocessing, and polynomial classical computation and communication. The leakage budget is shared across these windows. The commitment has efficient simulators against both parties and yields device-independent coin tossing with abort; each uses one window. Completeness of oblivious transfer gives device-independent secure computation with abort for every efficiently computable classical functionality on a fixed number of parties, against static corruption of any proper subset, provided each reached call to oblivious transfer satisfies the device and budget conditions. The construction combines short selectors with code-based choice masking, a global audit, and error correction across field symbols. The commitment extractor changes a classical code coset while leaving the device execution and its leakage unchanged. Sender security uses a global Fourier analysis and a selector-aware Magic Square repetition bound derived from the two-round threshold theorem of Kundu and Tan (2023).

authors.name: Rishabh Batra, Zhili Chen, Rahul Jain, YaoNan Zhang

papers.title: Exponential quantum space advantage in random data streams
papers.summary: We show two unconditional quantum space advantages in the random-order streaming model. First, we show the Yamakawa-Zhandry Code Intersection problem admits exponential quantum advantage in the streaming model when its inputs are streamed in random order. This means quantum computers exhibit exponential space advantage even when simply receiving $(x,f(x))$ pairs for a uniformly random function $f$ in a uniformly random order. Notably, our classical space lower bound does not follow from a communication lower bound. Instead, we utilize density-restoring partitions from communication complexity directly with potential-function analysis in the style used to prove memory-sample tradeoffs for learning. The resulting argument is distinct from both lines of work. Second, we use our framework to show quantum space advantage for the Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI) problem in certain regimes via a streaming version of the Decoded Quantum Interferometry algorithm. In particular, we show that for degree $d$ and $n$ evaluation points, attaining $1/2 + \Omega(\sqrt{d/n})$ fraction of satisfied OPI constraints via streaming requires $\Omega(n)$ classical bits of memory but only $O(d\log n)$ qubits. This yields provable quantum advantage in a "low-rate" regime when the number of evaluation points is much larger than the degree, with a space advantage that can be as large as exponential in certain parameter settings.

authors.name: Adam Bouland, Matthew Ding, Siddhartha Jain

papers.title: Approximation of a continuous-variable Gaussian state by discrete-variable quantum states
papers.summary: For every centered one-mode continuous-variable Gaussian state, we prove that the signed Wigner periodization defines a discrete-variable density operator in every odd dimension $d\ge3$. Positivity is equivalent to the one-mode uncertainty condition, and we determine the complete inertia outside and on its boundary. A covariance-independent isometric embedding gives exponential convergence in trace norm, with an explicit error bound uniform in Planck's constant. For covariance twice the identity, dimension $31$ gives a certified trace-norm error below $1/8000$. The trace-norm estimate controls all measurement probabilities. We retain the original canonical-coherent-frame formula in terms of the determinant and trace of the covariance matrix, with continuous normalization fixed to agree with the discrete frame convention. The coherence comparisons identify which diagnostics accompany the controlled state approximation. Position- and momentum-basis coherences have exponentially convergent values after division by the square root of the dimension. Numerical comparisons of purity and frame coherence illustrate the discrete-continuous transition.

authors.name: Nicolae Cotfas, Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang

papers.title: Fast mixing of the SYK model at high temperatures
papers.summary: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model is a strongly interacting fermionic system. Its dynamics are difficult to analyze with Lieb-Robinson bounds and cluster expansions due to its all-to-all disordered interactions. We prove that, with high probability over the disorder, the SYK model admits a quantum Gibbs sampler with a system-size-independent spectral gap at sufficiently high constant temperatures. This yields polynomial-time preparation of SYK Gibbs states on a quantum computer. While prior non-rigorous computations that suggested SYK thermalization were limited to studying local correlators, we emphasize that our result holds up to arbitrary inverse polynomial trace distance. Our proof introduces the pseudo-Lindbladian approach to fermions then applies two key new ideas: a Bochner inequality for quantum dynamics, and an especially simple SYK analysis based on a comparison to classical dynamics.

authors.name: Yiyi Cai, Yongtao Zhan, Alexander Zlokapa

papers.title: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
papers.summary: We study two problems: Local Leakage Resilience (LLR) for Shamir secret sharing, and worst-case Optimal Polynomial Intersection (OPI), over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$. For a polynomial $Q(X)$ of degree less than $k$, LLR for Shamir secret sharing asks what a few leaked bits from each of the $n$ shares $Q(\alpha_1), \ldots, Q(\alpha_n)$ reveal about $Q(0)$. Given (worst-case) input lists $S_1, \ldots, S_n \subset \mathbb{F}_p$, OPI seeks a polynomial $Q(X)$ so that $Q(\alpha_i) \in S_i$ for as many $i$ as possible. Leveraging recent connections between these two problems due to (Sun, Wootters 2026), we improve the state-of-the-art for both problems. For LLR, we show that there is some constant $\delta > 0$ so that Shamir secret-sharing is one-bit LLR (only a negligible amount about $Q(0)$ is learned) whenever $R := k/n \geq 1/2 - \delta$. This is the first result to break the so-called ``one-half barrier'' for LLR, and improves over the previous best known result, requiring $R \geq 0.668$ (Kasser, 2025). For OPI, we give a quantum algorithm that finds a polynomial $Q(X)$ that agrees with at least a $\mathsf{SCL}_\rho(R)-\varepsilon$ fraction of the lists, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, where $\mathsf{SCL}_\rho$ is the \emph{semicircle law} of (Jordan et al., 2025). This improves previous algorithmic (and existential) results of (Jo, 2026) and (Horinaga, Yamakawa, 2026). We also give further improved existential results for all OPI instances; and when the evaluation points $\alpha_i$ are chosen at random, for every rate $R > 0$ we show that, with high probability, for worst-case $S_i$ there exists \emph{perfect} solution. Finally, we adapt the hardness result of (Yamakawa, Zhandry, 2024) to apply to OPI (rather than a folded version); this gives an unconditional separation between the quantum and classical hardness of OPI relative to a membership oracle.

authors.name: Yihang Sun, Mary Wootters

papers.title: Quantum Folding in Chebyshev-Based Quantum Subspace Diagonalization
papers.summary: Quantum subspace diagonalization (QSD) with a Krylov space spanned by Chebyshev polynomials of the Hamiltonian is a natural ground-state method for fault-tolerant quantum computers, but every guarantee it offers---convergence rate, noise floor, and the cost of turning its classical output back into a physical state---is controlled by the overlap of the reference state with the true ground state, which decays exponentially with system size for any product state and non-trivial Hamiltonian. We propose quantum folding: for a system governed by a local Hamiltonian, seed the QSD with the product of the ground states of its subsystems, which differs from the target only through the interface terms. We prove a nonasymptotic error bound for the Chebyshev QSD that is linear in the measurement noise, by transplanting Kirby's effective-Hamiltonian analysis to the Chebyshev--Krylov basis, and identify the block-encoding rescaling of the Hamiltonian as a parameter of the guarantee. Exact simulations of antiferromagnetic Heisenberg chains show that the folded reference state reduces the Krylov dimension for a given accuracy severalfold and lowers the error under noise by two to five orders of magnitude relative to the N\'eel state. We show how the Ritz vector is prepared as a physical state and that the ground-state generation probability obeys a tight ceiling set by the overlap, so that recursive folding prepares ground states at polynomial cost. Taken together, these results allow for a scalable QSD framework that avoids the exponentially small ground-state overlaps associated with conventional product-state initialization. Finally we compute the fold fidelity itself: a slow power law for the gapless spin-1/2 chain, a size-independent constant for the gapped spin-$1$ chain, and an exact closed form converging to 1/4 for the AKLT chain.

authors.name: Seung Park, Dongni Chen, Stefano Chesi, Kyunghyun Baek, Mahn-Soo Choi

papers.title: Certifying information flow in multi-agent behaviours
papers.summary: We study which input-output behaviours of several agents can be produced by a declared communication schedule, that is, a fixed sequence of senders, recipients, message alphabets, and output times, together with shared randomness. Since a schedule admits only finitely many deterministic protocols, membership is a linear program, and an infeasible target is excluded by a separating inequality. Under explicit operational assumptions, we prove that the affine hull of the achievable behaviours is described exactly by the equalities stating that each joint output statistic depends only on the inputs that can reach the agents involved, so that a violated equality identifies both the statistic and the missing input. One binary message per event already attains this affine hull, so message capacity restricts which behaviours are achievable without being visible to any equality. We apply the result to one-bit broadcast and relay hierarchies for two and three agents, and to low-order projections of the local polytope.

authors.name: M. Haider Akbar, Onur Pusuluk, \"Ozg\"ur E. M\"ustecapl{\i}o\u{g}lu

papers.title: All-optical room-temperature spin coherence of aqueous asymmetrically chelated Cu(II) for chemoselective discrimination
papers.summary: Harnessing molecular electron spins as responsive quantum sensors in ambient water requires bridging ultrafast all-optical readout with selective chemical recognition. Here, we overcome the intrinsic magneto-optical sluggishness of 3d transition-metal complexes--which previously restricted all-optical detection to high concentrations of ~1 M--through a coordination-driven symmetry-breaking strategy. Coordinating aqueous Cu(II) with EDTA imposes a non-centrosymmetric ligand field with enhanced metal-ligand covalency, relaxing Laporte restrictions and amplifying d-d transition dipole moments. This design enables room-temperature all-optical initialization and readout of electron spin coherence down to 100 {\mu}M with an apparent dephasing time T_2^*~0.54 ns. Crucially, the chelated complex chemoselectively discriminates amino acid biomolecules: histidine binding induces a pronounced, concentration-dependent prolongation of T_2^* to ~0.8 ns, whereas glycine produces no measurable effect. These results transform spin dephasing into a chemically informative observable, opening avenues toward microwave-free, analyte-responsive quantum sensing in complex aqueous environments.

authors.name: Jinlei Li, Qiaoyun Wu, Qiaoqiao Shao, Zhubin Hu, Haitao Sun, Zhenrong Sun, Donghai Feng

papers.title: Classical and Quantum Logics with Multiple Non-Equivalent and Non-Isomorphic Models
papers.summary: Both quantum and classical logics have several mutually non-equivalent and non-isomorphic models as has repeatedly been proved in the literature. Yet, several authors have recently come with criticisms of this result. In this paper, we show that the criticisms are either unfounded or wrong.

authors.name: Mladen Pavicic

papers.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
papers.summary: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.

authors.name: Sayantan Dey, Abel Carreras, Siddhartha Patra

papers.title: Exceptional Points and Optimized Encoding in Qubit Stabilizer Codes
papers.summary: Continuous blind stabilizer measurements turn stabilizer codes into a Liouvillian spectral problem in which Hamiltonian terms compete with dissipative error channels. We show that this competition generically enables Liouvillian exceptional points, whose occurrence at weak error rates is constrained by the code distance. Exceptional points are detrimental in this regime of error correction as they maximize the decay rate of encoded coherences. We then optimize the encoding of the logical qubit using the eigenmodes of the Lindblad operator. This phase-optimized encoding cancels the linear short-time decay of logical qubit coherences. We apply this encoding to the [[5,1,3]] code and demonstrate that it outperforms naive encoding methods near the exceptional point, improves the fidelity of a logical $\pi$ rotation and remains effective in the presence of additional weak error channels.

authors.name: Yves Rottstaedt, Andrei I. Pavlov, Alexander Shnirman, Yuval Gefen, Bernd Rosenow

papers.title: Thermalization with Gaussian Quantum Cellular Automata
papers.summary: We study the long-time dynamics of many-body bosonic lattice systems under translation-invariant Gaussian quantum cellular automata. We formulate two sets of conditions on GQCAs which separately guarantee thermalization of any state on the local Weyl algebra to the infinite temperature state, whenever the state is locally normal and has uniformly bounded particle density. Our main intermediate result is a quantum many-body generalization of the classic Riemann-Lebesgue lemma which is a bound on expectation values of local Weyl operators involving their support and the state's particle density.

authors.name: Roman Geiko, Jake Gerenraich

papers.title: Measurement-induced spatially nonuniform fluctuations of the local particle number and their crossover in a quasiperiodic free-fermion chain
papers.summary: We study continuously monitored dynamics of a quasiperiodic free-fermion chain defined on a Fibonacci lattice. We focus on fluctuations of the local particle number, which do not exhibit quasiperiodic spatial modulation in the unitary limit. Remarkably, we demonstrate that they exhibit a nonuniform spatial pattern originating from the quasiperiodic long-range order under continuous measurement. Furthermore, employing both physicaland perpendicular-space analyses, we elucidate that a measurement-induced crossover emerges in fluctuations due to the interplay between the incommensurate modulation and the continuous measurement. While weak measurement yields a distribution reflecting the long-range spatial structure of the quasiperiodic system, an increase in measurement strength alters the distribution into one dominated by the local environment of each site. A structure-factor analysis further reveals that the weak-measurement regime is characterized by two dominant Bragg peaks corresponding to the golden-mean modulation, whereas the strong-measurement regime exhibits the characteristic Bragg-peak hierarchy of the Fibonacci pattern. We also elucidate that the measurement-induced crossover emerges in other physical quantities such as connected correlation functions. These findings offer insights into nonequilibrium quasiperiodic phenomena emerging in continuously monitored dynamics.

authors.name: Toranosuke Matsubara, Kazuki Yamamoto

papers.title: Entanglement Asymmetry in Random Quantum Automata
papers.summary: We investigate the subsystem entanglement asymmetry in random quantum automaton ensembles, which are generated by permuting the basis states in the Hilbert space and applying global phase shifts. We compute the ensemble average of the $U(1)$ subsystem asymmetry in different connectivity geometries, showing that the late-time limit of the ensemble associated to a 2-local circuit geometry coincides with the all-to-all ensemble average. By focusing on different subsystem sizes, we demonstrate that, similarly to Haar-random circuits, the system locally symmetrizes. However, in sharp contrast to the Haar-random setting, the scale at which symmetrization happens depends on the initial state, a phenomenon we associate with the interplay of conservation of the participation entropy and the uniform exploration of charge sectors. Additionally, we connect the growth of the subsystem asymmetry to the subsystem coherence and show that their growth is characterized by the same symmetrization scale.

authors.name: Olalla A. Castro-Alvaredo, D\'avid Sz\'asz-Schagrin, Michele Mazzoni

papers.title: Eddy currents and current reversal in curved magnetic thin-film Josephson junctions
papers.summary: Real-space geometric curvature in magnetic thin films introduces a controllable mechanism for tailoring the pathways of superconducting steady-state Josephson currents via the proximity effect. We present a generalized Green's function method for calculating diffusive transport in arbitrarily curved surfaces, and show how the competing mechanisms of curvature and distance regulate conversion between different superconducting pairings in a proximity-coupled ferromagnet. We show how this dictates the distribution of current density, with the possibility of curvature-controlled current density manipulation, induced eddy currents and current reversal.

authors.name: Einar Skoglund, Maxim A. Tj{\o}tta, Sol H. Jacobsen

papers.title: Random Garbage Creates Exponential Quantum Query Separations
papers.summary: We prove an exponential separation between standard (XOR) quantum queries and forward-erasing queries for a Boolean property of injective functions, answering a question of Aaronson~\cite{Aaronson2021Open}. We also obtain an exponential separation for a Boolean promise problem on permutations, where forward in-place queries are unitary but inverse queries are not supplied. Our construction follows Aaronson's suggestion of appending fixed random garbage to a Simon function. Let $X=\{0,1\}^n$ and $N=2^n$. We use the injection $f_{h,r}(x)=(h(x),x,r_x)$, where $h:X\to X$ is promised to be either a permutation or a Simon function, and $r:X\to X$ is an arbitrary tag table that is reused on every query. The resulting problem is solvable with at most $n+2$ standard queries, but requires $\Theta(\sqrt N)$ forward-erasing queries, matching classical collision sampling. Embedding these instances into permutations, with the copy of $x$ replaced by a single bit that keeps the embedding injective, gives a promise problem on permutations of $L=4N^2$ elements that requires $O(\log L)$ standard queries versus $\Theta(L^{1/4})$ forward in-place queries. The lower bounds use the recording method. We replace each query by a nearby contraction that records cells of a purified tag table. After $T$ queries, tracing out the purified tag table yields a sum of positive-semidefinite contributions, each depending on $h$ at no more than $T$ addresses. A query-by-query hybrid bounds the trace-norm difference between the actual and auxiliary final operators by $O(T/\sqrt N)$. Random permutations and random Simon functions have the same restriction distribution on such a set unless it contains a hidden Simon pair, an event of probability $O(T^2/N)$. Consequently, the actual final states in the two cases remain close unless $T=\Omega(\sqrt N)$, giving the required lower bounds.

authors.name: Khaled Elbassioni, Rishikesh Gajjala, Saurabh Ray

papers.title: Distinguishability Transitions from Global Quantum Snapshots
papers.summary: Quantum states generated by generic time evolution are locally featureless: local measurements return random outcomes that are identical for all states. However, global snapshots in the computational basis are surprisingly effective at distinguishing between quantum states. We explore the ability of Bayesian classifiers to discriminate between many random quantum states using a small number of measurement outcomes. We identify a phase transition in the ability of the classifier to distinguish between $k$ candidate states with $m$ shots controlled by the variable $x = m / \ln k$, and derive the threshold value $x_c$. We extend our results to low-depth circuits near the onset of anti-concentration, as well as to noisy circuits and phase-random states.

authors.name: Catherine McCarthy, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Romain Vasseur

papers.title: Noncommutative sharp Hausdorff-Young inequality
papers.summary: We prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality on quantum euclidean spaces. Our result implies the sharp Hausdorff--Young constants for the Weyl transform. The key ingredients are a sharp Hessian comparison inequality and a novel flow related to the mixed- norm of noncommutative Gabor transform; the Hessian comparison leads to the monotonicity of the flow. We also apply the same flow technique to prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities on Heisenberg groups and the affine group.

authors.name: Hongsen Qiu, Xiao Xiong

papers.title: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid
papers.summary: The chiral central charge $c$ measures the gravitational anomaly of a two-dimensional topological phase and fixes the heat current along its edge. It has been accessed through thermal transport, where phonons complicate the signal, or through wave-function probes that need a pure ground state. Here we show that a calibrated combination of directional edge absorption weights determines $c$. A modulation of the edge couplings that travels along the edge is absorbed according to the Virasoro algebra, and a static change of the same couplings measures the unknown probe normalization. Two harmonics then cancel the dependence on the edge state, so the estimator returns $c$ in any state of the ideal edge theory. A ratio of line weights with and without a vison gives the conformal spin of the Ising anyon. For the Kitaev honeycomb model, exact calculations recover $c=1/2$ and $h_\sigma=1/16$ to $10^{-5}$ and give $c$ within about $1\%$ on 96 spins. Compiled into gate circuits on the physical spins of a square-lattice quantum simulator, the protocol returns $c$ within $5\%$ on 48 qubits. For stochastic gate errors it requires two-qubit error rates of $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$.

authors.name: Kumar Ghosh

papers.title: Correlated quantum criticality and topological magnetoelectric response in Bi2Se3
papers.summary: A defining feature of quantum materials is that multiple orders govern low-energy physics and are not independent. We study Bi$_2$Se$_3$ by combining DFT with a renormalized correlated honeycomb model in which frustrated magnetic order and helical topological surface states are coupled via one control parameter. The surface states map to a honeycomb Hubbard model with frustrated $J_1$--$J_2$ exchange. Exact diagonalization up to 20 sites shows the N\'{e}el structure factor and valence-bond-solid order parameter cross at $J_2/J_1 \approx 0.22$, agreeing with QMC/DMRG, and a dynamical spin structure factor broadens near the crossover, as expected for a spinon continuum. Band inversion of the renormalized tight-binding model occurs on the same critical locus, producing jumps in the Chern number and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant mirrored by the skyrmion charge $Q$. This gives a microscopic link: $Q$ selects the axion angle and thus the topological magnetoelectric coupling. We distinguish axion coupling, independent of skyrmion helicity, from the helicity-dependent magnetoelectric multipole coupling, whose toroidal component scales as $\sin\gamma$ and vanishes for N\'{e}el-type textures. We derive the $Q$-topological magnetoelectric energy and estimate $\sim 10^{-20}\,\mathrm{J}$ per skyrmion per cycle for few-tesla fields. The cycle is thermodynamically bounded: constant-$\theta$ cycles extract no net work, and efficiency is limited by axionic entropy change.

authors.name: Aniekan Magnus Ukpong

papers.title: Restricted triangular ice beyond the solvable manifolds: chiral ice and the critical region of dominant chiral vertices
papers.summary: We study two restrictions of Baxter's symmetric twenty-vertex model on the triangular lattice, in which the three classes of vertices allowed by the ice rule carry the weights $a$, $b$ and $c$: chiral ice, in which only the twelve chiral vertices are allowed, and the model that excludes only the two alternating vertices. We show that neither model belongs to any of the known exactly solvable families of the twenty-vertex model, and we characterise chiral ice as the ice model in which every vertex has exactly one through line, a property that imposes a parity constraint along every closed lattice line. We compute the residual entropies of both models with transfer matrices on cylinders of up to twelve vertices in circumference, extrapolated with the finite-size correction predicted by conformal invariance, which we adapt to the triangular geometry and verify at two exactly solved points. The number of upward arrows crossing the cylinder is conserved, and the cost of changing it shows that both models are critical, with the long-distance behaviour of a free massless field. Chiral ice is the extreme point of a region of the phase diagram in which ordering had been suggested; along two paths through that region we find the same critical behaviour at every point, with no feature at the proposed boundary of the region. Along Baxter's exactly solved curve we obtain the corresponding exponents in closed form.

authors.name: Josep Batle

papers.title: Agentic inverse design of spatially programmed materials
papers.summary: Spatially programmed functional materials, from functionally graded alloys and metamaterials to quantum superlattices, use their spatial structure to tailor physical properties. However, translating a desired spatial structure into a practical fabrication recipe remains challenging due to the complex relationship between processing conditions and resulting material structures. Here we show that a large language model (LLM) agent can inverse-design such fabrication recipes by using a physics-based simulator of ion-matter interactions as a tool. Given an arbitrary depth profile of implanted ions or vacancies, the agent selects the ion species, energies, incident angles, and target material layers; writes, runs, and interprets simulations; and iteratively refines the recipe until the simulated profile matches the target, with minimal human input. Our work demonstrates physics-guided agentic inverse design as a practical approach to making the spatial structure of materials a programmable variable, opening new opportunities to explore emergent physical phenomena and functional phases of matter.

authors.name: Denisse C\'ordova Carrizales, Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk, L. Dagny Davis, Jeremy Ramsey, Ryotaro Okabe, Mouyang Cheng, Mingda Li

papers.title: Thermal Phase Transition of Three Dimensional Orthogonal Metals
papers.summary: Orthogonal metals provide a paradigmatic example of strongly entangled metallic states whose transport and thermodynamic properties resemble those of conventional Fermi liquids, while their single-electron excitations remain fundamentally distinct. Despite considerable interest in their unusual ground-state properties, orthogonal metals in three spatial dimensions and their finite-temperature behavior remain relatively unexplored. Here, we investigate a three-dimensional orthogonal metal and characterize the thermodynamic and spectroscopic signatures associated with its finite-temperature phase transition. Starting from a simple model of fermions coupled to spin degrees of freedom, we perturbatively demonstrate that the thermal transition known to occur in the purely bosonic limit persists in the presence of coupling to a gapless Fermi surface. We then examine physical observables that change prominently between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes. In particular, we calculate the evolution of the physical-electron spectral function and identify characteristic signatures in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find a pronounced contrast in low-energy spectral weight between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes without requiring conventional symmetry-breaking order.
